title: Mervin learning: price and pick the store (#1508)
text:
Mervin learning: price and pick the store (Pipelines to Iceberg vs R2 NDJSON + R2 SQL)
Price both options at our event volume before building anything (fan-out per merge and per repo). Pick the cheapest that R2 SQL can query, decide retention, and write the answer into mervin.md. Smallest live resources, destroy test ones after.

Design: apps/codesplitter/docs/mervin.md ("Learning your merge patterns"), PR #1505. Contest rule: keep main working and the demo matching its video until 2026-10-21; build on a branch or behind a flag.
Mervin learning: price and pick the store (#1508)
Closes #1508.

Prices Pipelines to Iceberg against R2 NDJSON plus R2 SQL at 1k and 100k opt-in repos and writes the answer into mervin.md.

- Pick: Pipelines to Iceberg. R2 SQL only queries Iceberg tables, so NDJSON is not queryable, and it is not cheaper either.
- Cost stays inside the monthly allowances until about 140k repos; storage dominates after that.
- Retention: 400 days; delete-my-data by deleting a per-repo salt.
- Not verified live: R2 SQL has no listed price, and no resources were created. The first live pipeline should check the bill.

Docs only; `bun run docs --check` passes.

text:
Agent Office: cheaper frames in the Druids skin (grass, shadow casters, fireflies, fire light)
Follow-up to the frame-rate governor (`apps/agent-office/power/`). That PR draws fewer frames. These make each frame cheaper. They're the Druids skin's own costs, found while auditing the office for battery drain:

- **Grass:** ~26,000 instanced blades (`druids/jungle.ts`) on a double-sided `MeshStandardMaterial` (PBR) with vertex sway, receiving shadows. Try `MeshLambertMaterial`, or fewer blades / no sway when power mode is saver or on battery.

- **Council fire:** a `PointLight` adds a light to every standard material's fragment shader, all over the room, for a flicker near the hearth. Look at a smaller `distance` or an emissive/sprite glow instead.

title: codeSplitter: move the Artifacts namespace off codesplitters (copy repos, rewrite remotes)
text:
codeSplitter: move the Artifacts namespace off codesplitters (copy every repo, rewrite the stored remotes)
Split from #809, which moved the D1, queues, bucket, index and app name to `codesplitter`. The Artifacts namespace stays `codesplitters` (`ARTIFACTS` in `apps/codesplitter/rustybuns.config.ts`) because it can't move the same way:

- It isn't a resource Alchemy replaces. Changing `namespace` only points the binding at a new, empty namespace, so every repo would vanish at once, and no deploy guard can see it.
- Each repo's git remote names the namespace, and D1 stores those remotes (`repos.remote`, `repos.crew_remote`), so moving it means copying every repo and rewriting those rows in the same step.

What moving it would take: list the namespace's repos, `git clone --mirror` each and push it to the same name under `codesplitter`, rewrite the stored remotes, then switch the binding in one deploy. Old repos stay until the new ones are checked.

Nothing is broken: the name only shows in the Cloudflare dashboard and in the remotes.

Follow-up to #1428 (PR #1639 took codex and pi off hosted runs, because each can read its own API key from the run's environment: codex via `env`, pi via an unconfined `read`).

title: Dependency doctor: health call fetches one package at a time (#1675)
text:
codeSplitter dependency doctor: the health call blows the 128 MB cap on big packages (express, vite)
Part of #859, found while running the repo health page (#860) for PR #1668's demo script.

`GET /api/repos/:o/:r/deps/health` fetches each package's full registry document (`npmrcRegistry` in `src/deps.ts` reads `versions`, `time`, `dist-tags`) and does several at once. With `express`, `vite` and `react` in package.json the request grew memory by 143 to 245 MB, and the 128 MB edge cap answered `503 Error 1102`. Cloudflare's isolate has the same cap, so the hosted page would likely fail on any repo with large packages. It passes with small ones (minimist, semver, chalk).

To repeat: `cd apps/codesplitter && bun scripts/dep-doctor-demo.ts`, then put `express` and `vite` in the seeded package.json.

Ideas, not decided: fetch one package at a time and drop each document once the few fields are kept; or keep only the versions near the pinned one and the latest. The abbreviated registry format has no release dates, which the doctor needs, so it can't be swapped in as is. Done when a repo with express, vite and react answers the health call under 128 MB.

text:
Containers: Dockerfiles as a first-class workflow (CLI, CI, prod-like runs, codeSplitter UX)
Makes Dockerfiles first-class in RustyBuns and codeSplitter. Today codeSplitter's three images (`sandbox/`, `deploy-sandbox/`, `deploy-sandbox/ci.Dockerfile`) only get built during a live deploy. There's no local workflow for them, local runs don't match Cloudflare's runtime, and the hosted containers' lack of Docker and Rust only shows up later as failed runs.

This issue holds the full spec. #814, #815, #816 and #817 were folded in here and closed.

## Order

Each part builds on the one before it:

- [ ] **Part 1:** CLI `rustybuns containers` (list, build, run, smoke) plus a Docker preflight on deploy (was #815)
- [ ] **Part 2:** CI builds and smoke-tests the images a PR touches, with a size and boot summary. It calls `containers smoke` (was #814)
- [ ] **Part 3:** `--prod-like` local runs with the real egress gate and CA (was #816)
- [ ] **Part 4:** codeSplitter flags runs that need Docker or Rust up front, with a one-click "Run on desktop" handoff (was #817)

Part 2 can ship first on plain `docker build` if we want the safety net sooner. It switches to `containers smoke` once Part 1 lands.

title: protect: Durable Objects and Artifacts show as REMOVED on destroy
text:
protect can't keep Durable Objects or Artifacts through a destroy
`protect: true` (packages/cli/src/protect.ts) only covers d1, kv, r2, queue, vectorize and hyperdrive. A destroy of a Worker still removes its Durable Object classes and their data, and destroying an Artifacts namespace removes the repos in it. For codeSplitter that is the repo, file, search and settings data.

Found while protecting live data in #1717 and #1718.

To decide:
- Can Alchemy retain a Durable Object class or an Artifacts namespace the way it retains the others?
- If not, should destroy refuse on any stage that serves users, or print them in the KEPT/REMOVED report as REMOVED so the risk is visible?
- Add a test that fails when a live config has an unprotectable data binding and no explicit acknowledgement.

Until then: never run destroy on a stage that serves users. The REAL-stage refusal only covers stages named prod, production, live, main or master.
protect: Durable Objects and Artifacts show as REMOVED on destroy
Closes #1726

Alchemy has no retain for a Durable Object class or an Artifacts namespace, so `protect` can't keep them. Instead of hiding that:
- destroy's KEPT/REMOVED report lists them as REMOVED (`protect can't keep this kind`); classes bound from another Worker (`scriptName`) are left out.
- they count as deleted data, so a destroy of a prod/production/live/main/master stage is refused until `--real`.

Test in `packages/cli/test/protect.test.ts`.

title: codeSplitter game: paste-a-GitHub-URL wrecking link (#1761)
text:
codeSplitter game: a paste-a-GitHub-URL link that digs the repo and opens the wrecking room
Giving a streamer a link to wreck their own repo takes three manual steps today: sign in, dig the GitHub repo into a fork (\`POST /api/github/dig\`), make it public, then send \`/play#r/<handle>/<repo>?mode=wreck\`.

Wanted: one link, e.g. \`/play#gh/<owner>/<repo>?mode=wreck\`, that digs the public GitHub repo on first visit and opens the wrecking room.

Things to settle:
- Who owns the dig for a signed-out visitor (a throwaway fork, like the "fork for a day" one in the README)?
- Rate limit: digs are 5 an hour per caller, so strangers following a link must not run up digs. Cache one read-only copy per GitHub repo and reuse it.
- Wreck mode touches nothing in the real repo, so a read-only copy is enough.

Found while sending a link to a streamer; the manual route was verified signed out: \`/play\`, \`/api/game/r/:o/:r\` and \`/walls\` all answer 200 for a public dig.

- A new copy is charged to a new site-wide `wreck` rule (20 an hour); cache hits cost nothing, so strangers following a link cannot run up the per-caller dig limit.
- The dig body is now `digRepo`, shared with `POST /api/github/dig`.

title: codeSplitter: rate-limit gitpath, no site token for anonymous callers
text:
codeSplitter: anonymous gitpath requests fan out to GitHub with no rate rule
Found in security audit round 4 (notes/SECURITY_AUDIT.md).

`GET /api/repos/:o/:r/gitpath` (worker.ts around line 587, gitpath-upstream.ts) makes up to about 41 GitHub API calls per request, uncached, and is open to anonymous callers on public dug forks. `ruleFor` has no GET rule for it, and when `GITHUB_TOKEN` is set the calls spend the site's GitHub quota even for anonymous callers.

Fix: return the `github` rule from `ruleFor` for `p[4]==='gitpath'`, pass no token when `user` is null, and consider caching the upstream answer per repo for a few minutes.
codeSplitter: rate-limit gitpath, no site token for anonymous callers
Closes #1822

- `ruleFor` counts `GET /api/repos/:o/:r/gitpath` against the `github` rule (anonymous callers by IP).
- gitpath only passes a GitHub token when someone is signed in, so anonymous requests no longer spend the site's `GITHUB_TOKEN`.
- Test: `ruleFor` case in `codesplitter.test.ts`.

Not done: caching the upstream answer per repo (the issue says "consider"); worth a follow-up if the rule proves too loose.

title: codeSplitter: cap crew share links on private repos at an hour
text:
codeSplitter: a removed crew member keeps clone access for up to 7 days
Found in security audit round 4 (notes/SECURITY_AUDIT.md).

`/share` in apps/codesplitter/src/worker.ts hands any reader an Artifacts read token that lasts up to `SHARE_MAX_S` (7 days). Removing a collaborator only deletes their `api_tokens` rows, so a share token they minted still clones the private repo (private lines blank) until it expires.

Design call: a TTL policy for private repos. Simplest: cap `ttl` at one hour on private repos unless the caller is the owner. Alternative: record share tokens per user and revoke them on removal.

title: codeSplitter: quota and rate rule for page assets (#1821)
text:
codeSplitter: page assets have no quota or rate rule
Found in security audit round 4 (notes/SECURITY_AUDIT.md).

`PUT /api/me/page/assets/:name` (apps/codesplitter/src/page.ts, around line 131) reads the whole body before the 5 MB check, sets no limit on how many files one account stores, and has no rule in `ruleFor` (limits.ts). Any signed-up account can fill R2 five megabytes at a time.

Fix: reject on `content-length` over the cap before reading, count files under the `page/<user>/` prefix and cap them, and add a share-style rule for `p[1]==='me' && p[2]==='page'`. Page file `content` (setText) wants a size cap too. Needs a decision on the per-user numbers.

- An account keeps at most 50 asset files (rewriting one is free); page file text is capped at 1 MB.
- New `page` rate rule (60/hour per user) on `PUT /api/me/page*`.
- Test extended in `test/page.test.ts`; audit note updated.

The numbers (50 files, 1 MB, 60/h) are my picks for the open decision in the issue; admins can tune the rate on the limits page.

title: codeSplitter: npm tokens only go to public https registries
text:

Found in security audit round 4 (notes/SECURITY_AUDIT.md).

`registryUrl` in apps/codesplitter/src/deps.ts (around line 262) matches tokens by host with the scheme stripped, and the tokens include the owner's `~/.npmrc` with `${VAR}` filled from the process environment. title: git-recon: sidearm, plasma grenade, better soldier physics
text:
git-recon: sidearm, plasma grenade, better soldier physics

Follows #1934 (the board). The kit now gets the same treatment: modelled in Blender at three polygon budgets, and fitted to each piece.

**Why fit instead of placing a model:** a piece's riding surface is its own height function, and in the parks it's draped over real ground. A rigid model can't match it. So `blender/kit.py` models each module in a unit box: x and z run across and along the piece, and y runs from the pad (0) to the riding surface (1). `src/render/kit.ts` stretches the module over the piece, so the top is exactly the surface the board rides, slope included. title: Park Hide & Seek: recorded ranger voice lines
text:
park-hide-seek: recorded ranger voice lines (commercial-safe)
Ranger calls are spoken by the browser's speech synthesis (slow, low, after a radio squelch since #1952). Real recorded lines would make the rangers much scarier.

A search found no CC0 pack with lines like "Anybody out there?":
- Kenney's voiceover pack is CC0, but it's announcer lines (https://opengameart.org/content/voiceover-pack-40-lines).
- lentikula's sci-fi pack is CC0, but robotic (https://lentikula.itch.io/sci-fi-ship-voices).
- The Ghost Voice Pack's licence is questioned in its own comments.

Options, cleanest first:
1. Record the eight `CALLS` lines in `src/ui/audio.ts` ourselves (we own them), run them through a radio filter, and ship them as small .ogg files in `public/`.
2. Generate them with an Apache-2.0 TTS model offline (for example Kokoro), and check the voice's own licence.
3. Freesound CC0 clips, checked per file.

Then play a clip per call, with the speech synthesis as the fallback.

Park Hide & Seek: recorded ranger voice lines
Closes #1953

The eight ranger calls are now small Opus-in-Ogg clips (`public/voices/ranger-<n>.ogg`, about 63 KB total) played after the radio squelch. They load and decode once, then play at the distance volume. If a clip won't load, the old speech synthesis speaks the line.

Licensing (issue option 2): we wrote the lines and generated them offline with Kokoro-82M (Apache-2.0, `am_michael`, speed 0.85), then pitched down 10% and ran a radio filter with ffmpeg. Nothing third-party is bundled. The recipe is in the app README.

text:
qCRM: dedupe is O(n^2) in the wasm engine, 1.6 s on 2,000 contacts
Profiling #2026: on 1,999 synthetic contacts, JSON.stringify is 1.6 ms, JSON.parse of 637 KB is 6 ms, the wasm dedupe call is 1,627 ms. Needs a wasm rebuild.

- Behaviour change: a pair whose only signal is a near-identical but not equal name is no longer found. Such a pair scores under 0.5 unless the names are very long, so this is rare.

qCRM scripts: the local twin runs scripts in-process, not in a sandbox
On the edge a stored script runs in its own dynamic Worker with globalOutbound null. The desktop and the tests use shell-bun's workerLoader, which imports the module in-process: no network block, and a synchronous infinite loop blocks the host. Code without `globalOutbound: null` still imports in-process as before.

Caveat, noted in the file header: Bun has no permission model, so this is a seatbelt, not a wall against deliberate escape. Isolated Workers can't import `cloudflare:workers`.

title: codeSplitter: an agent's lines survive a release (journey test)
text:
codeSplitter: an agent's lines survive a release (journey test)
A release restarts every Durable Object. This journey has an agent add and rewrite lines in a file, evicts the file's object the way a deploy does, and checks the same lines and revs come back and the file still takes edits.

Why: edits are written to object storage before they are acknowledged (`edit()` in `src/file-do.ts`), so a release shouldn't lose collab data. Now a test says so.

Not covered, and left as is: container runs (agents, checks, deploys) are replaced by a release, and the game lobby and city sockets don't reconnect on their own (the file editor does).

title: qCRM: webhook retry test waits up to 10s for the first attempt
text:
qCRM: flaky webhooks test "a failing endpoint is retried with backoff, then the delivery is dead"
Failed in CI at `apps/qcrm/test/webhooks.test.ts:63` (`expect(d.attempts).toBe(1)`, received 0) on #2052 and #2074. It passed on re-run, and 3 of 3 times locally, with no change to webhook code in either PR.

Likely a timing race: the delivery attempt has not been recorded when the assertion runs. Fix by awaiting the delivery to settle instead of relying on timing.

Found while landing the qCRM PR queue.
qCRM: webhook retry test waits up to 10s for the first attempt
#2089 made the test poll for the recorded attempt, but the poll stops after 2s, which a loaded CI runner can exceed (the original failure: attempts 0 at the assertion). Poll for up to 10s; it still exits the moment the row catches up.

Closes #2103

title: GeoBoxQ: exact packing check for tiny orders
text:
GeoBoxQ: better packing quality
The packer is a heuristic: "fits" is always true, "doesn't fit" can miss a tight arrangement. No tilting. Add an exact check for tiny orders.

Split out of #2088. apps/geoboxq lives in PR #2085 until it merges, so a PR for this is stacked on it (branch `office/nibble-ad1c`) and says "Part of #N".
GeoBoxQ: exact packing check for tiny orders
Closes #2101.

When the extreme-point heuristic says a box of 7 or fewer pieces doesn't fit, an exhaustive search over normalised positions, turns and orders settles it (capped at 200k placements). "No" is now exact for tiny orders, still axis-aligned. Tilting is not added; the README says so. Wasm rebuilt (135 KB, under budget). Test uses a real case the heuristic missed.

title: GeoBoxQ: Shopify wrapper, with optional per-store API keys
text:
GeoBoxQ: Shopify wrapper
A small app that calls `POST /api/solve` with a cart and maps the answer to the store's own box set. **Needs a decision first:** auth (API key per store) before the endpoint goes public; today it is open with CORS `*`.

Split out of #2088. apps/geoboxq lives in PR #2085 until it merges, so a PR for this is stacked on it (branch `office/nibble-ad1c`) and says "Part of #N".
GeoBoxQ: Shopify wrapper, with optional per-store API keys
Closes #2097

- `apps/geoboxq-shopify`: `POST /pack` takes a Shopify cart, looks up variant sizes (`STORE_DIMS`), calls GeoBoxQ `/api/solve` and answers with the id from the store's own box set (`STORE_BOXES`). Worker or `bun run serve`.
- Auth decision: GeoBoxQ gets `GEOBOXQ_API_KEYS` (comma-separated). Set, `/api/solve` needs `Authorization: Bearer <key>`; unset, it stays open as today, so nothing breaks until the owner sets keys on the deploy.
- Test: one journey of the wrapper against the real GeoBoxQ handler with keys on.

title: GeoBoxQ: failover across hosts
text:
GeoBoxQ: failover across hosts
The same `handle` runs on Cloudflare and on a plain Bun server (`bun run serve`). Missing: a Railway deploy, an AWS fallback only if those two are down, and something in front that picks a healthy host (health is `GET /api/health`). Config and code only; no deploys without the owner.

Split out of #2088. apps/geoboxq lives in PR #2085 until it merges, so a PR for this is stacked on it (branch `office/nibble-ad1c`) and says "Part of #N".
GeoBoxQ: failover across hosts
Closes #2096

- `src/front.ts`: tiny proxy that sends each request to the first host whose `/api/health` answers (Cloudflare, Railway, AWS last), 10 s cached probes, 2 s timeout.
- `Dockerfile` + `railway.json`: one image for Railway and the AWS fallback, running `src/serve.ts`.
- Journey test: failover down the list and back to primary on recovery.

Config and code only; nothing deployed. Needs the owner to create the Railway/AWS services and run the front off Cloudflare.

title: Dev host serves nothing .assetsignore names
text:
Dev host serves files .assetsignore names; the binary and Cloudflare leave them out
The desktop binary now stages its assets without what \`.assetsignore\` names (\`packages/cli/src/stage-assets.ts\`), as Cloudflare leaves those out of an upload. The dev host (\`rustybuns run desktop\`, \`build desktop --dev\`) still serves them, because \`packages/shell-bun/src/serve.ts\` only hides the \`.assetsignore\` file itself.

So a file can load in dev and 404 in the binary and on the edge.

Fix: \`serve()\` reads \`.assetsignore\` beside \`_headers\` and \`_redirects\` and treats a match as missing. \`assetIgnore()\` would have to move somewhere shell-bun can import (it imports nothing, so a copy into shell-bun with cli importing it from there works).
Dev host serves nothing .assetsignore names
serve() reads .assetsignore beside _headers and _redirects and treats a match as missing, so a file no longer loads in dev and 404s in the binary and on the edge. assetIgnore moved into shell-bun; stage-assets imports it from there.

Closes #2151

title: init: infer dashboard-set ai and r2 bindings instead of listing them as secrets
text:
init: Pages-dashboard bindings (env.AI, extra R2) become optional secrets
A Pages project often sets some bindings in the dashboard, not in \`wrangler.toml\`. \`init\` then finds \`env.AI\` or \`env.ANALYTICS_R2\` in \`functions/\` through \`codeSecrets\` and lists them as optional secrets, which they aren't: on the desktop \`env.AI\` stays unbound, and the app reports "AI binding not configured" instead of getting the local \`ai\` binding.

Seen on a 100-route Pages app: \`AI\`, \`ANALYTICS_R2\` and a few \`MOCK_*\` flags were all listed as secrets.

Ideas: infer the binding from how the code uses it (\`env.X.run(\` is \`ai\`, \`env.X.put(\`/\`.get(\` with \`R2\` in the name is \`r2\`), or at least print these as "used in code, not declared: add them to wrangler or rustybuns.config.ts" instead of making them secrets.
init: infer dashboard-set ai and r2 bindings instead of listing them as secrets
Closes #2152

A Pages project's dashboard bindings (`env.AI`, `env.ANALYTICS_R2`) used to show up as optional secrets. `codeSecrets` now infers `env.X.run(` as an `ai` binding and `env.X.put(`/`.get(` with R2 or BUCKET in the name as `r2` (bucket name is the lowercased, dashed binding name; init prints it so it can be edited). Names wrangler already declares are left alone.

Test: `packages/cli/test/secrets.test.ts`. Typecheck clean.

title: trial-github: fetch Git LFS files
text:
trial-github: fetch Git LFS files (trials get pointer files instead of images)
`scripts/trial-github.ts` clones repos without their Git LFS files, so a trial gets only the small pointer files. On zyra-project/terraviz the skybox (`public/assets/skybox/*.jpg`) and `Earth_Specular_2K.jpg` came through as pointers, and the globe drew on a black sky with no stars. The app was fine. The trial just didn't have the images.

git-lfs isn't installed on the trial machine. Downloading the 7 files from `media.githubusercontent.com/media/<owner>/<repo>/<sha>/<path>` fixed it by hand (found in #2153's trial).

Fix: when `.gitattributes` names `filter=lfs`, either run `git lfs pull` if git-lfs is there, or fetch each pointer file from media.githubusercontent.com. Do it before the build, outside the sandbox's offline profile. Cap the total size, and note in the trial report which files were fetched.

title: Agent Office: only a person sends a worker home; TerraViz report
text:
trial-github: fetch Git LFS files (trials get pointer files instead of images)
`scripts/trial-github.ts` clones repos without their Git LFS files, so a trial gets only the small pointer files. On zyra-project/terraviz the skybox (`public/assets/skybox/*.jpg`) and `Earth_Specular_2K.jpg` came through as pointers, and the globe drew on a black sky with no stars. The app was fine. The trial just didn't have the images.

git-lfs isn't installed on the trial machine. Downloading the 7 files from `media.githubusercontent.com/media/<owner>/<repo>/<sha>/<path>` fixed it by hand (found in #2153's trial).

Fix: when `.gitattributes` names `filter=lfs`, either run `git lfs pull` if git-lfs is there, or fetch each pointer file from media.githubusercontent.com. Do it before the build, outside the sandbox's offline profile. Cap the total size, and note in the trial report which files were fetched.

text:
TerraViz node-in-a-box: prove publishing, search and federation in the local binary
The pitch for TerraViz's author: his Tauri app is a viewer of a hosted node (`src/config/endpoints.ts` defaults to terraviz.zyra-project.org), while Rusty Buns can run the whole node (API, both D1 databases, KV, R2, Vectorize) as one binary, with no fork or Cloudflare account. - [ ] **Publish locally:** sign in to the publisher portal in the local binary, add one dataset, see it in the catalog. Its auth expects Cloudflare Access, so find out what a local node does instead (`DEV_BYPASS_ACCESS`?).
- [ ] **Search locally:** semantic search over the Vectorize twin. Embeddings come from Workers AI, so say whether it works offline, works with `MOCK_AI`, or needs a model on the desktop.
- [ ] **Federation:** two local nodes (two binaries, two data dirs) discover each other's catalog, or say what blocks it (node identity keys, public URLs).

title: TerraViz: weekly pinned re-check (#2198)
text:
TerraViz: re-check it on a schedule so a Rusty Buns change can't break it quietly
TerraViz ran on Rusty Buns from a fresh clone (#2153, #2196), but nothing re-checks it, so a change to `init`, `pages-functions` or the asset staging could break it quietly. Decide whether it becomes a recurring trial: a `scripts/trial-github.ts` run on a schedule, or a pinned entry in a sample list. A pinned commit is cheaper and stable. Following upstream's latest catches their changes too, but fails for reasons that aren't ours. It must clone outside the repo (`~/rustybuns-demos` or a temp dir): inside it, TerraViz's `tsc` picks up our `@types`.

Part of #2191

TerraViz: weekly pinned re-check (#2198)
Closes #2198

Decision: a pinned commit, run weekly (and on dispatch). Following upstream's latest would fail for reasons that aren't ours.

- `scripts/trial-github.ts`: `owner/repo@sha` pins a ref; `--check` exits 1 if install or any mode fails (toolchain gaps and skipped modes pass).
- `.github/workflows/terraviz-weekly.yml`: Monday run on macOS (so the sandbox applies), clone under the runner temp dir (outside the repo), opens or comments on a `ci-terraviz` issue on failure.
- Verified locally against the pinned SHA: worker mode serves 200, exit 0.

title: Desktop shell: opt-in public paths for peer nodes
text:
Desktop shell's launch-token gate blocks a peer node from reading /.well-known and the catalog
Found proving #2197. `serve.ts` gates every path on the per-run token cookie, so a second node (or anything not the browser the shell opened) gets 403 on a public discovery document such as `/.well-known/terraviz.json`. Federation between two local nodes needs some paths to be readable without the token, plus a public URL (tunnel). Add an opt-in list of public paths (like `guest.paths`, but with no passphrase) that a config can name. Part of #2191.

title: Desktop Workers AI answers bge embeddings locally
text:
Desktop has no embedding model: Workers AI throws, so local search is word-matching only
Found proving #2197. `LocalAi` (`packages/shell-bun/src/bindings/ai.ts`) throws on every `run()`, so an app that embeds text (TerraViz's semantic search) only works if it has its own mock (`MOCK_AI=true`, which hashes words). Search then matches words, not meaning. Options: a small local embedding model behind `env.AI.run` for the embedding models, or say plainly in the docs that it is off the desktop. Price the model's size against the binary first. Part of #2191.
Desktop Workers AI answers bge embeddings locally
Closes #2202

`LocalAi.run` now answers `@cf/baai/bge-{small,base,large}-en-v1.5` and `bge-m3` with a built-in embedder (hashed words and character trigrams, right dimensions, `{ shape, data }` like the real binding). Semantic-search code runs unchanged on the desktop. It matches shared words and stems, not meaning; a real ONNX model would add tens of MB to the binary, so I priced that out. Every other `env.AI` call still throws. README line updated.

Test: `packages/shell-bun/test/edge-twins.test.ts`. Typecheck failures in apps/artstewengine and apps/qcrm are not from this change.

codeSplitter merge: carry a branch's edit into a block main moved (and re-indented)
Found while rebuilding #1210 on main (merge commit 77af4b1, `bun scripts/merge-replay.ts 77af4b1`): git conflicted on `apps/codesplitter/src/mirror.ts` (`followBranches`), and codeSplitter's line-id merge left it as 2 cards.

Both sides reordered the same `if` chain in `followBranches`. Before, it was `if (tip === had) { delete merged branch } else if (open) { catchUp }`.
- main (#1209) put `if (open) { ...; continue }` first and moved the delete-merged block out under it, unindented.
- #1210 put `if (open) { catchUp }` first and the delete block under `else if (tip === had)`, then added one line to it: `update-ref -d squashRef(ref)`.

**Card 2 (L1037) is the gap.** Main moved the delete block and changed its indent, and the branch added one line inside it. The fix is main's moved block plus the branch's line. The line-id merge reads main's move as a delete plus an insert, so it can't carry the branch's line into the moved copy. To fix it: match moved runs by text, ignoring whitespace (as the stacked-branch rebase already matches merged lines by text), and replay the branch's in-run edits onto the moved copy.

title: codeSplitter: a repo can keep its git in an EU Artifacts namespace (#2301)
text:
codeSplitter: an Artifacts namespace per org, with an EU option: which way?
Item 5 of #1580, moved out of it because it needs a decision first: one Artifacts namespace per org, with an EU option.

What the docs say (2026-10-25):
- A namespace is made by the REST API only: `POST /accounts/:id/artifacts/namespaces {namespace, jurisdiction?: "eu" | "us"}`. The jurisdiction can't change after.
- A Worker's Artifacts binding names one namespace (`ARTIFACTS: { type: "artifacts", namespace: "codesplitters" }`). `create()` on it takes no namespace.

So a namespace per org means one of:
1. An account API token in the Worker (a new secret in 1Password) and the REST API for create, fork and tokens on non-default namespaces. Most flexible; the Worker then holds a broad credential.
2. A fixed few bindings (`ARTIFACTS` plus `ARTIFACTS_EU`), and a `repos.namespace` column saying which a repo uses. No new secret; "EU" is a choice per repo, not per org.

There are no orgs in codeSplitter yet either, so option 2 is the plumbing-only step. Owner: which way?

codeSplitter: a repo can keep its git in an EU Artifacts namespace (#2301)
Closes #2301.

Took option 2 (the plumbing-only step): no new secret, no account token in the Worker.

- `ARTIFACTS_EU` binding (optional) and `repos.namespace` (NULL = default, `eu`).
- `POST /api/repos {region: "eu"}`; 400 for other values, 501 when no EU binding.
- `handleFor`, the crew remote and fresh starts read the repo's namespace via `artifactsFor`.
- Left on the default namespace: GitHub imports and level digs (no org/region choice there yet).
- Not bound in `rustybuns.config.ts`: the namespace must first be created by REST with `jurisdiction: "eu"` (owner step, noted in the config).

title: codeSplitter: revoke an agent's Artifacts token when its run ends or its budget cap stops it
text:

Item 4 of #1580, moved out of it: when the agent budget cap (`tripped` in `src/budget.ts`, the cut in `src/agent-run.ts`) stops an agent, call `revokeToken` on every Artifacts token it holds.

Today agents hold no Artifacts tokens: hosted runs edit lines through the API, and only codeSplitter's own Worker mints tokens (`access` in `src/archive.ts`, 5-minute write tokens). So there is nothing to revoke yet. This lands together with the follow-up #1580 named, scoped tokens per agent session: mint one per run, keep its id or plaintext on the `agent_runs` row, and revoke it when the run is cut short, stopped or ends.

What the docs say (2026-10-25): a repo handle has `revokeToken(tokenOrId): Promise<boolean>` and `listTokens()`; `createToken` answers `plaintext` and `expiresAt`, no id documented. Notes in `apps/codesplitter/docs/artifacts-powers.md`.

title: codeSplitter auth: a provider sign-in can't adopt an unverified password account
text:
codeSplitter auth: can account linking adopt an unverified password account?
Split from #2222 (security round 5, "Needs validation").

Email sign-up needs no verification, and account linking is on. If Better Auth links a provider-verified sign-in onto an existing unverified password account and keeps its password, whoever created that account first keeps a working login on it, which can earn handles (the admin handle included).

Read the installed Better Auth version's account-linking code: does it link onto an unverified email-and-password account, and does it drop or keep the password? If it keeps it, either require `emailVerified` for linking (`trustedProviders` / `requireEmailVerification`-style options), or clear the password on link. Test with a password sign-up followed by a provider sign-in on the same email.

codeSplitter auth: a provider sign-in can't adopt an unverified password account
Closes #2297.

**Finding:** Better Auth 1.7.7 (`oauth2/link-account.mjs`) already refuses to link a provider sign-in onto a local user whose `emailVerified` is false (`requireLocalEmailVerified` defaults to true), so the squatter's password never gains a provider account. It is a library default, though, and this app has no email verification when mail is off.

**Change:** pin `requireLocalEmailVerified: true` in `identity.ts`, with a comment on why, and add `test/account-linking.test.ts`: password sign-up, then a verified GitHub sign-in (faked) on the same email. It is refused, and the passwo

title: codeSplitter: Ester flags slow checks; board line for where testing holds merging up
text:
codeSplitter: Ester flags slow, rarely-catching tests; Mervin stops waiting on them
## Idea

In a swarm, a long test is a bottleneck: it holds PRs for hours while the rest of CI is fine. Ester already records how long runs take and which tests have never failed; Mervin already sees which PRs are waiting. Join the two so slow, rarely-catching tests stop holding up merges, the owner decides what to do about them, and the work that remains can spread across more machines.

Like the rest of Mervin and Ester, it is deterministic: no model, no tokens. The insights look like AI but are queries over an append-only record.

## What it adds

1. **A `slow` verdict next to `wait` in `scripts/ester.ts`.** A check far above the median, or over a threshold (say 10 min), is `slow`. A PR waiting only on a slow check goes to a non-blocking lane: merge on the fast checks, the slow one is owed.
2. **A board line from Ester to Mervin** saying where testing holds merging up, by check name: "3 PRs waiting on `stress.ts` (about 40 min), 1 on typecheck (2 min)". Today the board only says a PR is waiting.
3. **Slow-lane debt.** Merges made without the slow check go on a list ("N PRs merged since the last green slow run"). One later run compares against the last green sha. Green clears the 
codeSplitter: Ester flags slow checks; board line for where testing holds merging up
Closes #2335

First slice of the issue: a `slow` verdict and the board line.

- `ciOf` keeps each check's name, time and done state on the stage.
- `slowChecks` (scripts/ester.ts): a check is slow when its median time is 10 min or more, or 5x the median check. A PR waiting only on slow checks gets `slow` instead of `wait` and is not held.
- `waitLines`: "2 PRs waiting on stress.ts (about 40 min, slow: merge without it)", printed after Ester's report.
- Test: `test/ester.test.ts`; docs table updated.

title: codeSplitter: a crew member can't claim the check its own push queued
text:
codeSplitter: a crew member can claim an auto-queued required check and pass it unrun
From security round 6 (#2295). `POST .../checks/claim` is open to the crew, and the claimant may report `passed` for the run (`checks.ts`, PUT on a run). Only hand-queued runs are kept from their recorder. So a collaborator or injected agent holding a write token can claim the auto-queued required check on its own branch and mark it passed without running anything, clearing the merge gate. Possible fixes: the runner that claims must not be the branch's last editor, or only the owner's runners (or a CI token) may pass a required check. Needs a decision on the trust model.
codeSplitter: a crew member can't claim the check its own push queued
Closes #2320

A run queued by a non-owner's push, edit or Run press now starts its log with `queued by @user's push`, and `claimRun` skips it for that user, the same way hand-recorded runs are already kept from their recorder. Another runner (or the owner's) has to run it before the gate clears. The log line can't be rewritten by a non-claimer (existing PUT guard).

Trust model chosen: the runner must not be the branch's last editor. Owner-only runners/CI tokens remain a possible later tightening.

title: Twins: an edge-like mode that evicts idle DOs and names import-time env reads
text:
Twins: an edge-like mode that evicts DOs and resets Worker globals
The desktop and box run one long process, so an app that keeps state in module globals, timers or an un-evicted Durable Object works locally and loses it on the edge. ADOPTION.md now names this ("Where the same code stops being the same"), but nothing catches it before deploy.

Proposal: a `--edge-like` switch on `dev`/`smoke` for the twins that
- evicts idle Durable Objects after ~70 s (the shell already has `namespace.evict()`),
- reloads the Worker module every N requests so globals reset,
- warns when a module reads `process.env` at import.

Out of scope here: desktop-to-edge data sync and multi-replica boxes (documented as limits).

Twins: an edge-like mode that evicts idle DOs and names import-time env reads
Closes #2376

`RB_EDGE_LIKE=1` (or `rustybuns smoke --edge-like`):
- evicts a Durable Object after 70 s without an event (never one with storage calls or queued events in flight); the next event rebuilds it from storage
- warns once per `process.env` key read while the Worker module loads

Not done: resetting Worker module globals every N requests. The host bundles the Worker into one file, so it can't be re-imported; filed as #2379.

With `RB_EDGE_LIKE` set, the host restarts itself (same port and token) after 100 requests, or `RB_EDGE_RECYCLE=N` (0 never), so a module-level counter starts over. The Worker is bundled into one file and can't be re-imported, so a new process is how its globals reset. DOs keep their state in storage.

title: Agent Office in a box: sandbox it with a permission set (office:box)
text:
Agent Office in a box: sandbox it with a permission set (office:box)
Run the office in a container that can only touch what a permission set lists.

Follow-up to [local-build-monster.md](local-build-monster.md), which planned around the Macs we

pages on 2026-10-24, excl. VAT. Hetzner raised prices on 15 June 2026, so blog posts quoting

## What CI actually spends time on

From the GitHub API, `apps.yml`, 40 runs between 2026-10-23 20:47 and 2026-10-25 00:24 UTC:

- 540 jobs, about 300 job-minutes. Roughly 13 jobs per PR.
- Each job spends about 20 s getting ready (checkout 2 s, setup-bun 2 s, `bun install` 13-16 s)

title: Two Fronts: three-place intro world, and orbit control against landings
text:
Two Fronts: three-place intro world, and orbit control against landings
Part of the Two Fronts direction (see the epic). Make a small intro world with three places: ours, theirs, and an empty one in the middle, where a new player learns capital-ship space fighting before landing. Then make orbit control matter: winning space limits how many troop transports the other side can land long term; rushing the planet instead makes landing hard. Landing is into one place, and you fight out of it, flanked or with your back to a wall; with a big space battle above, the front can be wider. text:
This is about GitHub issue #2392 "MANUAL RUN: Agent Office auto-update needs a Tauri updater key and a manifest host" (https://github.com/QuinnsCode/RustyBuns/issues/2392). Read it with `gh issue view 2392 --comments`.

MANUAL RUN: Agent Office auto-update needs a Tauri updater key and a manifest host
**About 10 minutes, your hands.** Tauri's updater (`tauri-plugin-updater`) needs two things an agent must not make:

1. A minisign keypair: `cargo tauri signer generate`. Keep the private key in 1Password (varlock), and give the public key to a worker to put in `shell/tauri.conf.json`.
2. Where `latest.json` lives (GitHub release asset is the cheapest) so the shell can check it.

After that a worker adds a Check for Updates item to the tray menu and the release step in `desktop-drop.yml`.

Part of QuinnsCode/RustyBuns#2282. Related: QuinnsCode/rustybuns-manual#117.

The owner's design for where Two Fronts goes next, kept here so nothing lives only in chat. Never name a commercial game it echoes: say "a dice-and-territory board game".

**Balance first (PR #2406):** AI against AI should be pure 50/50. A human counts for a lot: measured with a scripted player, the human wins about 73% at even forces, 60% against a foe with +30%, and about 50% against +45% to +60%. So when a human is in the battle, the AI side should field roughly +40-50% and the whole thing stays a little less overrun, then tighter when it is AI against AI.

**Strategy layer, dice under the hood:**
- A commander rolls a d8; troops roll d6 attackers against d6 defenders, unless an ability or bonus changes that.
- Cards give bonuses in an area (the bigger columns/regions) or at one specific world.
- You go world to world.

**The intro world has three places:** ours, theirs, and an empty one in the middle. You learn capital-ship space fighting there, and only then start landing.

**Space against landing:**
- Space fighting limits the other side's long-term troop transports to the surface. Rushing the planet makes it very hard for you to land at all (think of how landing on the moon 
MANUAL RUN: walk the Two Fronts deep-space station by hand (~10 min)

**Scripted player (`scripts/balance.ts` `bot`).** Attacking at even forces it wins 17-23% (48 battles each, with and without orders) and dies 2-3 times a battle: it runs at the nearest foe and into the clubs. So the human handicap in `src/battle/handicap.ts` (0.45 on the AI attacker when the human defends, 0 on the AI defender when the human attacks) rests on the owner's figure and a bot that is wrong in both directions. Two Fronts: scripted player backs off when hurt and stays with its squad (part of #2444)

text:
Azure as a deploy target: pick a route (Alchemy has no Azure provider)
This needs a decision before anyone builds it. Today rustybuns deploys apps to Cloudflare and servers (`box` targets in `packages/cli/src/box.ts`) to Hetzner and Railway. Azure isn't an option.

## What is already done
- #2461 (merged): an Azure VM, or any Linux machine, can be the **builder** agents run tests on (`scripts/builder-setup.sh`, the "A Linux builder" section of `MAC_SETUP.md`). This needs no Alchemy. It hasn't been tried on a real Azure VM yet.
- Windows code signing through Azure Artifact Signing is covered in `WINDOWS_LINUX_SIGNING.md`.

## What we found (2026-10-27)
- Alchemy has no Azure provider in any published version: not 2.0.0-beta.77 (ours), not 2.0.0-beta.84 (latest), not 0.94.0 (the last 0.x). There is also no `@alchemy.run/azure` package (`@alchemy.run/gcp` and `@alchemy.run/aws` do exist).
- Alchemy's Kubernetes provider deploys into a cluster that already exists. You give it a kubeconfig, a token, a client certificate or a login plugin, and its docs name `kubelogin`, which is what Azure's managed Kubernetes (AKS) uses. Only AWS EKS can have its cluster created by Alchemy, so an AKS cluster would be made outside it (`az` or the portal) and would cost mone

Follow-up to #2529, which fixed the per-pixel and shadow-map cost. The geometry side is untouched: every frame still draws the whole park (about 650k triangles) plus about 400k into the shadow pass, because the ground, pieces and rails are single park-wide meshes and scenery sets frustumCulled=false (render/scenery.ts), so three's frustum culling never removes anything. No tiling, streaming or occlusion.

Suggested, in order of payoff:
1. Shadow casters: only what is inside the sun's 120 m box should cast. Split the merged pieces/rails per park cell (say 60 m tiles) so the shadow pass and frustum culling can drop tiles; keep the ride surface sampling untouched.
2. Ground: build the 2 m heightfield as tiles with a 4 m or 8 m version past 120 m (a simple distance LOD swap each frame, no THREE.LOD needed), and let tiles frustum-cull.
3. Scenery: give each InstancedMesh a computed bounding sphere per tile instead of frustumCulled=false, or split instances per tile.
4. Sky: a cheaper sky shader on the low tier (one fbm octave, or a gradient).
5. Barrier posts and critters: one InstancedMesh each instead of ~200 small meshes with their own materials; plumes should skip the attribute uplo

- Ground is a `THREE.LOD` per 64 m tile: 2 m heightfield near, 8 m past 120 m. Normals come from the height function so tiles shade without seams.

title: Splat Spray and Splat Rooms: splat budget by quality tier, no per-frame regeneration
text:
Splat Spray and Splat Rooms: a splat budget, and stop regenerating every frame
Gaussian splats are GPU-heavy by nature, and both apps have no budget, LOD or quality setting, so neither will run on an integrated GPU. Splat Spray: roughly 400-600k splats (9000 per square metre), mesh.updateVersion() every frame re-runs splat generation (src/main.ts), and every shot re-uploads the full float texture (src/reveal.ts). Splat Rooms: whole 1M+ splat scans loaded at once (game/view.ts), plus a full-screen Canvas2D mask repainted with gradients every frame. Suggested: expose the existing density option through the quality tier from packages/util/src/quality.ts (low = a third), call updateVersion only when the reveal changed, cap the pixel ratio at 1 on low, and in Splat Rooms repaint the mask only when a shot lands.
Splat Spray and Splat Rooms: splat budget by quality tier, no per-frame regeneration
Part of #2534.

- Splat Spray: room density 3000 / 6000 / 9000 per square metre on low / mid / high (`?quality=` or GPU guess), pixel ratio from the tier, and `mesh.updateVersion()` only while paint is fading or just changed (it ran every frame).
- Splat Rooms: pixel ratio from the tier, and the full-screen mask repaints only when the look direction, the shots or the size changed.

Left for #2534: Splat Rooms still loads whole scans at once (needs a LOD or decimated scan; not done here); Splat Spray's float texture re-upload per shot is unchanged.

Alien Disc Golf: Planet Earth: a new example, disc golf on a globe with NOAA's live GFS wind

CI: Actions cache is over GitHub's 10 GB cap, so container layer caches get evicted (AGENT_SANDBOX 69 s warm vs 190 s cold)
Found while timing CI in #2665.

The repo's Actions cache is at 10.6 GB (`gh api repos/QuinnsCode/RustyBuns/actions/cache/usage`, 473 entries), over GitHub's 10 GB per-repo cap, so GitHub evicts the least recently used entries. That includes the BuildKit `type=gha` layer caches for the container images (`ghaCacheArgs` in `packages/cli/src/containers.ts`, `mode=max`).

Effect on `containers codesplitter AGENT_SANDBOX`:
- cache hit: 69 s (18 s pulling cached layers, 40 s `--load`ing the 1.8 GB image into docker)
- cache miss (evicted): 164 to 190 s, rebuilding apt and `npm install -g` layers and exporting them again

Ideas, cheapest first:
- `mode=min` for single-stage images (only the final image's layers), and check what else fills the 10 GB (`gh cache list --sort size_in_bytes`): stale per-branch Swatinem rust caches are likely candidates.
- A scheduled job that deletes caches from closed PR branches.
- Skip `--load` when only the size is needed, or load once and reuse for the base-size delta.

Bun's install cache was left out of #2665 on purpose for this reason: the repo's node_modules is 3 GB and would push the layer caches out.

Repo-wide cut: fewer lines, fewer casts, one type per wire shape. Survey of 2026-10-27, counts from grep and approximate.

## Rules the work follows

- A type is declared once, in a `types.ts` or `wire.ts` next to the code that owns it, and imported by Worker, Durable Object, page and test alike. Never a second hand-written copy at a call site.
- A parsed body, fetch reply, socket message or stored string is `unknown` until one `decode(raw: unknown)` or guard looks at it. No `as X` after `.json()`, `JSON.parse`, `deserializeAttachment()` or `localStorage.getItem`.
- Where the type already flows (D1 `first<T>()`/`all<T>()`, the `"use server"` action proxies in `packages/cli/src/glue/desktop-scaffold.ts`), use it instead of casting.
- Grep before writing a helper; copies die in the same PR.

Git Recon: cheaper battle tick (baked heightfield, sqrt over hypot, soldier grid)
Found while checking whether the games would gain from Rust/wasm (`notes/RUST_WASM_GAMES.md`): they wouldn't, but Git Recon's 120 Hz battle tick has plain TypeScript wins. At 64 players it costs ~0.7 ms (ffa) to ~1.0 ms (teams) per tick, 8-12% of one core on the world that hosts it.

Measure with `bun apps/git-recon/bench/battle.ts` (and `bun --cpu-prof` for a profile). Self time today:

- ~30% terrain `height()`: the decorator chain in `packages/terrain/src/terrain.ts` (pads, paths, stamps) re-evaluated on every query. Bake the finished ground into one `Float32Array` heightfield at level load and sample it bilinearly.
- ~14% `Math.hypot` (102 calls across `src/sim`). Swapping it for `Math.sqrt(x*x + y*y)` took 64 players from ~1,030 to ~810 µs/tick (teams). Hippo Tycoon made the same change for 1.7x.
- ~10% `soldierAt`, each bullet against every soldier: a uniform grid of soldiers rebuilt per tick.

The page and the world run the same `Game`, so these change both together; `tests/battle.test.ts` already holds them to the same battle.

Git Recon: cheaper battle tick (baked heightfield, len over Math.hypot, soldier grid)
Closes #2680.

`bun apps/git-recon/bench/battle.ts 5`, µs per tick (the world steps at 120 Hz):

| | before | `len` | + baked ground | + soldier grid |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ffa 64 | 641 | 461 | 246 | **221** |
| teams 64 | 1026 | 862 | 490 | **439** |
| teams 32 | 585 | 485 | 268 | **262** |

That's 12.3% of a core down to 5.3% for a full teams battle.

- **Baked ground**: `baked()` in `packages/terrain` samples the finished ground (pads, trails, stamps) onto a half-metre `Float32Array` and reads it bilinearly. `mapRepo` bakes its result, so the page's scene and the sim read the same ground

Follow-up to #2698 (part of #1052). In `bun run tune`, the drake beats the shell tank 13% of the time and the plant bruiser 32%. Water against fire is part of it (+25%/-20%), but the drake's bot also rarely lands its beams. Fix this in the drake's bot (`src/bot.ts`) or its body (`src/roster.ts`) until both pairings are 40-60%, without breaking the skirmisher's 40-60% against the tank and the drake. Also worth adding: a dive attack from the air.
Wildclash: the fire drake holds its own against the heavies, and dives from the air (#2699)
Closes #2699.

## Why the drake lost
- **Its heavies came out as launchers.** The bot held fly-up to keep its height, and heavy with up held is the launcher, so most of its swings were launchers thrown in the tank's face.
- **It almost never fired its beam.** Bolts (cost 15) kept its energy under the beam's 35: 3 beams in 30 matches against the tank.
- **Its melee ultimate went off from 8 m away** and missed.

## What changed
- **Flyer bot** (`src/bot.ts`): lets go of up before any swing, saves energy for the beam, uses the melee ultimate only in reach, and hovers on the middle side of the tar

Mythic Masters: an open world between the arenas on a real-world supercontinent
Part of #1052. The region list is in #2708, and the creatures are in #2706.

The open world between the arenas: a **Pangaea-style supercontinent built from the real world**. The continents are pushed back together, but each place keeps its real geography and the folklore that grew there. You walk from the New Jersey Pine Barrens to the Appalachians to the Great North Woods, and every region hides the legends of the cultures that live there.

## The idea

- **One landmass, real places.** The continents are joined roughly as they were in Pangaea, so you can walk from North America to Africa and Europe, with Asia and Japan further on. Inside each region, the landforms, rivers, coasts and climate come from real elevation data, scaled down to a playable size.
- **An arena in each region.** It's the same arena layout everywhere, wearing that region's skin: the pine barrens, a bayou, the Highlands, a Kyoto shrine. Beating a region's arena opens the road to the next one.

Game idea 1: Wildclash, a creature arena brawler where size and weight are real
Plan: [notes/game-ideas/1-creature-arena.md](https://github.com/QuinnsCode/RustyBuns/blob/office/sprocket-259a/notes/game-ideas/1-creature-arena.md)

An arena fighter for elemental creatures (all our own designs). The roster and full movesets feel like a creature-collecting RPG, the combat is a 3D lock-on brawler with dashes, flight, a charge meter and beam clashes, and the arenas add platform-fighter knockback and ring-outs.

The twist is that body physics is real. Mass, size, speed, turn rate, air control and stamina come from each creature's body, so a heavy shell-cannon tortoise is a tank and a small electric mouse is a pinball that can beat the big fire drake by staying in its blind spot. Type matchups are capped at about ±25%, so they don't decide the fight.

**First slice:** one arena, the heavy tank vs the light skirmisher with 6 moves each, local 1v1 with dash, guard, charge, a beam clash and ring-outs, plus a headless bot-vs-bot harness that tunes the underdog matchup to a 40-60% win rate.

title: Read wrangler's token through --json; hint to unset a refused shell token (#2669)
text:
wrangler auth token | tail -1 recipes break on wrangler 4.155 (token moved to stderr), deploy gets 403
`rustybuns deploy` with `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN=$(bunx wrangler auth token 2>/dev/null | tail -1 | tr -d '[:space:]')` fails with `Cloudflare refused the API token for account … (HTTP 403)`, even though the wrangler login is fine.

Wrangler 4.155 no longer prints the token as the last line of stdout: with `2>/dev/null`, stdout is one empty line, and the token sits on stderr after the banner. So the recipe exports a wrong value. Wrangler's own token checked separately gets HTTP 200 on the account.

`rustybuns plan/deploy` don't need the export: with no `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` set, they read wrangler's login themselves through `wrangler auth token --json` (`packages/cli/src/cloudflare-auth.ts`). Workaround: `unset CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` and set only `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`.

Mythic Masters: creatures from world folklore instead of the API roster, and procedural models
Part of #1052. Follows #2698.

Wildclash becomes **Mythic Masters**. The roster moves off the renamed creatures from the stats API and onto creatures from world folklore and mythology. Those are public domain, so they're ours to use, name and draw.

## Goal

Each creature is a beast from a real legend: the Jersey Devil, the Mothman, the Hodag, the kelpie, the tengu, the gumiho, the Mapinguari. It has its folklore name, a body sheet (mass, height, six stats) and six moves that come out of its legend. The region list for the whole game is in the Mythic Masters regions issue (#2708).

## Steps

1. **Rename the app and the game** to Mythic Masters (`apps/wildclash` → `apps/mythic-masters`, page title, README, plan, docs row).
2. **Creature sheets by hand, from the legend.** Mass, height and stats follow from the story (the Jersey Devil is a light, fast flyer; the Lambton Worm is a huge, slow bruiser). Moves are named after what the creature does in its tale.
3. **Retire the API importer.** Keep the API's numbers as a reference for stat spreads and move power if that helps balance, but nothing the game ships traces back to it. Delete `scripts/import-roster.ts` once the folklore roster r
Mythic Masters: 64 folklore fighters on twelve fields, shared and teachable moves, move effects
Part of #2706 (step 2: the folklore roster; step 3: the API importer is deleted). Leaves #2753 open: the beast sheets per creature are coming in three art PRs running in parallel tonight.

**The roster** (`src/creatures.ts`)

title: artstewengine: admin forms work in a real browser (Origin: null)
text:
artstewengine: admin sign-in forms likely refused in a real browser (Origin: null)
Found while building eqosys (#2764), which started from artstewengine's code. artstewengine sets `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` (`src/worker.tsx`). Chrome then sends `Origin: null` on the page's own form POSTs, and `crossSite` in `src/env.ts` treats `null` as a foreign origin and answers 403. In eqosys, Chrome got `{"error":"cross-site request refused"}` on our own sign-up form until the policy became `same-origin`. The journey test misses this because it sets `origin` itself.

Fix: use `Referrer-Policy: same-origin` (or have `crossSite` fall back to `Sec-Fetch-Site` when the origin is `null`), then sign in on the dev server in a browser.

artstewengine: admin forms work in a real browser (Origin: null)
Closes #2767

- `Referrer-Policy: same-origin` instead of `no-referrer` (`src/worker.tsx`), the same fix eqosys got, so Chrome sends our own origin on form posts.
- `crossSite` (`src/env.ts`): if a browser still sends `Origin: null`, the request passes only when `Sec-Fetch-Site` is `same-origin`. A sandboxed or cross-site `null` is still refused.
- The journey test adds both `null` cases.

Verified: `bun test test/journey.test.ts` passes. On `vite dev` with throwaway test values, real Chrome ran make admin account, Add a payer, Sign out and Sign in, with no 403.

title: AGENTS: what to do when a push gets no CI run
text:
CI: two pushes to a PR branch got no pull_request workflow run (office/widget-302f, 2026-10-29)
Seen while landing #2805. Two consecutive pushes to `office/widget-302f` (commits `284343d2` at 18:40 UTC and the empty nudge `f20c789b` at 18:46) registered on the PR's timeline but GitHub created no `typecheck` or `apps` run for either, while pushes to other office branches in the same minutes (#2810's `f465a41e`, #2816's branch) got runs within ten seconds. Both workflows were `active`; rate limit was fine; the pusher was the same account.

What worked: `gh workflow run typecheck.yml --ref office/widget-302f` and the same for `apps.yml` ran green (the plan step diffs against the root commit on a manual run, so every app ran). Those runs don't attach to the PR's check rollup, though, so the branch still needed a real `pull_request` run. A rebase onto main pushed with `--force-with-lease` (`98cbddce`) triggered normally.

Nothing to fix in the repo that I can see. Filed so the pattern is on record: if a push gets no run within a minute, an empty commit does not help; a rebase (new head and new merge-base) did. If it happens again, note the branch and times here. Two sightings would be worth a support ticket.

AGENTS: what to do when a push gets no CI run
Closes #2828

The issue found nothing to fix in the repo, so this records the playbook where agents read it: an empty commit does not trigger a missing run, a rebase with `--force-with-lease` does, and a manual `gh workflow run` never attaches to the PR's checks. Docs only.

## Rules the work follows

- A type is declared once, in a `types.ts` or `wire.ts` next to the code that owns it, and imported by Worker, Durable Object, page and test alike. Never a second hand-written copy at a call site.
- A parsed body, fetch reply, socket message or stored string is `unknown` until one `decode(raw: unknown)` or guard looks at it. No `as X` after `.json()`, `JSON.parse`, `deserializeAttachment()` or `localStorage.getItem`.
- Where the type already flows (D1 `first<T>()`/`all<T>()`, the `"use server"` action proxies in `packages/cli/src/glue/desktop-scaffold.ts`), use it instead of casting.
- Grep before writing a helper; copies die in the same PR.

codeSplitter: merge-replay stops when the mirror's sync refuses a file
Found while replaying the last day's merges for the talk page (#2842).

`bun apps/codesplitter/scripts/merge-replay.ts 8bb92b18bd960649d205f268d5cbac9d28bdaae8` (the merge of main into #2754) throws at `replay` (merge-replay.ts:90). The mirror sync answers `state: "clash"` on `apps/wildclash/public/models/jackalope.rig.json` with "edits here that aren't committed yet touch the same lines upstream changed", even though the replay's mirror is pull-only and nobody edited it.

Two things are wrong:
1. The replay's pull-only mirror shouldn't think it holds uncommitted edits. This is likely the same bug a real user's mirror would hit (users never see git errors).
2. With several commits on the command line, one throw kills the whole run. It should record that merge as failed and go on.

Repro: the command above, from a checkout that has the commit (it's on `office/*` branches in the shared .git).

codeSplitter: merge-replay no longer stops when a file has a line too long for a doc (closes #2843)
Closes #2843.

**Cause.** Opening a branch materializes main's copy of each file it touches. `jackalope.rig.json` is one 47 KB line; a doc line holds at most 10,000 characters (`MAX_TEXT`), so seeding the Durable Object was refused (400) after its `files` row was already inserted. That left an empty doc for a file git has, which the next sync read as every line deleted by uncommitted edits, and it stopped with `state: "clash"`. Any real mirror with such a file and an open branch would hit this.

text:
USDZ for native iOS: procedural three.js models and beast rigs
Follow-up to #2890 (\`bun run usdz\`, which only converts the GLB files in \`apps/*/public/models\`).

Still without a native iOS path:

title: qCRM: its own session cookie name (#2911)
text:
Work on GitHub issue #2911: "qCRM: its session cookie shares a name with the QNTBR site's .qntbr.com cookie".

Read it first with `gh issue view 2911 --comments`. Create a new branch, implement the change, verify it, then open a pull request that closes #2911.

You're in your own git worktree, on a fresh branch made for this task. Commit there, push it, and open the pull request from it.
qCRM: its session cookie shares a name with the QNTBR site's .qntbr.com cookie
The QNTBR site (qbear3, on `qntbr.com` and `*.qntbr.com`) sets Better Auth's default session cookie `better-auth.session_token` with `Domain=.qntbr.com` (`crossSubDomainCookies`). That cookie also reaches `qcrm.qntbr.com`, where qCRM's own Better Auth session uses the same name (`apps/qcrm/src/auth.ts:97`, `src/me.ts:32`, `src/openapi.ts:203`). A browser signed in to both sends two cookies with one name, and qCRM may read the site's cookie, which it can't verify. The person then looks signed out of qCRM, or flips between signed in and out.

eqosys had the same problem and now uses `cookiePrefix: "eqosys"` (#2910).

Fix: `advanced: { cookiePrefix: "qcrm" }` in qCRM's Better Auth, and update the three places that name the cookie. Everyone signed in to qCRM gets logged out once, which is why this isn't folded into #2910. Alternatively, qbear3 could rename its own cookie, but anything new on `*.qntbr.com` would still collide with whatever name it picks.

qCRM: its own session cookie name (#2911)
Sets Better Auth `cookiePrefix: "qcrm"` so the session cookie is `qcrm.session_token`, no longer the `better-auth.session_token` the QNTBR site sets on `.qntbr.com`. Updated the cookie check, the logout clear, the OpenAPI scheme, the seed script and the demo test.

Everyone signed in to qCRM is signed out once.

Tests: `bun test` in apps/qcrm, 45 pass.

Closes #2911

rustybuns init: a Pages app that compiles schemas at startup needs allow_eval_during_startup
Part of #2191.

TerraViz's first Workers deploy uploaded, then Cloudflare refused to start the Worker: `ScriptStartupError: Uncaught EvalError: Code generation from strings disallowed for this context` (from `compileSchema`). `functions/api/v1/_lib/stac-query.ts` line 11 does `new Ajv(...).compile(...)` at module load. Desktop (Bun) allows that, Workers don't. Adding `"allow_eval_during_startup"` to `worker.compatibilityFlags` in the clone's `rustybuns.config.ts` fixed it (deployed and answering).

## To do
- `init` should add the flag (or print a clear line) when the app's bundle compiles code from strings at load. Easiest honest signal: a module-level `new Ajv(` / `.compile(` in the Pages Functions, or just warn when `ajv` is a dependency.
- A table test over a few inputs (ajv present at top level, ajv inside a function, no ajv).
- Check against Cloudflare's docs that the flag name is right and from which compatibility date it is the default; say so in the PR.

Small PR against main, `packages/cli`.
init: add allow_eval_during_startup for a Pages app that compiles schemas at load
Closes #2931.

`init` on a Pages project now scans `functions/` for a module-level Ajv `.compile(` (Ajv imported, call on an unindented line). If found and the compatibility date is before 2025-06-01, it adds `allow_eval_during_startup` to `worker.compatibilityFlags` and prints a `flag:` line.

Flag name and default checked in workerd's `compatibility-date.capnp`: `allow_eval_during_startup`, on by default from compat date 2025-06-01 (disable flag `disallow_eval_during_startup`). So a current date needs nothing, and the flag is skipped there.

title: TerraViz Shared Sphere: key codes, hands, crowd mode (Closes #2935)
text:
TerraViz Shared Sphere: join by key code, hands for everyone, and a crowd mode that blends all the steering
Part of #2191. Follows #2930 (Shared Sphere on Cloudflare); can start on desktop, so it doesn't wait for it.

## What the owner wants
A shared view you join with a short key code, and an interactive mode where a crowd of people each have a little hand and together move the world.

## Where it is
`apps/terraviz-demo/sphere/`: rooms by name (`?room=`), pointers as coloured dots with names, one Lead at a time, a teacher word that locks the room. No join screen, no hands, and only one person steers at once.

## Plan (one worker, one PR, based on main)
1. **Key code.** A room gets a short code (4 to 6 characters, no look-alikes such as 0/O, 1/I) made when someone opens a new room; a small join box takes it and lands you in that room. Keep `?room=` working for the teacher links in the README.
2. **Hands.** Each person's pointer becomes a hand (lucide `hand`, no emojis) in their colour with their name, hidden round the back as the dots are now.
3. **Crowd mode** (a room switch; the teacher turns it on, or anyone in a room with no teacher word). **Blend everyone:** clients send their drag *deltas*, not their camera, at most about 20 a second; the room's Durable Object adds them up each tic
TerraViz Shared Sphere: key codes, hands, crowd mode (Closes #2935)
Closes #2935.

- Key code: New room makes a 5-char code (no look-alikes); a join box takes one. `?room=` still works.
- Hands: pointers are lucide hands in each person's colour.
- Crowd mode: clients send drag deltas (<=20/s); the room blends them each 100 ms tick (mean x sqrt(hands), so same-way pulls add up and opposite pulls cancel) and broadcasts one camera.
- Limits: guarded messages, per-socket TokenBucket on drags, 100 hands per room, RoomMintGate (12 new rooms/min per address).
- Cost: a 100-hand room all dragging is ~2,000 incoming msgs/s, about a tenth of a cent a minute.

Mythic Masters: from 3/10 to great: much more detail, effects and moves on the beasts
Part of #2753. Follows the second art pass (#2779, PR #2797).

The owner scores where the beasts are now at about **3 out of 10**. The second pass made them read better at fight size, but they're still simple blob-and-stick shapes. Aim much higher, on three fronts:

- **Detail:** more shape and surface per beast. That means faces with expression (brows, lips, teeth, ears that read), hands and feet with digits and claws, layered fur and scales, and markings and colour variation beyond flat palette regions. It probably needs new builder parts (scales or plates, teeth rows, broad feathers, ears, fur rooted on blob surfaces), not just sheet edits. The builder gaps in #2795 are part of this.
- **Effects:** each beast's element and legend shown on screen. Glow, breath, sparks, mist, trails on moves, hit flashes and impact particles that match the move, aura on an ultimate, and footprints and dust on landing.
- **Moves:** animation that sells each of the six moves. Distinct poses and anticipation for light, heavy, launcher, special, beam and ultimate per archetype, wing beats, tail swipes, grabs, and creature-specific signature motions from the legends, beyond the shared IK lunge and rear

Mythic Masters: orbit-and-commit combat, weighty attacks (parallel round)
Part of #2802. Parallel to the art hill climb in #2943.

## The goal (owner's words, tidied)

Fights should be less about running in circles at each other and more about **weighty, committed melee**. The owner is happy to circle: the fighter orbits the opponent, and the opponent can switch circle direction, but the two never stand and face each other down in a straight line. Goal (owner): codeSplitter holds the repo the Agent Office works on, so the office can edit itself live. GitHub is a mirror: it keeps getting pushed to and pulled from, but if GitHub is down while the internet is up, workers and PR coordination (branches, Mervin merge waves, conflict repair) keep going on codeSplitter, and sync back when GitHub returns. 3. PRs and merge waves run on codeSplitter's branch/PR model; GitHub PRs are mirrored when up.
4. A GitHub outage drill: pull the plug, finish a PR and a merge wave, plug back in, nothing lost or doubled.

title: eqosys: Qollab design note, the multiplayer layer on the one account (Part of #3046)
text:
Spike: Qollab, a party kit beside eqosys (lobby, chat, cloud saves)
Spike: decide the shape first, build later. Nothing here is built yet.

## Why

About seven apps each rebuilt lobby, room code, ready and chat: `park-hide-seek`, `hippo-tycoon`, `splat-spray`, `git-recon`, `skate-tech-park`, `two-fronts`, `fm-daw`. Most games need only keys and permissions from eqosys plus a party kit. Qollab is that kit (working name).

## The split

- **eqosys** owns identity, access (keys and permissions), and the library of apps a person owns or has. It stays auth only.
- **Qollab** owns the social pieces: parties, lobby, room codes, ready and start, chat, and a cloud-save backup (opaque, versioned blobs per user per app, size quota, keep the last N).
- **Games** own live game state and the schema of their own saves. Gameplay sync, ticks and simulation stay in each game.

Everything stays Workers and Durable Objects. Services are partitioned like shards: by user id (one DO per user) and party id (one DO per party). Each service has its own D1; no shared tables, no cross-service joins. The eqosys token is the only glue, which is also a deliberate way to dogfood the cached token.

## Questions this spike must answer

1. **Friends and presence.** They live in eqos
eqosys: Qollab design note, the multiplayer layer on the one account (Part of #3046)
The spike's design note, `apps/eqosys/QOLLAB.md`, linked from eqosys's README. Docs only, nothing built.

What it settles, per the owner's direction on #3046: Qollab is eqosys's multiplayer layer, not a sibling product. Friends and presence stay in the `Hub`; games keep their own world state and read user things off the account. It lives as `/q/*` routes and a `Party` DO inside `apps/eqosys`, so there is no service-to-service auth to design yet. Qollab 5: cloud saves (opaque, versioned, quota)
`PUT /q/save/<slot>` and `GET` with the token; body up to 256 KB, never read by eqosys. Keep the last 5 versions a slot, 20 slots an app, 50 MB a person across apps. Last write wins, and the reply carries the previous version's id and time so a game can offer 'keep the cloud one' itself. D1 blobs for now; R2 when a game needs bigger.

Test: put, get, a sixth version drops the oldest, a body over the cap is a 413, one app's save is not visible under another app's token.

Design: `apps/eqosys/QOLLAB.md` (PR #3060). Part of #3046.
Spike: Qollab, a party kit beside eqosys (lobby, chat, cloud saves)
Spike: decide the shape first, build later. Nothing here is built yet.

## Why

About seven apps each rebuilt lobby, room code, ready and chat: `park-hide-seek`, `hippo-tycoon`, `splat-spray`, `git-recon`, `skate-tech-park`, `two-fronts`, `fm-daw`. Most games need only keys and permissions from eqosys plus a party kit. Qollab is that kit (working name).

## The split

- **eqosys** owns identity, access (keys and permissions), and the library of apps a person owns or has. It stays auth only.
- **Qollab** owns the social pieces: parties, lobby, room codes, ready and start, chat, and a cloud-save backup (opaque, versioned blobs per user per app, size quota, keep the last N).
- **Games** own live game state and the schema of their own saves. Gameplay sync, ticks and simulation stay in each game.

Everything stays Workers and Durable Objects. Services are partitioned like shards: by user id (one DO per user) and party id (one DO per party). Each service has its own D1; no shared tables, no cross-service joins. The eqosys token is the only glue, which is also a deliberate way to dogfood the cached token.

## Questions this spike must answer

1. **Friends and presence.** They live in eqos

Mythic Masters: beast decimation is chaotic, so the canonical snap step and the hydra head-spread bound are fragile
Left over from #3086 (fixes #3080).

`canonical()` in `apps/mythic-masters/blender/beast.py` snaps vertices to 1 mm so the decimator gives the same result every run. The decimator is chaotic, so the snap step chooses which valid decimation each beast gets. Steps of 0.1, 0.2, 0.25 and 0.3 mm each broke feet counts on snallygaster, imugi, hodag, flatwoods-monster or fur-bearing-trout. 1 mm broke none, but a new sheet or part can land on a bad one without anyone changing the step.

Also, with the rebuilt models hydra's head spread in the shake test read 0.028 h, below the old 0.03 h bound, so #3086 lowered the bound in `test/beasts.test.ts` to 0.01 h.

To do: pick a decimation that does not flip a beast's rig (for example decimate with a colour attribute weight, or a deterministic simplifier), then restore the 0.03 h bound and check hydra's heads by eye.
Mythic Masters: beast build escapes a bad decimation by trying the next snap step (#3088)
Part of #3088 (the snap-step half). The hydra bound is #3095.

The decimator is chaotic and the snap step in `canonical()` picks which valid decimation a beast gets. `bun run beasts` now tries a fixed list of steps (1 mm first, then 0.5, 2, 0.25, 4, 0.1 mm) and keeps the first whose rig matches the sheet's feet and wings. A new sheet or part that lands on a bad step fixes itself, and the build is still the same every run. All 76 beasts still build at 1 mm, so no model files change. Forcing an 8 cm first step made hodag fall back to 1 mm and pass.

eqosys: erase URL for games that keep account data
From the Qollab spike (#3046), answer 2 in apps/eqosys/QOLLAB.md. Account delete clears sessions, links, access, the hub, saves and party seats. If a game ever keeps per-account data it registers an erase URL in `APPS` and eqosys calls it with a signed token (`aud: "erase"`, 60-second life) until it answers 200. No game keeps account data today, so this waits for the first one that does. Related to #3046 (closed).
eqosys: erase URL for games that keep account data
Closes #3122.

An app in `APPS` may set `erase`. Account delete (page and `/api/account/delete`) POSTs there with a bearer token (`aud: "erase"`, `sub` the person, 60-second life), three tries. If an app never answers 200 nothing is deleted and the reply is `ok: false`, so deleting again is safe. No game sets it yet. `sign` gains a `life` argument.

Test: `apps/eqosys/test/erase.test.ts` (retry, token claims, account kept on failure).

title: bun run outline: read a file by symbol, not by sed -n range
text:
Reading code by sed -n ranges is the biggest agent chore: an outline tool or codeSplitter code mode
Dexter's chore count over 14 days of sessions (620 sessions, PR #3165): reading code by `sed -n` / `cat` / `grep` was 5,316 calls and 5.3M result tokens, with 1,084 streaks of the same chore back to back (an agent paging through a file range by range). It is the biggest chore by far and PR #3165 only added a tip for it.

What would cut it:

- A local outline tool: `bun run outline <file>` (or a codeSplitter MCP tool) that prints each exported symbol, function, class and top-level const with its line range and the first line of its doc comment, so an agent jumps to one `sed -n` range instead of walking the file. TypeScript's own parser, or a regex over the top-level declarations, is enough for this repo's style.

A deep spike done as a designer, not a feature pass. Each app has grown its own buttons, dialogs, sheets, toasts and HUD chrome, and most of that drift isn't thematic, it's accidental. codeSplitter is the reference: paper buttons, one orange, black and white, quiet grain. - a default skin in the house look, injected only when asked;
- a way for a game to pass its own theme tokens (or its own CSS) instead.
Every game uses the same keys list, rebinding and touch/gamepad trims, styled its way or the house way.

title: Qollab: app data stays in the app (decision, #3168)
text:
Work on GitHub issue #3168: "Decks stay in the app; eqosys only for sign-in (decision, nothing to build)".

Read it first with `gh issue view 3168 --comments`. Create a new branch, implement the change, verify it, then open a pull request that closes #3168.

You're in your own git worktree, on a fresh branch made for this task. Commit there, push it, and open the pull request from it.
Decks stay in the app; eqosys only for sign-in (decision, nothing to build)
**Decision (owner, 2026-11-01): decks stay in the deck app's own storage (`DECKS_KV`). Do not move them to eqosys `/q/save`.**

Split of jobs:
- **eqosys:** sign-in and user identity, shared by all the owner's apps.
- **Qollab:** connecting apps (parties, friends, presence). Its saves are for small per-person things that should follow someone across apps, not an app's main data.
- **The app:** its own game/app data, such as decks, with its own caps (10 draft decks, tier limits).

So the app should only read who the person is from eqosys (the OIDC `access_token` / `userinfo`) and key its own decks by that user id. Nothing is built; no change in eqosys is needed.

Open only if wanted later: use `/q/save/<slot>` for small cross-app user settings. Limits there: 256 KB per save, 5 versions, 20 slots per app, 50 MB total.
