title: Delayed Reaction: chunked offline render (128-bar track in 21 s, was 5 min)
text:
Delayed Reaction: offline render of a 128-bar track takes five minutes; place voices in chunks
`bun scripts/render.ts "?setup=warren"` (128 bars at 86 bpm, six minutes of audio) takes about five minutes of wall clock, and `--all` (six 128-bar and six 64-bar setups) the better part of an hour. A 56-bar slice of the same track renders in 15 seconds.

Cause: `Music.prepare` places every voice of the whole song on the offline clock at once (`schedule(Infinity)`), so Chrome processes thousands of not-yet-started oscillators, buffer sources, filters and gains on every render quantum for the full six minutes. The cost is node count times length.

Fix: schedule in chunks on the offline clock with `OfflineAudioContext.suspend(t)` / `resume()` every few bars, the same look-ahead the live clock uses, so only the next bar's voices exist at any time. The stems already render concurrently (PR #3214); this is the next step for `--all` to take minutes.

Delayed Reaction: chunked offline render (128-bar track in 21 s, was 5 min)
Closes #3216

`Music.render` replaces `prepare`: the offline context suspends just before each four-bar chunk, the next chunk's voices are placed, and it resumes, the same look-ahead the live clock uses. Only a few bars of nodes exist at once.

Verified: `bun scripts/render.ts "?setup=warren"` (128 bars, 86 bpm) went from about 5 min to 21 s; all 102 kicks found, worst 2.49 ms off grid, all numbers in range.

title: Mythic Masters: pin Blender threads so beast GLBs are the same on every Mac
text:
Work on GitHub issue #3156: "Mythic Masters: beast GLBs depend on the build machine's core count".

Read it first with `gh issue view 3156 --comments`. Create a new branch, implement the change, verify it, then open a pull request that closes #3156.

You're in your own git worktree, on a fresh branch made for this task. Commit there, push it, and open the pull request from it.
Mythic Masters: beast GLBs depend on the build machine's core count
Found while making `bun run beasts` run one Blender per core (#3155).

Blender's thread count (`-t`) changes the decimated mesh. On the 8-core office Mac, Cadejo's GLB hash is different at `-t 1`, `-t 2`, `-t 4` and the default (8). Only the default matches `main`. So a build on a Mac with a different core count, such as the 64 GB builder, rewrites GLBs that didn't change. #3086's snap makes builds repeat on one machine, not across machines.

Possible fixes:
- pin `-t` to one fixed number in `scripts/beasts.ts` and rebuild every GLB once
- or find the threaded step (decimate, voxel remesh or subdivision) and make its input canonical, the way #3086 did for the decimator

Pinning `-t` also lets the builder Mac run more Blenders at once without changing the output.
Mythic Masters: pin Blender threads so beast GLBs are the same on every Mac
Closes #3156

Blender's `-t` changes the decimated mesh, so a Mac with a different core count rewrote unchanged GLBs. `scripts/beasts.ts` now passes `-t 8`, the count the committed GLBs were built with.

Verified: `bun scripts/beasts.ts cadejo` with the pin leaves `public/models/cadejo.glb` byte-identical (no diff), so no GLBs need rebuilding.

title: eqosys: eq_execute, code mode over the eq_ tools
text:
Work on GitHub issue #3293: "eqosys: real code mode (an execute tool) so agents run a program over the eq_ tools".

Read it first with `gh issue view 3293 --comments`. Create a new branch, implement the change, verify it, then open a pull request that closes #3293.

You're in your own git worktree, on a fresh branch made for this task. Commit there, push it, and open the pull request from it.
eqosys: real code mode (an execute tool) so agents run a program over the eq_ tools
PR #3292 gives eqosys its tools (WebMCP, HTTP, CLI) and `eq_batch` with `pick`. A program with loops or branches still needs one call per step. Add an `execute` that runs agent-written JS with `tools.eq_*` in a no-network sandbox, like codeSplitter's (`apps/codesplitter/src/codemode.ts`), returning only what the program returns. Workers can't eval and the CSP forbids it, so it needs a Dynamic Worker or similar. Also worth doing: measure eq_batch against call-per-fact and screenshots, as WEBMCP.md does for codeSplitter.
eqosys: eq_execute, code mode over the eq_ tools
Closes #3293.

- `eq_execute` runs agent-written JS in a Dynamic Worker (`LOADER` binding, no network); each read tool is `await tools.eq_x({...})`, only the return comes back. Runs as the caller via an `EQBridge` entrypoint (props read through a guard); admin and read-only rules hold, it can't call itself, unknown tools are refused before running. Limits: 50 calls, 10 s, 20k chars.
- Test measures it against call-per-fact: ~88 tokens vs ~874 for a per-app loop. Screenshots comparison not measured.
- Docs: README, WEBMCP.md, /agents text.

title: codeSplitter: merge train cars, one speculative run per merge-plan wave (#3323)
text:
codeSplitter: merge train cars, one speculative run per merge-plan wave (follow-up to #3314)
#3314's first step shipped as the \`fresh_main\` check setting: after a merge, every other open branch's green goes stale and (checks running here) reruns on main as it is now. That's a car of one per branch, so N open branches cost N reruns per merge.

Left from the issue's plan:
1. **Cars.** For each wave from \`merge-plan.ts\`, build one speculative tree (main + A + B, the way \`proveMerge\` builds a merged tree) and queue it as one check run on a train ref.
   - A green car lets \`/merges\` (branches.ts) merge the whole car without rerunning.
   - A red car splits, and \`blocks\` names the PR to blame.
   - Different waves don't clash, so their cars run side by side.
2. **Lane.** Wire it into \`src/pipeline.ts\` as cadence \`train\`, so a repo picks fresh_main per branch or the train.

Ester's \`mervin-board.ts --check\` already tests every open PR merged together; the car builder may share its code.
codeSplitter: merge train cars, one speculative run per merge-plan wave (#3323)

text:
Work on GitHub issue #3325: "Agent Office: sweep what sent-home workers leave on disk, by rules that are provably safe".

Agent Office: sweep what sent-home workers leave on disk, by rules that are provably safe
The office Mac's disk filled to 36 MB free on 2026-11-03 and stopped every agent's shell. Two places grow and nothing trims them.

**1. Claude Code's scratch, \`/private/tmp/claude-501/<worktree-slug>\` (the big one).** One folder per session, keyed by worktree path. Sending a worker home deletes its worktree but not this folder. A manual sweep on 2026-11-03 found 450 folders of worktrees that no longer exist, about 11 GB (one, \`nibble-d15c\`, was 6.7 GB). It deleted them and freed about 8 GB.
- Rule: delete a folder only when its slug maps to \`<repo>/.agent-office/worktrees/<name>\`, the repo's \`worktrees\` folder exists, and \`<name>\` is not in it. Skip anything that doesn't parse.
- Gotcha: the slugs start with \`-\`, so pass them after \`--\` (\`du\` and \`rm\` read them as options otherwise).
- Run it in send-home, plus a sweep on office start.

**2. The bun cache, \`~/.bun/install/cache\` (39 GB).** It keeps every version ever downloaded. Worktrees' \`node_modules\` are APFS clones of it, so they cost close to nothing; the cache itself is the growth. Bun has no "drop what no lockfile uses" command, only clearing all of it.
- Optional, after (1): collect every \`bun.lock\`

Closes QuinnsCode/RustyBuns#3325.

Work on GitHub issue #3422: "hippo-tycoon: "LAN party: host and guests share one ticking world" flakes in CI".

Read it first with `gh issue view 3422 --comments`. Create a new branch, implement the change, verify it, then open a pull request that closes #3422.

You're in your own git worktree, on a fresh branch made for this task. Commit there, push it, and open the pull request from it.
hippo-tycoon: "LAN party: host and guests share one ticking world" flakes in CI
Seen on PR #3420 (a codeSplitter-only change). The test failed once and passed when only the failed job was rerun.

- Run: https://github.com/QuinnsCode/RustyBuns/actions/runs/41744415850/job/126293813329
- Failure: `expect(received).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(expected)` after 6020 ms in `(fail) LAN party: host and guests share one ticking world`, under `bun test --parallel test`.

It looks like a tick-count threshold that a loaded runner misses within the 6 s window. Fix: wait on the tick condition rather than wall time, or loosen the bound.
hippo-tycoon: LAN test waits for 30 snaps instead of a 2 s window
Closes #3422

The LAN party test counted snaps over a fixed 2 s sleep and required at least 8 per second. On a loaded CI runner it got fewer and failed (the job passed when rerun). Now it waits until 30 snaps have arrived (20 s cap) and keeps only the upper bound, which still tells the ~15 Hz send rate apart from the 30 Hz tick rate.

Verified: `bun test test/lan.test.ts` in apps/hippo-tycoon passes locally (5.6 s).

title: rustybuns: no deleted_classes hint for a flagged DO class (#3428); lift the drain after every deploy (#3433)
text:
Work on GitHub issue #3428: "rustybuns: a plan with codeSplitter's flags off suggests deleted_classes, which would wipe live Durable Object data".

Read it first with `gh issue view 3428 --comments`. Create a new branch, implement the change, verify it, then open a pull request that closes #3428.

You're in your own git worktree, on a fresh branch made for this task. Commit there, push it, and open the pull request from it.
rustybuns: a plan with codeSplitter's flags off suggests deleted_classes, which would wipe live Durable Object data
Seen 2026-11-03. Running `rustybuns plan` in apps/codesplitter without `CODESPLITTER_DEPLOYS=1 CODESPLITTER_AGENTS=1` stops with:

```
✗ Durable Object classes DeployRunner, AgentSandbox are in wrangler.jsonc's migrations but no longer bound. Say what happened in worker.migrations: { tag: "v6", deleted_classes: ["DeployRunner","AgentSandbox"] } (deletes the data), or { tag: "v6", renamed_classes: [...] }.
```

The real cause is that the flags are off, and a plain `DEPLOYS=1` is silently ignored because the config reads `CODESPLITTER_*`. The message's first suggestion, which the triage prompt hands to a coding agent, deletes the live hosted-deploy and agent-sandbox data. `release-codesplitters.sh` sets the flags and is unaffected.

Fix: when a class is unbound only because the config gates it behind a flag, the guard should name the flag (or the config should declare that these classes stay bound), and list "turn the flag back on" before `deleted_classes`.
rustybuns: no deleted_classes hint for a flagged DO class (#3428); lift the drain after every deploy (#3433)
Closes #3428. Part of #3433 (items 1 and 2; 3-5 stay open there).

### Flagged Durable Object classes (#3428)
Running `rustybuns plan` in apps/codesplitter without `CODESPLITTER_DEPLOYS=1 CODESPLITTER_AGENTS=1` stopped with an error whose first suggestion was `deleted_classes`. That would wipe the live hosted-deploy and agent-sandbox data.

- New `worker.flaggedClasses` (config type + schema): maps a Durable Object class to the flag that binds it. With the flag off, the run still stops before deploying, but the message names the flag and says not to add `deleted_classes`.

title: rustybuns: protect keeps the Worker, its Durable Object classes and containers through destroy (#3416)
text:
Work on GitHub issue #3416: "rustybuns: a protect option for Workers, Durable Objects and containers".

Read it first with `gh issue view 3416 --comments`. Create a new branch, implement the change, verify it, then open a pull request that closes #3416.

You're in your own git worktree, on a fresh branch made for this task. Commit there, push it, and open the pull request from it.
rustybuns: a protect option for Workers, Durable Objects and containers
Split out of #1400's "also open" note. #1381 gave D1, KV, R2, queues, Vectorize and Hyperdrive a `protect` option, so a deploy can't delete them. Workers, Durable Object classes and containers have none yet. A deploy that drops a Durable Object class loses its data, which is the case that matters most.
rustybuns: protect keeps the Worker, its Durable Object classes and containers through destroy (#3416)
Closes #3416.

A Durable Object class keeps its storage inside its Worker, so a class can't be kept on its own. Keeping one means keeping the Worker.

- `protect: true` on a `durable_object` or `container` binding, or `worker: { protect: true }`, adds `Alchemy.RemovalPolicy.retain()` to the Worker. `destroy` then leaves the Worker on the account, with every class it hosts and their storage. Under adopt the Worker gets `.pipe(AdoptPolicy.adopt(true), RemovalPolicy.retain())`.
- A protected `container` also retains its `Cloudflare.Container` (the container application).
- The KEPT/REMOVED report

rustybuns: Durable Objects now keep old code up to 5 min after a deploy (deferred code updates)
Since 2026-10-30 Cloudflare defers Durable Object code updates by default ([changelog](https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-30-durable-objects-deferred-code-updates/)). After a deploy, an active object keeps running its old code until it goes idle or hibernates, for up to 300 s (best effort). Hibernation-API WebSockets stay connected across the switch. You opt out per deploy with `--durable-objects-code-update-mode immediate|deferred <duration>`, or in wrangler config with `durable_objects.code_update_strategy { mode, max_delay }`.

rustybuns was written for "a deploy restarts every object at once". Where that no longer holds:

1. **Drain.** A file Durable Object that was told to drain refuses new claims until it restarts. It keeps that state in memory only ("a restart is the deploy"). On a deferred update, a busy file kept refusing claims for up to 5 minutes after the deploy. **Fixed in the linked PR:** `rustybuns deploy --drain-url` now lifts the drain after every deploy, not only after a failed one.
2. **Docs.** `REFERENCE.md` ("What a deploy does to live sessions") said every instance restarts and its sockets drop. **Fixed in the linked PR.**

title: eqosys: home fits the window again, and the deploy plan passes (no missing Qlave roster item)

eqosys: home fits the window again, and the deploy plan passes (no missing Qlave roster item)
On a normal desktop window the eqosys home was ~2,300px wide: the header and card rows ran off the right edge, so you had to zoom far out to see the page.

**Cause:** \`.home\` is a grid with one implicit \`auto\` column. That column grows to fit its content's min-content width, so the widest row of cards set the width of the whole page.

**Fix:** \`grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1fr)\` on \`.home\`. The column now stays at the page width (64rem at most), and each row scrolls inside itself as intended.

CUTMAN: cut LOC and casts repo-wide, one type per wire shape
Repo-wide cut: fewer lines, fewer casts, one type per wire shape. Survey of 2026-10-27, counts from grep and approximate.

## Rules the work follows

- A type is declared once, in a `types.ts` or `wire.ts` next to the code that owns it, and imported by Worker, Durable Object, page and test alike. Never a second hand-written copy at a call site.
- A parsed body, fetch reply, socket message or stored string is `unknown` until one `decode(raw: unknown)` or guard looks at it. No `as X` after `.json()`, `JSON.parse`, `deserializeAttachment()` or `localStorage.getItem`.
- Where the type already flows (D1 `first<T>()`/`all<T>()`, the `"use server"` action proxies in `packages/cli/src/glue/desktop-scaffold.ts`), use it instead of casting.
- Grep before writing a helper; copies die in the same PR.

Left over from the second art pass (#2779). Each one needs a builder change in `apps/wildclash/blender/beast.py` rather than a sheet edit:

- Smaller misses: the rougarou's side tuft rows read as flaps from the front, and the wampus cat's ruff reads as a jagged collar.

Work on GitHub issue #3497: "Pixel RAG: find the same face across photos (detect, embed, same index)".

Pixel RAG: find the same face across photos (detect, embed, same index)
The owner wants Pixel RAG (`apps/pixel-rag`) to find faces: drop in photos, click a face, and get every photo with the same person.

## Why the index can't do it today

The app cuts every picture into fixed 160 px squares, and each square gets a fingerprint of its shapes and colours. That finds the same button or chart across screenshots. It won't find the same person: a face is rarely one whole square, and the same face in different light, at a different angle or size gives a different fingerprint.

## What it takes

1. **Find the faces.** A small face detector, run locally (wasm in the tab, native on desktop), returns a box for each face.
2. **Fingerprint the face.** A face-embedding model turns each cropped face into a vector, so one person's faces come out close together and other people's far apart.
3. **Search.** Quantize those vectors to bits like the tiles' fingerprints, put them in the same shared index, and search them with the same Rust `hamming_topk`. The search engine doesn't change: only what goes into it does.

The rule from #3475 stays: local first, no hosted vector DB. The models run on the user's machine.

Pixel RAG: click a face, get every photo of that person (detect, fingerprint, same index)
Drop in photos, click a face, and every photo with the same person comes back. Closes QuinnsCode/RustyBuns#3497.

## How

1. **Find**: YuNet (OpenCV zoo, **MIT**, 230 KB) gives each face a box and five points.
2. **Fingerprint**: the five points line the face up in a 112 px crop (a similarity transform onto the usual template), and SFace int8 (OpenCV zoo, **Apache 2.0**, 9.4 MB) turns it into 128 numbers.
3. **Search**: the 128 numbers against 1024 fixed, seeded random directions give 1024 bits. They go through the crate's `quantize` into the rows after the tiles **in the same `SharedIndex`**,

text:
Work on GitHub issue #3501: "Mythic Masters: matchup locks hill climb to 90/100 (pairings the underdog can still win)".

Read it first with `gh issue view 3501 --comments`. Create a new branch, implement the change, verify it, then open a pull request that closes #3501.

You're in your own git worktree, on a fresh branch made for this task. Commit there, push it, and open the pull request from it.
Mythic Masters: matchup locks hill climb to 90/100 (pairings the underdog can still win)
From #2706, whose last step was "run `bun run tune` until every pairing is 40-60%". That target was set for 8 creatures; the roster is now 76 with a field chart, and it isn't met.

## Where it stands (2026-11-04)

- `bun scripts/tune.ts --fit 6` keeps every creature near 50% overall: 43-50% across all 76.
- Single pairings are not even. `cd apps/mythic-masters && bun scripts/tune.ts --each 6` (about 90 s) ends with **1,127 of 2,850 pairings are locks** (the underdog wins under 20%). A 52-pairing sample at 20 matches each had 34 outside 40-60%.
- The worst locks are slow tanks and bruisers against flyers and fast skirmishers, with long fights (Mapinguari vs Jersey Devil: 8%, ~93 s; Ahuizotl vs Mothman: 18%). That reads like the bot and reach, not the numbers alone; `edge` (damage dealt) can't fix it.
- The field chart is meant to lean a matchup (+25% / -20%, `src/fields.ts`), so 40-60% on every pairing may be the wrong target. Locks are the real problem: a pick that can't win.

## Score

Pairings that are not locks, out of 100: (2850 - locks) / 2850. Today **60/100**, target 90.

## Next

2. Look

The war panel was wordy: a world's sector rows, dropdowns and paragraphs of rules, and nothing that said plainly what you have, where it goes, or what happens. Now each phase is a call sheet: a few big picks in a row, a step strip over them, and one Confirm.

text:
Work on GitHub issue #3548: "Mythic Masters: the Book talks to you mid-journey and waits for an answer, hill climb to 8/10, rounds 3+ (from #3538)".

Read it first with `gh issue view 3548 --comments`. Create a new branch, implement the change, verify it, then open a pull request that closes #3548.

Mythic Masters: the Book talks to you mid-journey and waits for an answer, hill climb to 8/10, rounds 3+ (from #3538)
Score: 7.0/10 (target 8)

Moved up from #3538. Rounds so far: round 1 is #3539 (merged), round 2 is #3547. The owner's tone brief and the five-point goalpost are in #3532 and still hold: target 8/10 from the owner, and judges score about two points above the owner.

## Where it stands after round 2 (fresh cold judge, 7.0/10)
1. **Moments: 1.6/2.** Eleven beats now stop you: open, bind, bind-fail (this one stops the fight itself), downed, loss, streak, campfire, last-stone, trail-end, mythic, named. Regions 5 to 8 have their own mythic talks. Gaps: `signed` is used unevenly, and the probe shot shows the mid-fight talk over a bare backdrop.
2. **Answering: 1.5/2.** The save keeps replies, a nickname, and ledger notes; the latest note shows under the demand. Gap: no reply changes play.
3. **Jokes: 1.4/2.** 132 Book lines across 33 talks, and a test checks no two are alike. Gap: recalls hard-code where a reply was made ("In the pines", "Four regions ago"), which is false if it was made somewhere else. A few lines are circular or stock: "The ones who put things at the end.", "Do. Courage is not a line-up.", "Then you will get it, on time and in full."
4. **Group-safe: 1.0/2.** `holdOf`

eqosys skin: each game injects or updates its skin through the merged hook (three lines per game)
The eqosys skin hook merged in #3540 (`packages/util/src/skin.ts`, `eqosys({ ..., skin })`). Each game now carries its own look onto the eqosys surfaces: account chip, achievement toast, report form, party lobby and spaces panel. eqosys's badge (#3597) stays the same in every game, and with no skin the house look follows the system's light or dark mode. This issue lists what each game still needs, so each menu climb can pick up its own line.

## The three lines a game adds (in its `eqosys.ts`)

```ts
export const SKIN = { theme: { "--ui-bg": "var(--paper)", "--ui-ink": "var(--ink)", "--ui-accent": "var(--hot)" }, css: ".eq-who{font-family:var(--f-hand)}" };
export const { signIn, login, accountChip, reportButton, achieve } = eqosys({ app: APP, url: EQOSYS, from: SIGN_IN_FROM, prefix: "xx", skin: SKIN });
accountChip(document.getElementById("account")!, { note, onSignOut: () => location.reload() }); // replaces the game's own sign-in row
```

`theme` takes any `--ui-*` token from `packages/ui/src/tokens.ts`. Read the game's own CSS variables there rather than copying hex values. `css` adds rules on `.eq-form`, `.eq-toast`, `.eq-chip.in`, `.eq-who`, `.eq-btn`, `.rb-lobby` and `.rb-sp

title: codeSplitter: a run's reply drops lines quoting private lines it read, and its commit note leaves its words out (#3637)
text:
Work on GitHub issue #3637: "codeSplitter: a commit note can quote private lines from the other files an agent run read (round 10, medium)".

Read it first with `gh issue view 3637 --comments`. Create a new branch, implement the change, verify it, then open a pull request that closes #3637.

You're in your own git worktree, on a fresh branch made for this task. Commit there, push it, and open the pull request from it.
codeSplitter: a commit note can quote private lines from the other files an agent run read (round 10, medium)
From security round 10 (`notes/SECURITY_AUDIT.md`). Confirmed from source, not executed; severity medium.

**What**: `commitNote` (`apps/codesplitter/src/why.ts:34`) keeps an agent's own words (its handoff note, or the DONE/NEXT/BROKE/DONT lines of its reply) out of the commit's git note only when the committed file itself has private lines (`open` at `worker.ts:903` and `pick.ts:226` is per path). A fix or rebuild run reads its `also` files as the agent handle, a collaborator, so crew: their private lines arrive with real text (`agent-run.ts:191-194`). `hidden` gathers every private line the run read (`agent-run.ts:310`) but `leakIn` runs only over the files the agent wrote back, never over `output` or the handoff note (`agent-routes.ts:668, 683`). A note quoting another file's private line goes onto the public remote's `refs/notes/codesplitter` and is served by `GET /api/repos/:o/:r/commits/:sha/note` to any reader.

**Fix**: in `runAgent`, once `hidden` is known, redact output lines that contain any hidden text (the `leakIn` rule, `MIN_HIDDEN` and all) before `output` is returned, and do the same to the handoff note in `finish`; mark the run (`result.private = true`) when `hidde
codeSplitter: a run's reply drops lines quoting private lines it read, and its commit note leaves its words out (#3637)
Closes #3637.

A fix or rebuild run reads its `also` files as crew, so their private lines reach the agent with real text. Only the files it wrote back were checked for copies; its reply (stored on the run, used for the handoff note, and written into the commit's git note on the public `refs/notes/codesplitter`) was not.

- `leaks.ts`: `redact(text, hidden)` cuts every line quoting a private line, with `leakIn`'s rule (`MIN_HIDDEN`, trimmed).

title: eqosys: a handoff code goes only to an app's registered callback (#3634)
text:
Work on GitHub issue #3634: "eqosys handoff: a return URL is bound to an app's origin, not its registered callback (round 10, high)".

Read it first with `gh issue view 3634 --comments`. Create a new branch, implement the change, verify it, then open a pull request that closes #3634.

eqosys handoff: a return URL is bound to an app's origin, not its registered callback (round 10, high)
From security round 10 (the security-audit skill, run on codeSplitter and eqosys; `notes/SECURITY_AUDIT.md`). Confirmed from source, not executed; severity high.

**What**: `returnTo` (`apps/eqosys/src/apps.ts:76-82`) lets a handoff `return` be any path on one of the app's registered origins (or any URL on its custom scheme). Neither `/login`, `/do/continue` nor `/oauth/token` compares a registered callback, and the `codes` row keeps no return URL. codeSplitter's origin is registered, and codeSplitter serves pages any account holder writes at `GET /api/users/<name>/page` with inline scripts allowed (`apps/codesplitter/src/page.ts:37-50`; `page.ts:143` keeps the query on the `PAGES_ORIGIN` redirect). So a link `/login?app=codesplitter&return=https://codesplitter.../api/users/<attacker>/page&challenge=<attacker's S256>` hands a signed-in eqosys user's code to the attacker's page: silently when they already have a links row for that app, else after one press of a Continue page that names only the app. The attacker trades it at `/api/exchange` with their verifier for the person's id, email, name, roles and a token that eqosys accepts on account routes (`/api/privacy/export`, `/api/acco
eqosys: a handoff code goes only to an app's registered callback (#3634)
Closes QuinnsCode/RustyBuns#3634.

A `/login` return could be any path on one of an app's origins, so a page any codeSplitter account writes (`/api/users/<name>/page`, inline scripts allowed) could receive a signed-in person's code, and with the attacker's own PKCE challenge it traded in for that person's token.

**eqosys**
- `APPS` gains `returns`: the exact URLs a sign-in comes back to, matched after dropping the fragment. Left out, each origin's root `/`, which is where `@rustybuns/util/eqosys` returns for every game in this repo (checked: each signs in from its `index.html` at `/`). QNTBR

Mythic Masters: run the balance sims in Rust, byte for byte with the TS sim
The tuner is slow enough to shape how we balance. On the office Mac, `bun scripts/tune.ts --each 20` (2,850 pairings, 57,000 bot fights) takes about 4 minutes, and `--fit 6 4` about 12. The flyer round (#3518, PR #3621) needed about a dozen bot variants, so I scored only the 834 flyer pairings (about 3 minutes, four runs in parallel) and refit once at the end. A faster sim means full-table scores per variant and refits at 20 matches instead of 6.

## The idea
Port the fight sim and the bot to Rust (`src/sim.ts`, `src/bot.ts`, plus what they read from `roster.ts`, `moves.ts`, `fields.ts`, `creatures.ts` and `balance.json`: about 1,500 lines, no DOM). Run the tuner on it, and prove it matches the TS sim **byte for byte**: same seed, same creatures, the same `Match` state every tick.

## Shape: one sync, functional crate that runs on the server and in the browser
- **Pure and synchronous.** `step(match, inputs) -> match` and `bot(state, seed) -> input` are plain functions over plain data. No async, no tokio, no I/O, no globals, no clock. A fight is a sequential loop of ticks, which is what it already is in TS.

From security round 10 (the security-audit skill, run on codeSplitter and eqosys; `notes/SECURITY_AUDIT.md`). Confirmed from source, not executed; severity high.

**What**: `returnTo` (`apps/eqosys/src/apps.ts:76-82`) lets a handoff `return` be any path on one of the app's registered origins (or any URL on its custom scheme). Neither `/login`, `/do/continue` nor `/oauth/token` compares a registered callback, and the `codes` row keeps no return URL. codeSplitter's origin is registered, and codeSplitter serves pages any account holder writes at `GET /api/users/<name>/page` with inline scripts allowed (`apps/codesplitter/src/page.ts:37-50`; `page.ts:143` keeps the query on the `PAGES_ORIGIN` redirect). Work on GitHub issue #3667: "Pull the edge whoIs (eqosys token or guest uid) up into @rustybuns/util: six copies".

Read it first with `gh issue view 3667 --comments`. Create a new branch, implement the change, verify it, then open a pull request that closes #3667.

You're in your own git worktree, on a fresh branch made for this task. Commit there, push it, and open the pull request from it.
Pull the edge whoIs (eqosys token or guest uid) up into @rustybuns/util: six copies
Six games have the same edge door, `whoIs(url, env)`: an eqosys token checked with `TokenChecker` becomes `eq:<sub>` and the token's name, and anyone else is a guest with a browser-made uid (`UID`, 8-64 chars) and a cleaned name.

- `apps/git-recon/src/edge/eqosys.ts`
- `apps/splat-spray/src/edge/eqosys.ts`
- `apps/hippo-tycoon/src/eqosys.ts`

The fix: one `whoIs({ app, eqosys, fallbackName })` in `packages/util/src/token.ts` (or its own `edge-who.ts`), with the optional `get` for tests, then delete all six copies in the same PR. Each app's existing door test covers it.

title: codeSplitter threads: a crew member's @agent asks the owner to start it again (#3728)
text:
Work on GitHub issue #3728: "codeSplitter threads: may a crew member start the agent again from a thread?".

Read it first with `gh issue view 3728 --comments`. Create a new branch, implement the change, verify it, then open a pull request that closes #3728.

codeSplitter threads: may a crew member start the agent again from a thread?
Carried over from #3720 (item 3), which the threads list and @mentions PR closes. This one is the owner's call.

**Today:** once a thread's run has ended, only the repo's owner can start the next one (Go, or @agent in what they say). A crew member who says @agent gets `started: null, why: "only the repo's owner starts its agent again"`. It's the same rule as starting a run, because a desktop run uses the owner's own CLI login and a hosted run bills the site's keys.

**The question:** should a crew member be able to start the agent again from a thread?

Ways it could go:
1. **Keep it owner-only** (today). Close this issue.
2. **Crew can, on the desktop only**, where it's the owner's own CLI and machine. Hosted stays owner-only.
3. **Crew can ask, the owner approves**: a crew member's @agent after the run has ended @mentions the owner ("sam wants the agent to pick this up again") and the owner's Go starts it. This builds on the mentions inbox from #3720.
4. **A per-repo setting** the owner turns on.

Part of #3423.

- Local first. A hosted preview

codeSplitter team threads: a one-command demo for a test account (florence)
A small spike: one command that sets up team threads (#3711, #3714, #3731) for a test account, `florence`, so someone new can sign in, plug their own agent in and try it, with no keys, deploys or bill.

## What they get
`bun run thread-demo` (in `apps/codesplitter`) starts codeSplitter on the local twins (like `scripts/live-demo.ts`) and seeds:
- a demo repo, owned by a demo owner, with `florence` on its crew;
- a running agent thread on one file, whose agent answers in the thread and goes on when told something;
- a sign-in link it prints: open it and you're `florence` (alias mode signs in by name; no password).

From there Florence can:
- chat in the thread, as the page and as the modal, and see the agent react;
- drop a file or screenshot in and watch the agent get it;
- open the file page and see its runs come in without polling;
- **plug in their own agent**: the printed MCP config line (or `bun run cli`) lets their Claude Code `tell_agent` into the same thread from a terminal.

## Spike scope
- The agent is scripted by default (canned answers, like `test/fake-claude.ts`), so nothing is billed. `--real` uses their own `claude` CLI login instead.
- Local first. A hosted preview

1. His sign-up link, which puts him on the crew of the demo repo.
2. A paragraph he pastes into Claude Code. It claims its own agent invite with curl, opens a thread on `src/greet.ts`, and keeps answering him there over plain HTTP using the token it got. There's no `claude mcp add` step and no restart.

Mythic Masters walk together: a jump is believed only at a landing spot this player could reach
Found by the round 15 judge (#3785, PR #3789).

`landing()` (`apps/mythic-masters/src/net/dens.ts`) believes a jump to any arena, campfire or trailhead in `T.land`, including ones in regions the player hasn't opened and campfires they never visited. So a page can teleport to any of them, be trusted at once, and walk to a den in a locked region.

The room has no save to check against, so a full fix needs some care. Options:
- A jump lands only in the player's current region, or a region next to it, unless it's their first pose.
- The page sends the region list it has opened. That is a claim, but it bounds how far a lie reaches.

Done when a test shows a jump to a locked region's campfire stays untrusted, honest travel still lands trusted (all 88 cases from round 14), and the price stays under $0.005 per player-hour.
Mythic Masters walk together: a jump is believed only at a landing spot in a region the save has opened
Closes #3791.

Until now `landing()` believed a jump to any arena, campfire or trailhead in the world, including ones in regions the player hadn't opened. A page could teleport into a locked region, be trusted at once, and report dens and contracts there.

I went with the issue's second option. The first one (only your current region or one next to it) would doubt honest travel, because the big map lets you travel to any region you have won, however far away.

Found by the round 15 judge (#3785, PR #3789).

1. **`vouch` retells contracts, not dens.**
   - When the room trusts a player again it sends `vouch`, and the page runs `onCompany` (`shareHunts` plus `seen`, in `apps/mythic-masters/src/main.ts`).
   - A den walked into while untrusted is not told again: `src/edge/region.ts` cleared `met` when it refused the den, so the friend never hears the den and the fight report after it is dropped.
   - Fix: on `vouch`, the page also tells the den it is at (with `ago`, as after a reconnect).
2. **Trust only returns on your own pose.**
   - `beside` is checked only when the untrusted player moves. If they stand still while a trusted friend walks up, nothing changes: no `vouch`, and they stay untrusted.
   - Fix: when a trusted player's pose lands within BESIDE_M of an untrusted seat, clear that seat's flag and send it `vouch`.
3. **No test of the real page's path.** `test/online.test.ts` runs `vouch` against a stand-in `onCompany`. The Chrome journey (`test/together.test.ts`) should take a contract while untrusted and see it reach the friend.

Fix Ester (codeSplitter's merged-tree test check) so it stops reporting false failures on PRs that touch the game apps.

Root cause (already found, don't re-investigate): #3190 added `export-ignore` lines to the root `.gitattributes` for 8 game apps (hippo-tycoon, mythic-masters, skate-tech-park, two-fronts, git-recon, alien-disc-golf, park-hide-seek, delayed-reaction) so ZIP downloads leave them out. `apps/codesplitter/scripts/shadow.ts:200` builds Ester's trees with `git archive "$tree" | tar -x -C "$dir"`, which honours export-ignore, so the trees have no game apps. Mythic Masters walk together: a seat's first pose is believed wherever it stands
Found while doing #3791 (PR #3797).

Since #3797, a jump is believed only at a landing spot in a region the page says its save has opened. But the first pose a seat sends to the room is never a jump, because `step` (`src/net/party.ts`) has nothing to measure it from. So a page that joins already standing in a locked region, or right beside a stone, is trusted from its first pose. This worked the same way before #3797.

Options:
- A first pose is trusted only at a landing spot in a claimed region, or beside a trusted friend. Otherwise the seat starts out doubted. That would doubt an honest page that joins mid-walk until it reaches a campfire or a friend, so check how often Start lands somewhere other than a landing spot.
- At least require that the first pose's region is in the page's claim (the `open` event).

Done when a room test shows that a page joining in a region it hasn't claimed stays doubted, an honest Start still lands trusted, and the price stays under $0.005 per player-hour.

Mythic Masters walk together: a contract or den taken in the frame of a jump is checked against the pose before it
Found while working on #3790.

When a page teleports and walks onto a sighting board in the same frame, `reach` takes the contract and calls `online.hunt` **before** that frame's `online.update` (`apps/mythic-masters/src/main.ts`, world tick ~line 1528). `Online.hunt` runs `sendPose()` first, but `here` still holds the last frame's pose. So the room checks the contract against where the player stood *before* the jump. `huntNear` allows 2 km, so the contract is believed even when the jump itself would have flagged them. `met` (dens) has the same ordering.

Repro: the Chrome journey in `test/together.test.ts`. From the campfire at (20175, 5674), teleport straight onto board `1.20002.6206` (559 m away). The friend gets the contract, though the room would doubt the jump. The journey now jumps to 100 m short of the board first, to work around this.

Fix idea: have `hunt` / `met` refresh `here` from the world's pose before `sendPose` (pass the pose in, or have main.ts call `online.update` before the place hooks run). Test: the same journey step, without the 100 m stop first.

The owner's direction (2026-11-06): the multiplayer and chat features that get rebuilt in nearly every game become Qollab primitives the game calls. Games first. codeSplitter stays standalone (#3818 closed), and Excalibrawl and What Would Fantano Say are skipped for now.

CUTMAN keeps going as a hill climb, so `bun run climbs --next` hands out a sweep round whenever a worker is free. Carries on from #3484 (round 3), #3479 (round 2) and #2489 (moves 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6 merged there).

## Score

`Score = 10 - (unchecked values in scripts/boundary-audit.allow.json) / 40`, to one decimal. `bun scripts/boundary-audit.ts --update` prints the count. 220 gives 4.5, 201 gives 5.0, and the target of 9 means 40 or fewer unchecked values repo-wide. Follow-up to #3903 (merged in #3907). Part of #3878.

#3907 added the `invite` party rule (anyone in / the host). With "the host", two things change:
- With "friends of anyone in", only the host's friends count.

text:

codeSplitter pipeline: run the bus's AI pass and the merge hooks' AI review off the request
From #3983 (slice 4 of #3313). The bus's AI pass (`src/pipeline-bus.ts`) is awaited inside the commit's checks, and the merge hooks' AI review (`hookGate`, `src/pipeline-hooks.ts`) inside the merge route. So a commit that fills a bus, or a merge with an `ai` hook, waits for an agent run that can take minutes. On the hosted site that holds the request open.

Ask: start both as background work (`waitUntil`, or an `agent_runs` row the sandbox finishes) and let the check run or the hook card say *running* until the verdict comes back. The verdict is already claimed before the agent starts (`bus_passes`, `hook_verdicts`), so a retry while it runs still pays nothing. This also closes slice 1's gap: the AI review isn't in the run list.

**What changes for people:** filling a bus with a commit, or merging a branch with an `ai` hook, no longer holds the request open while an agent reads the change (that can take minutes on the hosted site).

- **Merge hooks:** the first merge claims the hook's verdict as `running` for the branch as it is, and answers 409 straight away. The hook card says *reading the branch*. Once the agent answers, merging again goes on (yay) or holds with the reason (nay).

The token gate in `apps/codesplitter/src/tokens.ts` (`bearer`) turns a call away with an untagged 403 when the token can't do it: read-only, held to another repo, not admin scope, a cookie-only route, or a live socket. title: rustybuns: a custom domain also gets its exact route, so a zone's wildcard route can't take it
text:
Work on GitHub issue #4006: "rustybuns: a custom domain is silently beaten by a wildcard route on the zone (eqosys preview went to qntbr.com)".

Read it first with `gh issue view 4006 --comments`. Create a new branch, implement the change, verify it, then open a pull request that closes #4006.

You're in your own git worktree, on a fresh branch made for this task. Commit there, push it, and open the pull request from it.
rustybuns: a custom domain is silently beaten by a wildcard route on the zone (eqosys preview went to qntbr.com)
Seen 2026-11-08 during #3898. `eqosys --stage preview` deployed with `domain: "eqosys-preview.qntbr.com"`. Alchemy attached the custom domain, and the dashboard showed it, but every request still went to another Worker: qbear3 (qntbr.com) has the route `*.qntbr.com/*`, and on Cloudflare a route takes precedence over a Custom Domain on the same hostname ([docs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/routing/routes/)). The site answered with a 302 to https://qntbr.com/... and the deploy looked fine.

The owner unblocked it by hand: a route `eqosys-preview.qntbr.com/*` on the preview Worker (most specific route wins). That route isn't in the config or Alchemy's state.

Fix in rustybuns: when an app sets `domain` (top level or per stage), also make the exact route `<domain>/*` for its Worker, or at least have `plan` warn when a wildcard route on the zone covers that domain. Then remove the hand-made route on `eqosys-worker-preview-*` (or let the deploy adopt it). Production eqosys.qntbr.com works today; check how, so the fix matches it.

rustybuns: a custom domain also gets its exact route, so a zone's wildcard route can't take it
Closes #4006

**What was wrong:** on Cloudflare a zone route beats a Custom Domain on the same hostname. qbear3's `*.qntbr.com/*` took every request to `eqosys-preview.qntbr.com`, so the preview answered with qntbr.com's 302 while the deploy looked fine.

**What changes:** when an app sets `domain` (top level or per stage), the generated Alchemy Worker also gets the route `<domain>/*`, beside any `routes` the config lists (not added twice if it's already there). title: Park Hide & Seek: the closing-circle test's walk can't stall
text:
Work on GitHub issue #4079: "Park Hide & Seek: the closing-circle countdown test can time out on its walk".

Read it first with `gh issue view 4079 --comments`. Create a new branch, implement the change, verify it, then open a pull request that closes #4079.

You're in your own git worktree, on a fresh branch made for this task. Commit there, push it, and open the pull request from it.
Park Hide & Seek: the closing-circle countdown test can time out on its walk
`apps/park-hide-seek/tests/two-player.test.ts`, "a camper outside the closing circle gets a countdown, is safe back inside, and is out when it runs down" (added in #4024), failed once in CI with `walk timed out` after 43.5 s, then passed on a rerun of the same commit.

- Run: https://github.com/QuinnsCode/RustyBuns/actions/runs/42583380232/job/129047351617 (PR #4077, a change that doesn't touch park-hide-seek; it touched `packages/`, so every app's suite ran at once)
- The `walk` helper moves the camper 0.8 per 50 ms report toward or away from the circle's middle through `tryMove`, and gives up after 40 s. Two likely reasons it never got there: a loaded runner, or `tryMove` held against an obstacle on the way from a random `openSpot`, so the camper never reaches the edge.

Fix: make the walk unable to stall (step around a blocked move, or move the camper straight to a point just inside or outside the circle), so the test doesn't depend on the route or the runner's speed.

Park Hide & Seek: the closing-circle test's walk can't stall
Closes #4079.

The closing-circle test walked the camper with `tryMove`, which refuses a step up a steep rise, so a walk from a random open spot could hold against a slope or a trunk until its 40 s ran out (the CI failure in #4079).

The walk now moves the way the host does: a straight step, then `resolve` pushes it out of whatever it walked into, so the test's body stays where the host has it. If a step makes no headway (a trunk dead ahead), the next one goes half sideways round it.

Ran `tests/two-player.test.ts` on the builder: both tests pass.

title: codeSplitter merge: an edit both sides made to the same lines reaches the lines each side added (#4133)
text:
Work on GitHub issue #4133: "codeSplitter merge: a file both sides added comes out clean but keeps only one side's edit on lines both wrote (#2654, fm-daw net.ts)".

Read it first with `gh issue view 4133 --comments`. Create a new branch, implement the change, verify it, then open a pull request that closes #4133.

You're in your own git worktree, on a fresh branch made for this task. Commit there, push it, and open the pull request from it.
codeSplitter merge: a file both sides added comes out clean but keeps only one side's edit on lines both wrote (#2654, fm-daw net.ts)
Found by the full #1141 shadow check (run for #3946): the only merge in 69 where codeSplitter's own merge broke tests that pass on what landed.

**What happened.** PR #2654's merge 17cdbb0 (fm-daw). Both sides created `apps/fm-daw/src/ui/net.ts` (no base version, so a merge from empty). main's lines report `{ state: "online", peers, locked }`, the branch's lines report `{ state: "online", peers, floor }`. git conflicts on them. codeSplitter calls the file clean, but on each of those lines it keeps one side's version, so the result drops `locked` from some status calls and `floor` from others:

```diff
-      else if (m.t === "floor") { floor = { state: m.state, host: m.host }; opts.onStatus({ state: "online", peers, floor, locked }); }
+      else if (m.t === "floor") { floor = { state: m.state, host: m.host }; opts.onStatus({ state: "online", peers, floor }); }
-        opts.onStatus({ state: "online", peers, floor, locked });
+        opts.onStatus({ state: "online", peers, locked });
```

(`-` is what landed, `+` is codeSplitter's merge.) What landed keeps both fields. The same merge's `Full.tsx` also came out clean, with the branch's single-component layout and main's split car
codeSplitter merge: an edit both sides made to the same lines reaches the lines each side added (#4133)
Closes #4133.

**What was wrong.** One fm-daw merge from PR #2654 (net.ts) came out clean but broke two tests. The issue's title says the file was added on both sides, but it wasn't: there was a base version. Main added a `floor` field to every `onStatus({ state, peers })` call, and the branch added `locked` to the same calls. On those shared calls the word merge kept both fields. But main also wrote a new `floor` call, and the branch a new `lock` call, and each of those new calls carried only its own side's field. So the merged file lost `locked` on one call and `floor` on another.

## The goalpost

**Target 7/10** for how a fight feels to watch and to play: weighty, committed melee where the fighters circle but never stand and trade, hits you can see land (squat, stagger, camera shove, shockwave), and wind-ups you can read and punish.

Agent judges run about 2 points high on visual climbs (#2943: judges 5, owner 3), so the owner's score at the target decides it, through one MANUAL RUN.

The owner scores where the beasts are now at about **3 out of 10**. The second pass made them read better at fight size, but they're still simple blob-and-stick shapes. Aim much higher, on three fronts:

- **Detail:** more shape and surface per beast. That means faces with expression (brows, lips, teeth, ears that read), hands and feet with digits and claws, layered fur and scales, and markings and colour variation beyond flat palette regions. Yes, it still happens. No Bun release after 1.4.4 exists yet (1.4.4 is still the latest), and building the box on `oven/bun:1.4.4` today (linux arm64, local Docker) panics in `bun install --frozen-lockfile`: `index out of bounds: the len is 1985 but the index is 4294967295`, during the isolated install. It's the same failure the Linux CI runners hit.

This PR uses the workaround the issue suggested: install on 1.4.3, compile on 1.4.4. A compiled binary embeds the Bun that built it, so binaries built this way get 1.4.4's CVE fixes (#2228) without running 1.4.4's broken install.

**Code mode (`packages/util/src/codemode.ts`):**

Mythic Masters spike: a texture maker for beast hides (scales, spots, fur, skin)
The owner wants better skin textures on the beasts, starting with the four-legged Tatzelwurm (PR #4178, Part of #4172), and better textures in general. This is a spike: find out what works, show it on one beast, and report back before anything is rolled out.

## Where textures stand

`blender/beast.py` has no textures. Each part is one flat Principled material from `PALETTE`, and the hide's look (belly, `paint` patches, countershading, AO) is written into a per-vertex colour attribute, `tone`, and multiplied in. On a 6,000-triangle starter, a vertex is the smallest thing that can change colour, so the builder can't draw scales, spots, scutes, fur or pores. The `scales` part makes geometry shards instead, and at fight size they read as jagged spikes.

## The spike

A texture maker the beast builder calls after the mesh is done:

- UV-unwrap the joined beast (Smart UV Project or a seam per chain) and bake an albedo map, plus a normal map if it helps, from procedural Blender nodes (Voronoi for scales and spots, noise for skin and fur) into the GLB. The triangle budget stays the same, and the detail lives in the image.
- Hides as sheet params a sheet can opt into: `hide: {pattern: "sca

Work on GitHub issue #3527: "Tests that bite: check new tests fail on the old code, then property and mutation tests".

Read it first with `gh issue view 3527 --comments`. Create a new branch, implement the change, verify it, then open a pull request that closes #3527.

You're in your own git worktree, on a fresh branch made for this task. Commit there, push it, and open the pull request from it.
Tests that bite: check new tests fail on the old code, then property and mutation tests
From `notes/TESTING_TRUST.md` (written 2026-10-13, removed in #3521; full text in git history). The note was a plan, and none of this is built yet.

The problem: PRs arrive faster than anyone can read them, and a green check only means the tests that exist passed. AI-written tests tend to confirm whatever the AI-written code does. The goal is not more tests but evidence that the tests can fail.

## Highest gain first

1. **Fail-before / pass-after check** (`scripts/test-bites.ts`, about 30 lines plus its test). For a PR that adds or edits `*.test.ts`, run those files against `origin/main`'s source: `git worktree add` the base in a scratch dir, copy the PR's test files over it, `bun test <files>`, expect failures. A new test that passes on old code proves nothing.
2. **Changed-lines coverage, report only.** `bun test --coverage --coverage-reporter=lcov` on the touched app, then list changed lines (`git diff -U0`) with no hits. Finds code nobody ran. Don't gate on it.

Git Recon: rewatch the in-level set pieces (insertion, jump, extraction...) once seen
Follow-up to #4096 (memories: rewatch a cutscene once you've seen it).

Git Recon's film (the newsreel, the credits) can now be watched again from the menu. Its in-level set pieces can't yet, and they're the most meme-able parts: the helicopter insertion and slow-motion drop, the strike that knocks your gun away (incoming), the roadster jump and dive-roll bail-out, the hovercraft that deflates, the landing craft, the barrage, the extraction up the rope ladder.

Why they weren't in the first cut: `apps/git-recon/src/sim/director.ts` runs them as live gameplay beats driven by the game state (your input, the squad, the vehicle you're in). They aren't standalone scenes in a `SceneTable`, so `playNamed` can't replay them.

Possible approaches, owner to pick:
- Record the beat's camera, stage and the soldiers' positions while it plays, then replay that recording on the level's world (like the newsreel's `footage`).
- Or restage each beat on a fresh copy of the level, with scripted input (like `stageClip` in `src/sim/credits.ts`), and mark it as a memory when the live beat first finishes.

Either way: mark with `memories.mark` from `@rustybuns/util/memories` once the beat has been seen to
Git Recon: watch the in-level set pieces again once you've seen them
Closes #4097.

Git Recon's set pieces are live gameplay beats, so there was no scene for the menu to play again. I took the second approach from the issue. `src/sim/rewatch.ts` builds the beat's level again, stages only what the beat needs to start, and then plays the beat with scripted input. What it stages: a yard's guards are taken down for the strike, a roadster is put beside you for the jump, and the clock is moved on for the hovercraft and the barrage. The page's normal frame plays the take, so you see the real beat in the real renderer, with the camera, letterbox, radio and slow motion.

## Goalpost (owner, 2026-11-10): the Book reacts to you, then its hand frays

Two stages, in this order.

1. **It reacts to you.** A surface counts when its line names something *you* did: a beast you bound, saw or let go, your last fight, a reply you gave, a setting you changed. A line that only fits the page doesn't count, and neither does one demand shared across several pages.
2. **Its hand frays.** Once every surface reacts, the Book's hand gets more scrawled the longer one of its demands goes unmet (#3278 option 1C).

Each surface is half a point (the owner's halving, 2026-11-05), so stage 1 tops out at 5 and stage 2 carries it to 10.

text:
Work on GitHub issue #4267: "Mythic Masters: the puppet reads a beast with tall wings as half upright (Mothman leans half as far in flight)".

Read it first with `gh issue view 4267 --comments`. Create a new branch, implement the change, verify it, then open a pull request that closes #4267.

Mythic Masters: the puppet reads a beast with tall wings as half upright (Mothman leans half as far in flight)
Found while rebuilding set B in #4249 (PR #4257).

`Puppet` decides how upright a beast stands from its rig root's height over the whole mesh's height
(`this.upright = clamp01((this.rest.y / sheet.height - 0.45) / 0.25)` in `apps/mythic-masters/src/beasts.ts`).
`sheet.height` is the rig's height, which counts wings. A biped whose wings tower over its head reads as half upright,
and `upright` scales how far it leans into a flight, how far its legs trail and how much it bobs.

From the rigs in #4257 (the root's share of the height, then `upright`):

| beast | old model | rebuilt |
|---|---|---|
| Mothman (wing tips at 2.8 m over a 2.2 m body) | 0.653, 0.81 | 0.562, 0.45 |
| Kappa (a real crouch, so this one is fair) | 0.646, 0.78 | 0.552, 0.41 |
| Jersey Devil (first build, big haunches put the root low) | 0.640, 0.76 | 0.434, 0.00, failed the upright-flyer test; fixed in the sheet, now 0.70 |

The Mothman is the one to fix: it is a standing biped, but it now flies leaning about half as far as before. Ideas:

- measure `upright` against the body's height without the wings (the rig already knows the wing joints: `sheet.wings`)
- or against the head's height (`headOf`) rather than the 
Mythic Masters: a winged biped is measured to its head, not its wing tips
Closes #4267

**What was wrong:** the puppet works out how upright a beast stands by comparing its hips' height to the whole rig's height, and that height counts the wings. The Mothman's wing tips rise well above its head, so it came out half upright (0.45). That made it lean about half as far into a flight, and its legs trailed and it bobbed less.

**The fix:** a new `uprightOf()` in `src/beasts.ts`. When a beast's head stands over its hips (a winged biped), its height is measured to the head instead of the wing tips. Wings folded over a back that runs forward still count, so a sphinx or snal

Part of #4249 (lane 1, hides v2).

`stylize` in `apps/mythic-masters/src/beasts.ts` adds a view rim term scaled by `1 - luminance`, plus the sky fill. On pale or blue-green beasts in the gallery (Nessie, Tatzelwurm, Leshy) it washes the whole silhouette toward white, so they read as glass or ice. It is the same on main's GLBs, before any baked hide (shot compared 2026-11-11).

It also caps how slick a hide can look: under about 0.6 roughness the specular stacks on the rim, so the hide patterns' roughness (`ROUGH` in `blender/beast.py`) stays above it and wet skin can't truly shine.

Do: soften the rim on a material with a roughness map (or scale it by roughness), and cap the rim on pale materials. Judge with gallery close-ups of Nessie, Tatzelwurm and Loveland Frogman (`bun run probe mythic-masters "?gallery=1" --js ... focus('nessie','three-quarter')` as in `docs/HIDES.md`), and check a fight still reads at stadium size.

The 2026-11-12 overnight stall (session ef9f309b, a `.claude/worktrees/mythic-factions` session, not an office worker) was **not** the model ending its turn on a notice. The transcript shows:

- 07:50:08 a background install's task-notification arrives **mid-turn** (`queue-operation` ... `reason: "absorbed_mid_turn"`). The turn was still the owner's.

title: kitesurf-bench: turn off Browser Run's cache so each turn is a real render
text:
Work on GitHub issue #4369: "MANUAL RUN: Kitesurf bench, our numbers (deploy, run, paste, destroy)".

Read it first with `gh issue view 4369 --comments`. Create a new branch, implement the change, verify it, then open a pull request that closes #4369.

You're in your own git worktree, on a fresh branch made for this task. Commit there, push it, and open the pull request from it.
MANUAL RUN: Kitesurf bench, our numbers (deploy, run, paste, destroy)
**About 10 minutes, on the office Mac. Needs your Touch ID for the deploy. Free on the Kitesurf side; about a minute of Chromium browser time.**

Measures Cloudflare's Kitesurf against Chromium on our own live pages, using `apps/kitesurf-bench` (#4368, on top of the `browser` binding from #4353). Merge #4368 first.

1. `cd apps/kitesurf-bench && bunx rustybuns plan`: it should show one Worker and the BROWSER binding, nothing else.
2. `bunx rustybuns deploy`, then open the URL it prints.
3. Press **Run the bench** (3 turns per engine is the default). It takes a couple of minutes.
4. Press **Copy results** and paste the JSON in a comment here. A screenshot of the table works too.
5. `bunx rustybuns destroy`.

What we'll learn: time per read on our pages for each engine, Cloudflare's reported browser time if it sends one, and which of our pages Kitesurf can't handle (the Skate Tech Park row is the WebGL case). It won't show CPU or memory: those are measured inside Cloudflare's engine, and a Worker can't see them.
kitesurf-bench: turn off Browser Run's cache so each turn is a real render
The first live run of the bench (#4369) gave medians of about 20 ms on every row. Turns 2 and 3 reported the same browser time as turn 1, to the decimal: Browser Run had cached turn 1's result (it keeps a Quick Action result for 5 s by default). So every median was a cache hit, and only turn 1 was a real render.

This passes `cacheTTL: 0` on every call, so each turn renders the page again. The test checks that every call carries it.

Part of #4369. After this merges, a redeploy and one more run give real medians.

text:
Work on GitHub issue #4505: "fm-daw Shape: per-track EQ, Nyquist-matched bells, linear phase, band listen".

Read it first with `gh issue view 4505 --comments`. Create a new branch, implement the change, verify it, then open a pull request that closes #4505.

fm-daw Shape: per-track EQ, Nyquist-matched bells, linear phase, band listen
Follow-ups to Shape, the master EQ (#4503). These were left out to keep the first version small. Take them one at a time, each as its own PR.

- **Shape on every track.** Today it sits on the master only. A per-track insert (each track summed after its own Shape) needs the engine to render tracks into their own buffers, in both Rust and TypeScript.
- **Bells that keep their shape near Nyquist.** The bilinear transform narrows a high bell (for example 15 kHz at 48 kHz). Matched second-order coefficients (Vicanek, "Matched Second Order Digital Filters", 2016) or 2x oversampling inside the EQ would fix that. The curve already shows the narrowing honestly.
- **Linear phase mode.** An FIR built from the same curve, run with FFT convolution. It needs latency compensation in the sequencer and the bounce. Useful for mastering, and it shows "phase" as a choice.
- **Listen to a band.** Hold a dot to hear only its range (band pass at its frequency and Q), then let go to return to the full mix. This is the quick way to find a ring.
- **Automate the EQ.** Make bands automation lanes, like track params.

fm-daw Shape: bells matched up to Nyquist, and hold a dot to hear only its range
Closes #4505. Of its five items, two are here; the other three each got their own issue, as #4505 asked for one PR per item:
- Shape on every track: #4516
- Linear phase mode: #4517

**Bells keep their shape near Nyquist.** Bells now use Vicanek's matched second-order design ("Matched Second Order Digital Filters", 2016). The matched biquad is mapped back onto the same trapezoidal SVF, so a bell still glides without clicks and `response()` still draws exactly what plays. Work on GitHub issue #4687: "Spike: happy paths from a RustyBuns web app to iOS (home-screen web app, WebView shell)".

Read it first with `gh issue view 4687 --comments`. Create a new branch, implement the change, verify it, then open a pull request that closes #4687.

Spike: happy paths from a RustyBuns web app to iOS (home-screen web app, WebView shell)
Spike: find the happy paths from a RustyBuns web app to an iPhone, without rewriting the app. Not a main goal; this is a try-out. Related: #2876 (iOS shell, xcframework and TestFlight), `notes/STORES.md`.

## The words

- **Swift**: Apple's programming language. Every iOS app has at least a little.
- **SwiftUI**: Apple's toolkit for drawing native screens in Swift. Feels like a real iPhone app, but every screen is a rewrite of our web UI.
- **WebView (`WKWebView`)**: a browser tab with no address bar, inside the app. Same engine as Safari. Our built page (HTML, JS, wasm) runs in it unchanged; the Swift part is ~50 lines that open a full-screen window.

## Happy paths, easiest first

1. **Installable web app (Add to Home Screen).** The deployed app plus a manifest and a service worker for offline. Full-screen icon, no Mac, no App Store review. Close to free.
2. **`rustybuns build ios`: the page inside a tiny Swift app.**
   - The built page is bundled into the app and shown in a full-screen WKWebView.
   - The backend (Workers-style `fetch()` code) runs in a Web Worker inside that WebView; a small shim sends the page's `/api` fetches to it.
   - D1 becomes SQLite compiled to wasm on

Closes QuinnsCode/RustyBuns#4567.

**Device sync.** `src/relay.ts` is a small Cloudflare Worker with one Durable Object that only fans out. After anything a page shows changes (a job made, edited, deleted, synced, run by hand, or a minute that fired), the Bun server POSTs `/publish`; every open page's socket hears `{ t: "changed" }` and fetches `/api/jobs` again. The DO stores nothing and keeps no clock, so the Bun ticker stays the clock. Sockets hibernate between nudges. text:
Work on GitHub issue #4686: "Look again: a libretro-style save/load contract for game sims (save states, rewind, rollback netplay)".

Look again: a libretro-style save/load contract for game sims (save states, rewind, rollback netplay)
A note to look at this again later. It came out of a chat about what libretro has that RustyBuns games don't. Nothing is built yet.

## What libretro is

Libretro is one small C header (`libretro.h`, MIT) that splits a game into two halves:

- A **core** (the game or emulator) does three things: step one frame from the inputs, hand back video and audio, and save its whole state to bytes and load it back.
- A **frontend** (RetroArch) does the rest: the window, audio, controllers, shaders, saves and netplay.

Because every core keeps the same contract, every frontend feature works with every core for free.

## What it has that we don't

1. **One contract shared by every game.** Our `state()` handles for `bun run probe` read a game's state, but they can't load it back.
2. **What save and load make free:** save states anywhere, rewind, run-ahead (lower input lag than the original game), and replays.
3. **Rollback netplay.** Machines predict the other player's input and roll back when the guess was wrong. Qollab rooms are server-authoritative instead, which is worse for frame-tight duels in Mythic Masters.
4. **A shared shader layer** over any game's output.
5. **Controller mapping at s

title: bun run preview: a PR's preview on demand, one comment with the URL, taken down on close or after 3 days (Closes #2238)
text:
Work on GitHub issue #2238: "Preview deploy on demand (Worker Previews + PR comment, destroyed on close)".

Read it first with `gh issue view 2238 --comments`. Create a new branch, implement the change, verify it, then open a pull request that closes #2238.

You're in your own git worktree, on a fresh branch made for this task. Commit there, push it, and open the pull request from it.
Preview deploy on demand (Worker Previews + PR comment, destroyed on close)
**Not needed now. Parked.** Build it only when someone actually asks for a preview.

## Design: on demand, not on every PR

Nothing deploys by default. A preview is made when someone says "now make me this".

- **Trigger:** a `/preview` comment on the PR, or the `preview` label. Agent Office can add a "Preview this" button, and an agent can ask for one with `office-workers preview <pr>`.
- **What it does:** deploys that one PR as an Alchemy Worker Preview (`preview: { of: parent }`, [docs](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/compute/previews)) with its own Durable Objects, then posts or updates one PR comment with the URL. A later push refreshes a preview that already exists; it never creates one.
- **Cleanup:** destroyed when the PR closes, after a time-to-live (about 3 days), or on `/preview off`.
- **Cost guard:** one preview per PR, a cap on how many are live at once. Price the per-PR resources first.

## Blockers

- Needs shared state (#2237) so CI can see the stack.
- The CI token is a secret the owner sets, so that part becomes a `MANUAL RUN:` issue when we get there.

Alchemy CI guide: https://alchemy.run/environments/ci. Map: `notes/ALCHEMY.md` (#2234).

title: Splat Rooms: the scan splat budget follows the quality tier (Closes #2534)
text:
Work on GitHub issue #2534: "Splat Spray and Splat Rooms: a splat budget, and stop regenerating every frame".

Read it first with `gh issue view 2534 --comments`. Create a new branch, implement the change, verify it, then open a pull request that closes #2534.

You're in your own git worktree, on a fresh branch made for this task. Commit there, push it, and open the pull request from it.
Splat Spray and Splat Rooms: a splat budget, and stop regenerating every frame
Gaussian splats are GPU-heavy by nature, and both apps have no budget, LOD or quality setting, so neither will run on an integrated GPU. Splat Spray: roughly 400-600k splats (9000 per square metre), mesh.updateVersion() every frame re-runs splat generation (src/main.ts), and every shot re-uploads the full float texture (src/reveal.ts). Splat Rooms: whole 1M+ splat scans loaded at once (game/view.ts), plus a full-screen Canvas2D mask repainted with gradients every frame. Suggested: expose the existing density option through the quality tier from packages/util/src/quality.ts (low = a third), call updateVersion only when the reveal changed, cap the pixel ratio at 1 on low, and in Splat Rooms repaint the mask only when a shot lands.
Splat Rooms: the scan splat budget follows the quality tier (Closes #2534)
Splat Rooms thinned every scan to a flat 500k splats. Now the quality tier sets it: low 170k (about a third), mid 300k, high 500k, the same steps Splat Spray uses.

The rest of #2534 was already on main:
- Splat Spray: density per tier (3000/6000/9000 per m²) and a splat budget per tier; `mesh.updateVersion()` runs only while a reveal is animating; a shot uploads only the texture rows it painted (#2627); pixel ratio capped by the tier (1 on low).
- Splat Rooms: pixel ratio capped by the tier; the Canvas2D mask repaints only when the view, the shots or the size change.

Closes #2534

1. A warm `blender -b` on Bob that takes jobs over a local socket, started and stopped by a script (`bun run builder` style, `effect`-scoped: it must not outlive the session).
2. Three calls through it: `load(glb)`, `stats(part)` and `render(vi

title: codeSplitter mirrors: a fork's commits from before the turn go up as this machine's git identity
text:
Work on GitHub issue #4771: "codeSplitter mirrors: a fork's commits from before it was a mirror go up under the person's identity".

Read it first with `gh issue view 4771 --comments`. Create a new branch, implement the change, verify it, then open a pull request that closes #4771.

You're in your own git worktree, on a fresh branch made for this task. Commit there, push it, and open the pull request from it.
codeSplitter mirrors: a fork's commits from before it was a mirror go up under the person's identity
Moved from #4333 (audit 2026-11-12, at `72281fae`). It says what you do and what comes back.

- [ ] **Commits made in a fork before it becomes a mirror go upstream under the person's identity** (`ana <ana@codesplitters.local>`), not the machine's, which REFERENCE.md ("Commits go up as this machine's git `user.name` and `user.email`") promises. Turning a fork (`turnRoute` in `src/mirror.ts`) pushes the commits since the dig as they are. Fixing it means rewriting those commits' author before the first push (with a `Co-authored-by` for handles other than the owner, as `byline` in `archive.ts` does), and checking nothing here holds their old shas (notes, line history).

codeSplitter mirrors: a fork's commits from before the turn go up as this machine's git identity
Closes #4771

Before this, turning a fork into a mirror pushed the fork's commits since the dig unchanged, under the person's handle (`ana <ana@codesplitters.local>`). REFERENCE.md says every mirror commit goes up as this machine's git `user.name` and `user.email`, so this was a broken promise.

**What changes** (`apps/codesplitter/src/mirror.ts`)
- When a fork is turned, it gets a `refs/turned/<branch>` marker at the commit it was dug at.
- Before that mirror's first push (in both `step` push paths), its own commits are made again as this machine's identity, the same way `byline` in `archive.

text:

Read it first with `gh issue view 4772 --comments`. Create a new branch, implement the change, verify it, then open a pull request that closes #4772.

codeSplitter merge cards: moved blocks, lint with no way out, word blends, mergiraf's answer dropped (4 items)
Moved from #4333 (audit 2026-11-12, at `72281fae`). Each item says what you do and what comes back.

- [ ] **The card for a block one side moved and edited shows `branch: null`.** Picking `main` or `both` lands 200 and leaves `const x = compute(2, "fast");` / `return x;` orphaned at top level beside a function holding the branch's body.
- [ ] **A blended stretch that fails lint has no way out.** Main rewrites a loop into one line, the branch edits a line of the loop, and the merge makes `sum = items.reduce((s, it) => s + it.price, 0) * it.qty;`. Lint refuses it (409 `MergeBroken`), but the only choice offered is `lint:undefined:it`: `main` returns the same 409 every time and `branch` lands the broken line. - [ ] **With `MERGIRAF` on, its clean answer is thrown away when it differs from the card's layout.** A function the branch moved and renamed a local in, while main edited a call: the binary merges it

Now the card shows both lines, and main, branch, both and text all land inside the moved block. A one-line word merge still settles it when it can.

title: codeSplitter lines, claims and picks: queued grants, neighbour clashes, private reverts, overspent runs (Closes #4773)
text:
Work on GitHub issue #4773: "codeSplitter lines, claims and picks: queued grants, neighbour clashes, private reverts, budget after one round (4 items)".

Read it first with `gh issue view 4773 --comments`. Create a new branch, implement the change, verify it, then open a pull request that closes #4773.

You're in your own git worktree, on a fresh branch made for this task. Commit there, push it, and open the pull request from it.
codeSplitter lines, claims and picks: queued grants, neighbour clashes, private reverts, budget after one round (4 items)
Moved from #4333 (audit 2026-11-12, at `72281fae`). Each item says what you do and what comes back.

- [ ] **A waiter granted its lines can't take the grant by id while someone is queued behind it.** `POST …/do/claims {id}` answers 409 `LinesQueued`, and with `wait: true` 409 `HoldingLines`, against what `claim_lines` says to do. It can still edit by naming the claim, and with nobody behind the same call is 200.
- [ ] **Revert and cherry-pick answer 409 `PickClash` when a different, neighbouring line changed** ("the same lines changed since"). `merge3` in `src/sync.ts` wants the line either side untouched. Git's own merge also stops on touching hunks, so decide first whether picks should be looser than git (`plan` in `src/pick.ts` could try a looser merge there only).
- [ ] **A commit that changed only a private line can't be reverted** (409 `NothingToPick`); the same merge without the private mark reverts with 200. The repo's git has the line blank on both sides, so the pick has to read the crew's copy. Since the PR for #4333, a change to private lines alone makes no commit in the repo's own git at all (no empty commits), so the revert has to start from the crew's commit.

title: codeSplitter git: notes without a run, line endings kept, no forced pushes to the desktop remote, no dangling staging commit
text:
Work on GitHub issue #4774: "codeSplitter git: missing notes, line endings, forced pushes to the desktop remote, a dangling commit (4 items)".

Read it first with `gh issue view 4774 --comments`. Create a new branch, implement the change, verify it, then open a pull request that closes #4774.

You're in your own git worktree, on a fresh branch made for this task. Commit there, push it, and open the pull request from it.
codeSplitter git: missing notes, line endings, forced pushes to the desktop remote, a dangling commit (4 items)
Moved from #4333 (audit 2026-11-12, at `72281fae`). Each item says what you do and what comes back.

- [ ] **No git note for a commit that carries an agent's line when no run is on record** (the line was written through the API): `GET …/commits/:sha/note` is `{note: null}`.
- [ ] **A first commit changes line endings.** A file with no final newline gains one and a UTF-8 BOM is dropped (git numstat `+2 -2` for a one-line edit). `pushCatalogues` in `src/archive.ts` always adds a final newline, and the file's doc remembers neither; it needs to keep both from the file it was read from.
- [ ] **The desktop's push-back remote accepts a forced push:** git's main is rewritten while the app's lines keep the old text.
- [ ] **A fresh start leaves one dangling staging commit** in the new git (`git fsck`: "dangling commit"). Harmless.

codeSplitter git: notes without a run, line endings kept, no forced pushes to the desktop remote, no dangling staging commit
Closes #4774

All four items:

- **Note without a run on record.** `commitNote` (`src/why.ts`) gave up when none of the agents in a commit had a run on the file. Now each such agent gets a short block, `agent: <name>` / `run: none on record`, so `GET …/commits/:sha/note` isn't `{note: null}`.
- **Line endings.** `asGit` / `endsOf` / `endsAt` in `src/archive.ts` take the UTF-8 BOM and the final newline (or the lack of one) from the file's last git copy. The doc doesn't need to remember either, because git already does. A one-line edit is now `+1 -1`. This applies wherever app lines become git t

title: cli test: pin the package manager in the deploy guardrail test (Closes #4809)
text:
Builder: cli 'deploy guardrail' test fails there, expects `rustybuns plan` but gets `npx rustybuns plan`
On the builder Mac, `bun run builder run packages/cli bun test test/glue.test.ts -t "deploy guardrail"` fails at `packages/cli/test/glue.test.ts:189`:

```
Expected to contain: "`rustybuns plan --stage staging`"
Received: "✗ [DeployRefused] no plan on record for this config. Run `npx rustybuns plan --stage staging` first ..."
```

It passes in GitHub CI (the `packages` job). The likely cause: the builder's environment makes package-manager detection pick npm (an `npm_config_user_agent`, or a lockfile it sees), so `execCmd` adds `npx`. The fix is either to pin the user agent in that test, as `init.test.ts` does with `npm_config_user_agent: ""`, or to clear it in `remote-ci.ts`. I found this while working on #4791.
cli test: pin the package manager in the deploy guardrail test (Closes #4809)
The deploy guardrail test's temp app has no lockfile, so the refusal hint names the command the way the shell's user agent says to run it (`npx` on the builder, see #4809). The test now pins `npm_config_user_agent: bun/1` and expects `bunx rustybuns plan --stage staging`. Passes on the builder.

Closes #4809
