title: init: a Nitro preset inside a conditional spread is not the build's preset (Closes #4107)
text:
init: a Nitro preset inside a conditional spread reads as the build's preset
Found in the #2167 research (notes/tanstack-start-top-ten.md). josephmqiu/game-theory-model's vite config:

```ts
nitro({ serverDir: "./server", ...(isElectronBuild ? { preset: "node-server" } : {}) })
```

`startLayout` (`packages/cli/src/glue/start-layout.ts`) matches `preset: "node-server"` with a regex, so `init` warns the preset starts its own server and drops `NITRO_PRESET=standard`, though the normal build sets no preset. Without the variable Nitro's default (node-server) builds a server the desktop can't mount.

Fix idea: only take a preset that is a direct property of the `nitro({...})` call (not inside `...(` / `?`), else treat it as unset; one table row in the start-layout test.

Part of #2167.

Part of #4849. Follow-up to #4859.

The park (`apps/load-in/src/venues/park.ts`) scores spill at the houses' property line with free-field coverage only. The plan (#4859) also has wind moving the highs: a breeze toward the road carries the mids and highs further (a few dB at 40 m), a breeze away cuts them. - `env.ts:5` `Row`: a table row, or an entity's fields before `validate` check

- **Tape echo**: Jiles-Atherton hysteresis on record (as in Chowdhury's real-time tape model, 2019), playback gap and spacing loss, wow and flutter, a speed knob with motor inertia (pitch glide), several heads at fixed spacing, feedback through the record amp's circuit so a runaway saturates.

Start with spring reverb (its driver and recovery are tube circuits we already solve), then tape. Lives in the amp's effects loop from #4827.

- **OTA**: current-controlled gain

Q Amp: an expression pedal or MIDI CC moves the wah's treadle
Left from #4828 (PR #4945). Q Wah's treadle is the pedal's one knob, and each turn rebuilds the link (a new pot value). Rocking it from an expression pedal or a MIDI CC needs something cheaper: drive the wah from `wah("foot")` (a `VarR` on control `foot`, as Q Envelope does) and set that control from the input, so the circuit isn't rebuilt. Web MIDI CC 11 (expression) or a chosen CC; on a page with no MIDI, drag the treadle.

Test: a CC sweep from 0 to 127 moves the wah's peak from the heel (~570 Hz) to the toe (~1.8 kHz) and never rebuilds the circuit.
Q Amp: an expression pedal or MIDI CC rocks the wah's treadle, a pot turn and never a new circuit (Closes #4947)
Closes #4947.

Q Wah's treadle used to rebuild the pedal's circuit on every turn. Now it is a real pot, so rocking it from an expression pedal costs next to nothing.

- **The treadle is a `Pot`** (`effects.ts`): 100 Ω plus a 220k rheostat, with the same heel-to-toe curve as before. A pot glides over about 10 ms, so a 7-bit CC doesn't zipper, and the Rust solver already has `Pot`. I used this instead of the `VarR` the issue sketched. Q Envelope keeps its `VarR` on `foot`.

Part of #5029 (step 7: the crowd is part of the sound). Starts with the dive bar.

## What it does

When the doors open, ninety people come in and pack against the stage. They change the sound in the ways a real crowd does:

- **Bodies take the highs.** Sound that passes under head height loses mids and highs: about 10 dB per 10 m at 4 kHz through a packed crowd, and next to nothing in the bass. Tops on stands at 1.2 m fire straight through every row. Raised to 2 m, they clear the heads and only graze the last few rows.

Save states, step 2: a round-trip check on Mythic duels, then rewind on Two Fronts
Follow-up to #4686. Two Fronts passed the round-trip check (save mid-fight, load, step on, same state as stepping straight through). The contract is in `@rustybuns/util/lab/save-state` (`save`, `load`, `firstDiff`, `roundTrip`).

Next, one at a time:

1. **Mythic Masters duels:** run `roundTrip` on a duel sim the same way `apps/two-fronts/test/save-state.test.ts` does. Report the first path that differs, if any. A duel is the game that needs rollback most.
2. **Rewind and replays on top of it:** a ring buffer of `save` bytes, one every N frames, plus the inputs between them. Two Fronts already records inputs (`src/battle/replay.ts`), so rewind there is: load the nearest save, then replay the logged inputs.
3. **Rollback netplay:** only once a duel round-trips and one save plus a re-step fits inside a frame. Measure that time first. Qollab rooms stay server-authoritative until then.

What the check showed so far: the Two Fronts state is plain JSON. Its random stream is `seed` on the battle (`nextRandom`), and nothing in it relies on shared references or `"k" in o`. A sim whose dice live outside its state fails the check, and the test shows that.

Mythic Masters: the opening, in an order that explains (title, tape, Book, witch, world)
The owner: "The intro is like non sensical we need to explain and clearly lay out more and two to three times explaining a thing". Walked through a fresh New game on 2026-11-15. Here is what a new player sees, in order, and where it breaks.

**Today's order**

title: Q Amp: time the Rust solver per sample; a pedal doesn't fit a Cortex-M7 as it is (Closes #4938)
text:
Work on GitHub issue #4938: "Q Amp: does a pedal fit on a DSP dev board? Time the Rust solver per sample".

Read it first with `gh issue view 4938 --comments`. Create a new branch, implement the change, verify it, then open a pull request that closes #4938.

You're in your own git worktree, on a fresh branch made for this task. Commit there, push it, and open the pull request from it.
Q Amp: does a pedal fit on a DSP dev board? Time the Rust solver per sample
Follow-up from the spike #4832 (ANALOG.md section 8). Lane: future idea.

The spike measured the TypeScript solver on Q Drive: about 1.2 µs per sample on one M1 Pro core (17× real time at 48 kHz; the rigs run 4× oversampled, so 192 kHz, about 5× real time). A Cortex-M7 at 480 MHz (the usual audio dev board) has about 10,000 cycles per sample at 48 kHz and 2,500 at 192 kHz. The estimate from that: Q Drive at 48 kHz might just fit on the M7 as Rust, but 4× oversampled it probably doesn't, and a 4-tube amp doesn't. A Cortex-A board (a Pi-class SBC with an audio codec hat) has room.

That is an estimate. To get a number:
1. Build the Rust solver (`native/`, `circuit.rs`) for the host on Bob and time Q Drive per sample: native Rust against the TS figure above.
2. Count the Newton iterations per sample for each pedal (that's the real cost driver, since the diodes clip).
3. If it looks close, build for `thumbv7em-none-eabihf` and run it on an M7 board, or in a cycle-counting emulator, at 48 kHz with 1× and 2× oversampling.
4. Write the result into ANALOG.md section 8 (a pedal on an M7: yes, no, or only at 1×).

Hardware purchases are the owner's call.

Q Amp: time the Rust solver per sample; a pedal doesn't fit a Cortex-M7 as it is (Closes #4938)
Closes #4938.

**The answer: a pedal doesn't fit a 480 MHz Cortex-M7 as the solver is now, even at 1×. A Cortex-A board fits one pedal, even at 4×.**

text:
Work on GitHub issue #4948: "Q Amp: split an over-budget pedalboard across worker threads (SharedArrayBuffer ring)".

Read it first with `gh issue view 4948 --comments`. Create a new branch, implement the change, verify it, then open a pull request that closes #4948.

Q Amp: split an over-budget pedalboard across worker threads (SharedArrayBuffer ring)
Step 2 of #4827's budget, left over once the pedalboard landed.

Q Amp's board (`apps/fm-daw/src/amp/board.ts`) runs the whole chain on the audio thread. Measured in Bun on the 16 GB office Mac, 128-sample blocks, the riff:

| Board | × real time |
|---|---|
| Q Lead 50 alone, 4× | 2.1 |
| Q Drive into it | 1.4 |
| Q Drive, Q Fuzz, the amp, Q Space in the loop, 4× | 0.9 (over budget: the page drops to Eco by itself) |
| the same at Eco (2×) | 1.6 |
| Q Space in front (the amp runs once a side), 4× | 0.7 |

So a full board at 4× does not fit on one thread. The plan from ANALOG.md section 2:

- Only when one thread is over budget, split the chain at a slot boundary and run the tail on a worker, handed blocks through a `SharedArrayBuffer` ring: one audio block (2.7 ms at 48 kHz) of extra latency per hop.
- `SharedArrayBuffer` needs cross-origin isolation (COOP and COEP headers) on `/amp.html`, in dev and on the deployed page.
- The per-slot loads the board already reports (`qamp.state().board[i].load`) are what to split by.
- Show the hop on the board (where the split is, and the latency it adds).

Test: the journey in `test/amp.test.ts` with a board over budget, the split on, output 
Q Amp: split an over-budget rig across worker threads through a SharedArrayBuffer ring (Closes #4948)
Closes #4948. Leaves #5114 open (the live listen, a MANUAL RUN).

**What it does, in plain words:** when a big pedalboard needs more of the audio thread than it has, the page cuts the chain in two or three. The audio thread plays the first pedals, worker threads play the rest, and they hand blocks to each other through shared memory. Each hand-off adds one block of delay (2.7 ms at 48 kHz). Apart from that delay, the sound is exactly the same.

- **gear `Rig`** (`packages/gear/src/circuit/rig.ts`): `splitRig(spec, cuts)` cuts a rig at slot boundaries (`cutPoints`, never inside a split's sides)

Q Amp: a pedalboard, slots in any order, effects loop, stereo, load per slot
Lane 2 of the analog map (`apps/fm-daw/ANALOG.md`, section 2). Q Amp has one pedal slot. Make it a board:

- Slots in any order, drag to reorder, a footswitch each.
- An effects loop on the amp: time effects after the preamp, before the power stage.
- Mono until the first stereo effect, stereo after.
- A load share on each slot, so a player sees what costs what.

Budget (CIRCUITS.md "Speed"): pedal 5 to 6x real time, 4-tube amp 2.3 to 3.3x, so a full board won't fit at 4x oversampling on one thread. In order:
1. Oversample only links that clip; linear ones (tone stacks, phasers) at 1x.
2. Split the chain over worker threads with a `SharedArrayBuffer` ring, one block of latency per hop, only when one thread is over budget.

`qamp.state()` reports the chain and each slot's load. Test: one journey through `src/amp/live.ts` that reorders two pedals while the riff plays, output bounded, no Newton misses.

title: Q Amp solver: sparse Jacobian and a Newton cap per sample, measured for a Cortex-M7
text:
Work on GitHub issue #5109: "Q Amp: make the Rust solver fit a Cortex-M7 (sparse Jacobian, iteration cap, f32, no_std)".

Read it first with `gh issue view 5109 --comments`. Create a new branch, implement the change, verify it, then open a pull request that closes #5109.

Q Amp: make the Rust solver fit a Cortex-M7 (sparse Jacobian, iteration cap, f32, no_std)
Follow-up from #4938 (ANALOG.md section 8, "A pedal on a DSP chip, timed"). Lane: future idea.

`bun scripts/pedal-bench.ts` timed the Rust solver on the builder (M1 Max): Q Drive takes about 800 ns per sample, roughly 2,500 host cycles, with 4.6 Newton iterations per sample on average and up to 18 on a hard-clipped sample. A 480 MHz Cortex-M7 has 10,000 cycles per sample at 48 kHz. The same f64 code on an M7 (about one instruction per cycle, no hardware `exp`, slower f64) likely needs 3 to 6 times the M1's cycles, so it doesn't fit as it is, even at 1×. Making it fit is a solver job first, a board second:

1. Count the cost: the Newton loop builds the port Jacobian as a dense `kk × kk × kk` product even when most of `j` is zero. Precompute the sparsity, or build it once per iteration from the nonzero ports only.
2. Cap the iterations per sample (say 6) and carry the rest to the next sample; measure the error against the uncapped solve on the riff.
3. An f32 build of `circuit.rs` (the M7's single-precision FPU is about twice as fast as its f64 unit) and how far it drifts from f64.
4. A `no_std` + `libm` build for `thumbv7em-none-eabihf`, and a cycle count on a board (DWT cycle coun

Closes #5109. Steps 1 and 2 are here. Steps 3 and 4 (f32, `no_std`, a board's cycle count) moved up to #5150.

**What changed**

- **Sparse Jacobian** (`circuit.rs`): `Circuit::new` records where `currents` writes the ports' Jacobian, and the Newton loop (building `I + H J`, then the final current update) multiplies only those entries. Each entry adds its terms in the same order as before, so the output is the same to the bit. 48 kHz on the builder: Q Drive 840 to 695 ns per sample, Q Dist 880 to 750, Q Fuzz 1,780 to 1,250. Q Germ barely moves.

Office workers freeze (stopped, state T) and the reaper never ends stopped orphans; swap fills
Workers in the office hang for hours. Two separate faults cause it. Both were seen on the office Mac (16 GB) on 2026-11-18.

## 1. Live workers get frozen and nothing resumes them

The office's `claude` processes stop with state `T` (a suspend signal, like SIGTSTP or SIGSTOP). Their parent is the running office's pty host. Nothing sends `SIGCONT`, so to the owner the worker looks hung.

- PIDs 91224 and 75988 were stopped for 8 and 37 minutes. Both sat in the repo root.
- PIDs 99013 and 99437 were stopped for about 2.5 h, along with their `bun office-workers.js mcp` and `caffeinate` children. `kill -CONT` brought them back at once.

Still to find: what sends the stop. Candidates are the pty shim (`apps/agent-office/shim/node-pty/`), a ctrl+z byte written into a worker's terminal, or a job-control signal when the pty loses its controlling terminal.

**Goal:** load a player's own VST3 / CLAP / AU plugin inside the FM DAW desktop app, so a jam's track can be played by it and everyone in the sesh hears it.

4. Others in the sesh hear it: the host's output goes on the live line as audio (Opus over the room socket or WebRTC), since their machines don't have the plugin.
5. The plugin's own editor window opens as a native window beside the webview.

Qlave already gets Cloudflare TURN for its voice rooms. Options:
- The World hands out short-lived Cloudflare TURN credentials with the sesh (a Worker call to the TURN key API, priced per GB relayed; price it first). A guitar at 128 kb/s is about 58 MB an hour per listener.
- Or carry the guitar on Qlave's room, once a sesh can get a Qlave ticket (eqosys mints them for spaces today, `apps/eqosys/QLAVE.md`).

Until then, the status line says the guitar couldn't get through once a call fails.

Part of #4900.

Qollab Studio guitar line: a TURN relay pass from GET /ice for players behind strict networks (Closes #5187)

Follows #5118. On Bob, `brit --short` gets 11 of 13 parts back from three takes. V1 cc comes back at 0.013u (true value 0.022u). V2 cc doesn't change the sound enough to measure, so it can't be fit. `--tone-only` gets 13 of 13 back.

Q Amp profiling: V1 and V2 coupling caps walk their valley together, brit 13 of 13 (Closes #5162)
Closes #5162.

**Why V1 cc missed.** V1's and V2's coupling caps are two high-pass filters in a row, and they sound alike wherever their corners add up the same. The full fit settled on V1 cc 0.013u with V2 cc 0.068u, which scores 0.0011 (the true pair scores 0). Stepping either cap alone only makes the score worse. V2 cc wasn't really "can't hear": at 0.068u its own corner is low, but it is trading off against V1 cc.

**Goal:** server print files for originals over 12 MP. A 24 MP phone photo is the default on recent iPhones.

No sheet needs more than about 17 MP (a 30 x 40 cm tee front at 300 dpi is 3543 x 4724).

Cheapest idea: when the widget uploads, it also uploads a print copy capped at the largest zone it could print on, as a PNG. It already decodes the full photo with `createImageBitmap` (`src/widget/image.ts`). The server would print from that copy, and the original stays as uploaded.

Other ways, if that one is no good:
- measure peak memory on the live Worker and raise `PRINT_MAX_PX` (`src/print-render.ts`)
- downscale with the Cloudflare Images binding first (paid: price it in the PR)

title: hippo-tycoon lan.test: wait for the snap that shows the guest's input (Closes #5070)
text:
Work on GitHub issue #5070: "hippo-tycoon lan.test: guest input check races the snap count on a loaded runner".

Read it first with `gh issue view 5070 --comments`. Create a new branch, implement the change, verify it, then open a pull request that closes #5070.

You're in your own git worktree, on a fresh branch made for this task. Commit there, push it, and open the pull request from it.
hippo-tycoon lan.test: guest input check races the snap count on a loaded runner
`apps/hippo-tycoon/test/lan.test.ts:108` (`LAN party: host and guests share one ticking world`) failed once in CI on PR #5063. That PR doesn't touch hippo-tycoon; the test ran because `packages/` changed.

```
expect(last.hp[1]![0]).toBeGreaterThan(0)   // guest one slid right: input crossed the LAN
Expected: > 0
Received: 0
(fail) ... [5747.24ms]
```

The test sends one `in` message and then waits for 30 snaps. It does not wait for a snap that shows the input. On a loaded runner, 30 snaps can arrive before the input is applied. Fix: wait with `g1.until(() => (g1.of("snap").at(-1)?.hp[1]?.[0] ?? 0) > 0)`, the same way the couch-partner check below it already waits.

hippo-tycoon lan.test: wait for the snap that shows the guest's input (Closes #5070)
Closes #5070

`apps/hippo-tycoon/test/lan.test.ts` sent one guest input, waited for 30 snaps, then checked the last snap for the move. On a loaded runner 30 snaps can arrive before the host applies the input, so the check read `0` (seen once on #5063).

The test now waits for a snap that shows the guest moved right, the same way the couch-partner check below it waits. The 30-snap wait stays, because the send-rate check needs it.

Test only: no app code changed.

RustyBuns is a developer tool and workflow designed to package a web application into a native binary and deployable server.

Core Concept

title: fm-daw: fix the two Windows test failures (CLAP folder separators, Q Drive kit lookup)
text:
Work on GitHub issue #5409: "fm-daw: two tests fail on Windows (CLAP folder separators, Q Drive kit lookup)".

Read it first with `gh issue view 5409 --comments`. Create a new branch, implement the change, verify it, then open a pull request that closes #5409.

You're in your own git worktree, on a fresh branch made for this task. Commit there, push it, and open the pull request from it.
fm-daw: two tests fail on Windows (CLAP folder separators, Q Drive kit lookup)
Two fm-daw tests fail on Windows runners: both `windows-x64` and `windows-arm64` in the `desktop-drop` dry run. These failures are already on main. They showed up on #5406 because that PR edits `scripts/ci-apps.ts`, which runs every app's Windows dry run. They aren't required checks, so they don't block merges.

Job log: https://github.com/QuinnsCode/RustyBuns/actions/runs/44833296357/job/136623659165

1. `test/clap-host.test.ts:134`, "plugin folders follow the CLAP spec per OS, CLAP_PATH first": the mac folder comes back as `\Users\q\Library\Audio\Plug-Ins\CLAP`. The code builds the path with the host's `path.join` and not the target OS's separator (use `path.posix` for mac/linux targets).
2. `test/kit.test.ts:37`, "look at Q Drive on the pedal wall, open its build sheet with your swap, and download the kit": gets `made: false` with empty `parts`/`layers`. The kit folder lookup most likely misses on Windows paths (separator or a `/`-split).

fm-daw: fix the two Windows test failures (CLAP folder separators, Q Drive kit lookup)
Closes #5409.

- `pluginFolders` built every OS's folders with the host's `path.join`, so on a Windows runner the mac folder came back as `\Users\q\Library\...`. It now joins with `path.posix` for mac/linux and `path.win32` for Windows, whatever the host is.
- The kit test read `circuits/q-drive/` with Bun's `Glob.scan`, which gives `gerbers\top.gtl` on Windows, so `isKit` found no `gerbers/` layers and the sheet came back `made: false`. The page reads the same folder through Vite's `import.meta.glob`, which always uses `/`, so only the test's disk reader was wrong: it now turns `\` into `/`.

Mythic Masters: "Too strong to bind yet" stays on screen after the creature is worn down
Found by the rules judge on the levels climb (#5382), in the running game through the probe.

**What happens.** In a wild fight, press the bind key once while the creature is still over 45% health. The note "Too strong to bind yet: wear it under 45%." comes up, as it should. It then stays on screen for the rest of the fight: at 40% health and at 5% health it still reads "Too strong to bind yet", beside the live odds ("bind 88%"). A new player who pressed the key early never sees "Bind it now, before it drops".

**Why.** `bindNote` in `apps/mythic-masters/src/main.ts` is set by the early press (about line 1421) and only cleared at the start of a fight or by the next press (about lines 1408 and 1593).

**Fix.** Clear the note (or swap it for the "bind it now" line) once the creature's health is under `bindBelow`. One journey test: press early, wear it down, and the note no longer says it is too strong.

Mythic Masters: the too-strong bind note gives way once the beast is worn down (Closes #5386)
Closes #5386.

**What was wrong.** Pressing bind while a wild beast was still over the line set "Too strong to bind yet: wear it under 45%." and nothing cleared it, so the note stayed for the rest of the fight, beside odds like "bind 66%". A player who pressed early never saw "Bind it now, before it drops".

**Fix.** The too-strong note is one function (`tooStrong`), used by both the solo and the co-op press. The bind prompt (`bindView`) drops that note as soon as the odds are above zero, so the normal "Bind it now" call shows. Other notes ("It tore free", "The Book holds ...") stay as before.

title: Releases page job: its checkout catches up to origin/main (Closes #5428)
text:
Work on GitHub issue #5428: "Releases page job: its checkout never moves to a newer main".

Read it first with `gh issue view 5428 --comments`. Create a new branch, implement the change, verify it, then open a pull request that closes #5428.

You're in your own git worktree, on a fresh branch made for this task. Commit there, push it, and open the pull request from it.
Releases page job: its checkout never moves to a newer main
The hourly job (`bun run releases --install`, launchd `com.rustybuns.releases`) runs `scripts/releases.ts` from the checkout that installed it. An agent's worktree is deleted when the worker goes home, so on 2026-11-20 it was installed from a detached worktree at `~/.rustybuns/releases/rustybuns` (origin/main a5c997cc6, plus #5418's one-line Pacific-time fix applied by hand).

That checkout stays on that commit. Code changes to the page never reach the job, and the scan reads that tree's app list.

Fix: `--publish` first moves its own checkout to `origin/main` (`git fetch`, then `git checkout --detach origin/main`, then `bun install --frozen-lockfile` if the lockfile moved). Or `--install` refuses to run from `.agent-office/worktrees/` and makes that checkout itself.
Releases page job: its checkout catches up to origin/main (Closes #5428)
The hourly releases job ran from whatever commit it was installed from, so page fixes and new apps never reached it.

- `catchUp(repo)` in `scripts/launchd.ts`: for a detached, clean checkout, fetch `origin main`, `checkout --detach` onto it, and `bun install --frozen-lockfile` when `bun.lock` moved. A checkout on a branch or with changes is left alone.
- `--publish` calls it first. If it moved, it runs itself again once (`RELEASES_CAUGHT_UP`) so the new code builds the page.
- `--install` from `.agent-office/worktrees/` makes (or catches up) a detached worktree at `~/.rustybuns/releases/rusty

The plan for getting Rusty Buns apps onto Steam and the iOS App Store (iPhone and iPad), decided with the owner 2026-10-30. Full record: notes/STORES.md (branch office/sprocket-083a until its PR merges).

**Shape:** one pure Rust core per app (wasm for web and edge, cdylib for desktop, staticlib + UniFFI xcframework for iOS), with a renderer per platform: three.js on web and Steam, SwiftUI + RealityKit on iOS.

**Order**
- iOS: Park Hide & Seek, then Hippo Tycoon, then qCRM. Native SwiftUI, online only, edge first; more moves onto the phone later.
- Steam: Hippo Tycoon is the pilot, in a bundled-Chromium window (Electron or Electrobun with CEF) so Steam Deck gets real WebGL.

**Releases:** one version per app across every store. `<app>-vX.Y.Z-beta.N` goes to TestFlight and the Steam beta branch; `<app>-vX.Y.Z` goes to App Store review and the Steam default branch. Betas any time, a stable train monthly per app. Store builds run in GitHub CI behind the `drops` approval.

text:
Work on GitHub issue #5500: "codeSplitter over ssh://: spike on Workers inbound TCP (local first)".

Read it first with `gh issue view 5500 --comments`. Create a new branch, implement the change, verify it, then open a pull request that closes #5500.

You're in your own git worktree, on a fresh branch made for this task. Commit there, push it, and open the pull request from it.
codeSplitter over ssh://: spike on Workers inbound TCP (local first)
Cloudflare shipped inbound TCP to Workers in public beta on 2026-11-19. Notes are in `notes/INBOUND_TCP_GRPC.md` (#5499).

**Goal:** `git clone ssh://git@<host>/<owner>/<repo>` and `git push` against codeSplitter with your own SSH key, and every push lands in Artifacts the same way an HTTP push does.

**Shape:** a Spectrum app (one port, `traffic_type: worker`) goes to codeSplitter's Worker `connect()`, then a Durable Object per repo, then a small container (`sshd` + `git-shell`, or a TS SSH server). SSH brings its own encryption, so Spectrum's lack of edge TLS on Pro doesn't matter.

CI: checkout takes ~35 s in every app test lane; try a sparse checkout
Follow-up to #5492 (PR #5503).

In every `test <app> n/3` lane, `actions/checkout` takes about 35 s, and this is already a depth-1 checkout (`.github/workflows/apps.yml`, the matrix job). text:
Work on GitHub issue #5505: "codeSplitter ssh://: pushes over ssh land in Artifacts like HTTP pushes".

Read it first with `gh issue view 5505 --comments`. Create a new branch, implement the change, verify it, then open a pull request that closes #5505.

codeSplitter ssh://: pushes over ssh land in Artifacts like HTTP pushes
Follows the ssh:// spike (#5500, `apps/codesplitter/ssh/`). In the spike, pushes land in a bare repo in the gate container's `/srv/git`, which is lost when the container sleeps.

**Goal:** a push over `ssh://` lands in the repo's Artifacts remote the same way an HTTP push does, so checks, agents and the feed see it. A fetch reads from there too.

- The spike found that the Worker can't route per repo, because SSH is encrypted until sshd. So the gate container stays a stateless bridge: `git-serve.sh` maps `owner/repo` to codeSplitter's smart-HTTP remote, using the user from the key lookup.
- Simplest bridge to try first: a scratch bare repo per connection. Fetch from the HTTP remote, run `git-receive-pack` locally, then push on over HTTP with the user's token, and send the HTTP push's rejections (protected branch, checks) back on stderr. Then measure it against a true stream proxy.
- The container needs internet (or a binding back to the Worker) for this. Today the spike starts it with `enableInternet: false`.
- Depends on #5504 (key auth) for the user.

2. fetches every ref into a scratch bare repo, then runs `git-upload-pack` / `git-receive-pack` on that.

Spike: Goose for small hot kernels (port hippo_fluid, load via bun:ffi)
**Question:** is [Goose](https://github.com/aardappel/goose) (a new memory-safe systems language: no GC, no heap allocator, no lifetime annotations; compiles to one C file; Apache 2.0) worth a place next to Rust for small hot kernels in RustyBuns?

- Goose emits a single C file. Bun can compile and load C at runtime with `cc()` from `bun:ffi` (TinyCC, the same backend Goose bundles). So a Goose kernel could load straight into a Bun script: no cargo, no `build:native`, no Bob.
- Agents may write it more easily than Rust (no lifetimes).

## Target: `hippo_fluid`

`apps/hippo-tycoon/native/crates/hippo_fluid/src/lib.rs` (177 lines) is the oil geyser's particle sim. It already has a C ABI (`fl_init`, `fl_step`, `fl_count`, `fl_out`), uses only f64 `+ - * / sqrt`, and has a TypeScript twin (`src/client/render/fluid.ts`) that agrees bit for bit. That twin is the oracle.

## Steps

1. Install Goose locally (scratch dir, not the repo). Note how it installs and its version.
2. Port `hippo_fluid` to Goose with the same four exports.
3. `goose` -> C, then load it with `bun:ffi` `cc()` in a t

text:

Read it first with `gh issue view 5504 --comments`. Create a new branch, implement the change, verify it, then open a pull request that closes #5504.

codeSplitter ssh://: SSH keys for codeSplitter users (key store + AuthorizedKeysCommand)
Follows the ssh:// spike (#5500, `apps/codesplitter/ssh/`). That spike lets in one key passed as `AUTHORIZED_KEY`.

**Goal:** any codeSplitter user can add an SSH public key, and `git` over `ssh://` lets that key in as that user.

- Key store: decide where keys live (a `ssh_keys` table in D1 next to `deploy-keys.ts`'s rows is the obvious one) and add a page or API to add and remove a key.
- Lookup: `sshd`'s `AuthorizedKeysCommand` in the container asks codeSplitter over HTTP who owns the offered key (fingerprint in, user out). The reply has one guard that both sides import. The container keeps no key list.
- The forced command gets the user (for example, `command="/git-serve.sh <user>"` in the lookup's reply) so the next step can push as them.
- Test: `ssh/try.ts` adds a key through the API and pushes with it, and a key nobody added is refused.

Agent Office, the desktop shell and many workers on one Mac run many Bun processes, and our single-binary installs ship Bun binaries.

- `new Function` / `eval` (`packages/cli/src/glue/port-vite.ts:69`, `packages/shell-bun` tests): AOT may fall back to the interpreter or fail.

- A brand-new compiler may have correctness bugs in its first releases.

1. Wait for the first AOT release to settle.
2. Build the Agent Office binary both ways.
3. Compare memory and CPU with `mem_stats`.
4. Run the existing journey tests against the AOT build.
5. If they pass, switch. If not, file an issue with the numbers.

No code changes yet.

**Code mode (`packages/util/src/codemode.ts`):**

Agents open hundreds of PRs a week, so not every PR should wait the full soak (3 green hours, 3 green nights, Monday). Each PR gets a score from facts we already measure, and the score picks its lane. The checks stay the same in every lane; only the waiting changes.

- What it touches: one app +30, a few apps +15, `packages/` or the lockfile 0, CI, deploy or secrets wiring -25

probe: --js rejects statements, though its help says it is an async function body
`bun scripts/probe.ts --help` says: "The expression is the body of an async function: `await` works, and its last expression is the answer", with the example `golf.aim(90, 0.8); golf.throw(); await new Promise(...); golf.state()`.

In practice (2026-11-21, `bun run probe sharesplat "/?demo=1" --js ...`):

- `(async () => { ...; return x })()` prints `undefined`

Only a single expression works, for example `shareSplat.clean().then(c => ...)`. Either make `--js` the async body the help describes, or change the help and the examples.
probe: --js runs as a real async function body, statements and all (Closes #5560)
Problem: `bun run probe <app> --js` put the whole text inside `return (...)`. So `const x = ...; x` and `a = ...; await ...; b` failed as syntax errors. Also, any text that held `return ` (an async IIFE) ran with no return and printed `undefined`.

Fix: `asyncBody` cuts the text at the last top-level `;` (one outside strings, comments and brackets) and returns the last expression. An explicit `return`, or a statement at the end, stays as written. The help line now says that statements work.

title: Qollab Studio web plugins: an Insert effect in the bounce, with pan and send, on web plugin tracks too (Closes #5551)
text:
Work on GitHub issue #5551: "Qollab Studio web plugins: an Insert effect in the bounce, with pan and send, on plugin tracks too".

Read it first with `gh issue view 5551 --comments`. Create a new branch, implement the change, verify it, then open a pull request that closes #5551.

You're in your own git worktree, on a fresh branch made for this task. Commit there, push it, and open the pull request from it.
Qollab Studio web plugins: an Insert effect in the bounce, with pan and send, on plugin tracks too
Part of Qollab Studio's plugins (#4899, group #4904). Follows #5359, which put a Web Audio Module effect in an FM track's **Insert** (`apps/fm-daw/src/ui/wam.ts`, the worklet's second output in `src/engine/worklet.ts`). What that first cut leaves out:

- **The bounce goes dry.** `bouncePlugins` renders web instruments on an offline context (#5360), but an inserted track is rendered by the engine with no effect. One way: render the track's tap offline, then run it through a copy of the effect on the same `OfflineRig`.
- **Pan and the Space send are lost on an inserted track.** It leaves the sum through the engine's tap, which is mono and skips the send (as an amp's does). The return could be panned by the track's PAN, and a send taken after the effect.
- **Only FM tracks have an Insert.** A plugin track (a web instrument) could chain its node into the effect before its fader; an amped track keeps its amp and the insert gets silence.

Test: extend `apps/fm-daw/scripts/web-plugin-check.ts` (Gain at 0.5 in a bounce halves it).

Qollab Studio web plugins: an Insert effect in the bounce, with pan and send, on web plugin tracks too (Closes #5551)
Closes #5551. Part of #4904.

**What it does, in plain words.** A web effect in a track's Insert (#5359) now works in three more places:

- **Pan and the Space send work.** The effect's sound comes back into the engine on its own input. The engine pans it with the track's PAN and sends it to Space with the track's SEND, after the effect. Before this, it came back mono and skipped the send.
- **The bounce has the effect in it.** The bounce renders each FM track that has an Insert on its own. Then it runs that sound through a copy of the effect offline and mixes the result back in (two passes).

text:

FM DAW: the drum grid shows a free note where it is, not on its nearest step
Moved out of #5591 (what #5578 left open).

**What a user sees:** a note on a drum track can sit anywhere in time, because a note's start and length are any number of beats: recorded with Quantize input off, imported from a MIDI file, or moved in the roll. The drum grid still draws steps, so it shows that note on its nearest step. Editing the step moves the note onto the grid, and the piano roll is the only place to edit a drum note freely.

**What to build:** the drum grid shows a free hit where it is: an offset mark inside its step, or striped as recorded hits are today until quantized. Clicking it doesn't snap it to the step unless the user asks (the Snap magnet, as in the roll). One journey test: record a hit off the grid, see it off the step, toggle it without moving it.

- Shift-click accents the hits in a step and leaves them where they are. A plain click clears the step.

**What a user sees:** on FM DAW's Shape tab, only the master's Shape draws a live spectrum. A track's, a player's or a return's Shape says "curve only" (`src/ui/App.tsx`, `src/ui/DeskPanel.tsx`).

- Drop the "curve only" labels.

The walker (`bun run releases --rerelease`, scripts/releases.ts) deploys from `~/.rustybuns/releases/rustybuns`. Today that folder is a worktree of the agent-office clone (`~/agent-office/QuinnsCode/RustyBuns/.git`). The live apps' Alchemy state is shared through a different clone's git dir: `~/Documents/projects/RustyBuns/.git/rustybuns/alchemy`.

So from the walker's folder every app has empty state. On 2026-11-21 eqosys planned as FRESH (a second eqosys) and then failed on the qollab reference. #5584 makes the walker skip such apps, but skipped means they never get re-released.

- `jobCheckout` (scripts/launchd.ts) makes the walker's checkout as a worktree of the clone that holds the state, `~/Documents/projects/RustyBuns`, instead of the clone the script is run from.

- This adds a worktree entry to the owner's real checkout's `.git`. It changes nothing in their working tree, but the owner signs off before it ships.

From #2328, row 6. Read only: no adopting, and no change to codeSplitter's stack.

`@alchemy.run/git` (https://alchemy.run/git) is a git server on Workers, Durable Objects and R2. It has smart HTTP, pull requests with a server-side merge base, tree diffs, fast-forward and three-way merge, and a GitHub REST v3 facade that `gh` and Octokit can point at.

- Read its merge code next to codeSplitter's (the merges, `mirror.ts`, its GitHub-shaped API).
- Run the merge cases that codeSplitter's tests already cover through both.
- File one issue for each thing worth taking (most likely the GitHub facade's coverage, or a merge case it gets right and we get wrong). Then close this one with the list.

codeSplitter stays on Cloudflare Artifacts and keeps its own merge rules.

I read `@alchemy.run/git` 2.0.0-beta.87 (Apache-2.0, from npm). Mythic Masters: faction quest steps 4 and 5 are out of road order

    game: beat institute-5 needs institute-4, which is further down the road

title: codeSplitter ssh://: the Worker answers the gate's remote lookup (#5541)
text:
Work on GitHub issue #5541: "codeSplitter ssh://: the remote lookup in codeSplitter's Worker (repo + user -> Artifacts remote and token)".

Read it first with `gh issue view 5541 --comments`. Create a new branch, implement the change, verify it, then open a pull request that closes #5541.

You're in your own git worktree, on a fresh branch made for this task. Commit there, push it, and open the pull request from it.
codeSplitter ssh://: the remote lookup in codeSplitter's Worker (repo + user -> Artifacts remote and token)
Follows #5505. The ssh gate's \`git-serve.sh\` now bridges every connection to the repo's smart-HTTP remote. It asks \`LOOKUP_URL\` (Bearer \`GATE_SECRET\`) with \`user\`, \`repo\` and \`mode\` (\`read\` or \`write\`) and reads back two lines, the remote and a token. An error status's body is the reason the client sees. So far only \`apps/codesplitter/ssh/try.ts\`'s stand-in answers it.

**Goal:** codeSplitter's Worker answers the lookup for real.

- A route (for example \`GET /api/ssh/remote\`) that only the gate's secret opens (a varlock secret, never a shell export).
- \`access()\` decides: \`read\` needs read access, \`write\` needs write access. A private repo the user can't see answers "not found", like the API does.
- The remote and token come from \`handleFor\` + \`artifactAccess\` / \`handOut\`, with short tokens (minutes, not hours). That includes the crew remote when the user is crew, as \`GET /api/repos/:o/:r\` does.
- A push that lands there runs codeSplitter's usual after-push path (checks, agents, feed). Check that an Artifacts push made outside the app is seen, and if it isn't, have the lookup or the gate tell the Worker.
- The user comes from the key lookup (#5504)
codeSplitter ssh://: the Worker answers the gate's remote lookup (#5541)
Closes #5541.

codeSplitter's Worker now answers the ssh gate's lookup. Until now only the stand-in in `ssh/try.ts` answered it.

`GET /api/ssh/remote?user=&repo=owner/name&mode=read|write` (`src/ssh-remote.ts`):

- **Who can call it:** only callers with the gate's secret, `SSH_GATE_SECRET`. It's an optional varlock secret (`rustybuns.config.ts`, next to `DRAIN_SECRET`): without it the route answers 404, like the drain does. It sits before sign-in, so the gate's Bearer is never read as an API token.

title: Preflight's Merge after line can't be forgotten: the guard checks the PR body (closes #5344)
text:
Work on GitHub issue #5344: "Make preflight's "merge after #N" real: an after:#N label and a runner that merges main in once blockers land".

Read it first with `gh issue view 5344 --comments`. Create a new branch, implement the change, verify it, then open a pull request that closes #5344.

You're in your own git worktree, on a fresh branch made for this task. Commit there, push it, and open the pull request from it.
Make preflight's "merge after #N" real: an after:#N label and a runner that merges main in once blockers land
Split out of #4956 (third box there). The office now holds same-app tasks at hire and at seating, and `gh pr create` waits for `bun scripts/preflight.ts` on HEAD, but preflight still only reports: nothing acts on its "merge after #N".

## What's left

- Preflight labels the PR `after:#N` for each open PR it names (or writes it into the body in a fixed form a script can read).
- A runner (Ester, or the hourly ring) watches those PRs: once every blocker has merged, it merges `main` into the branch and pushes, or, on a `card`, tags the PR's worker or a person on a card.
- AGENTS.md's preflight line then says the runner does it, in place of "write merge after #N in the PR body".

## Why

On 2026-11-16, 18 PRs came back CONFLICTING (#4903-#4945). Holding tasks stops new pile-ups; this lands the ones that still overlap (a hire sent with `anyway`, a file move like #4928) in order without a person rebasing each by hand.

Preflight's Merge after line can't be forgotten: the guard checks the PR body (closes #5344)
#5494 built most of #5344. Preflight prints a `Merge after #N` line, and `scripts/after.ts` (`after.yml`) merges main into the branch once those PRs land. But the runner only acts on that line, and nothing made anyone paste it. If an agent forgot the line, its PR was never handled.

- **Preflight** now writes the PRs it named into its stamp (`<head> <code> 12,34`), next to the HEAD it read.

text:
Work on GitHub issue #5657: "Agent Office: 50 half-deleted worktree folders (no .git, not in the worktree list, ~400 MB each) that no sweep removes".

Read it first with `gh issue view 5657 --comments`. Create a new branch, implement the change, verify it, then open a pull request that closes #5657.

Agent Office: 50 half-deleted worktree folders (no .git, not in the worktree list, ~400 MB each) that no sweep removes
In the office's worktree folder, 50 of 172 folders are half-deleted. They have no `.git`, and `git worktree list` no longer names them. Each is a partial checkout of about 6,000 files, roughly 400 MB; 31 of them date from Nov 20 to 22 (for example `bolt-2fe0`).

Likely causes, seen in the code but not yet proven:
- The office exits 300 ms after `shutdown` (`cli.js` `stop`), even in the middle of a send-home.
- The `fs.rm` fallback in `remove()` (`worktrees.js:278`) fails while a process still writes there. Then `git worktree prune` drops git's record of the folder.
- #5549 raised only the `add` timeout to 5 minutes. `remove` keeps 60 s. The 5-minute `add` runs through `execFileSync`, which can block the office, reaper included, for up to 5 minutes.

The sweep never touches these folders. Because they still exist, the reaper counts their scratch folders as live too.

The fix:
1. Add a sweep rule for any folder in `.agent-office/worktrees` older than an hour that has no `.git` and is not in `git worktree list`. The rule ends the processes in it (`endIn`), then deletes it.
2. Give `remove` the same longer timeout as `add`, run asynchronously.
3. Finish a send-home that is in progress

Agent Office: reuse node_modules between workers (each hire writes and deletes ~250k files, feeding fseventsd to 27 GB)
On 2026-11-23, leftovers held the office Mac to three workers: swap was at 97%. macOS's file watcher, fseventsd, held 27 GB after 33 days up, and it was using half a CPU core.

The likeliest cause is the file churn from each worker. Every hire runs `bun install --frozen-lockfile` (`live/install.ts`, #3167). That writes an isolated `node_modules/.bun`, about 250,000 files in one worktree. Send-home then deletes them again, through `git worktree remove` or `sweepBuilt` (#4314, #5486). Each worker so makes about 500,000 file events, plus the 10,000-file checkout.

The smallest fix:
- On send-home, rename the worktree's `node_modules` into a pool keyed by a hash of `bun.lock`, under `.agent-office/`. Don't delete it.
- On hire, rename a matching one into the new worktree before `bun install --frozen-lockfile`, which then has next to nothing to do.
- Keep at most two pooled copies, and drop a copy when `bun.lock` changes.

One rename replaces about 250,000 create events and 250,000 delete events. The hire gets faster too.

Check: run fseventsd's memory (`top -l 1 -o mem -stats command,mem -n 3`) before and after a day of hires.

Agent Office reaper: old orphans in seated worktrees, workers without a worktree, multi-repo send-home, a Chrome without a watchdog, the box
These leftover processes are still missed after the reaper fix in the 2026-11-23 PR:
- `orphans()` in `live/reaper.ts` spares every process under pid 1 in a seated worktree. A dev server or watcher left by an earlier session of a long-running worker lives as long as that worker does. That earlier session may have crashed, or the office was stopped with Ctrl-C (`manager.js shutdown` kills only the claude process). Fix: end such a process once it is older than about 24 hours, which keeps a demo server that was left on purpose for a day.
- A worker with no worktree gets `endIn('')`, which ends nothing, so processes it started from the main checkout are never ended. A worker with several repos (`info.repos`) gets `endIn` on its first worktree only. Fix: call `endIn` on each repo worktree. For a worker with no worktree, end what its session started (its process group).
- `apps/delayed-reaction/scripts/render.ts:48` starts headless Chrome itself instead of through `scripts/chrome.ts`, so it has no `dieWith` watchdog. Fix: switch it to `scripts/chrome.ts`.

**More modules for the sound wall**, each a real board with fab files (`circuits/wall-<id>.tsx` on `wall-kit.tsx`, a panel in `wall-panels.ts`, a sim in `src/wall/sims.ts`), in this order:

1. **MIDI to CV:** the room's computer keys (and a MIDI keyboard) play the wall: pitch at 1 V an octave and a gate. On a real board, a small microcontroller and a DAC; in the sim, the keys straight to volts.
2. **A clock on the sesh's tempo:** a clock out (and Q Steps' clock in) at the sesh's BPM, so the wall plays in time with the band.
3. **Noise and sample and hold:** a reverse-biased transistor junction's noise, amplified; a sample-and-hold on a clock (a JFET or analog switch and a hold capacitor).
4. **A bucket-brigade delay:** the BBD machine already in `packages/gear/src/circuit/machines.ts` as a module, with its clock and compander on the board. BBD chips are hard to buy: check stock first.
5. **The transistor ladder low-pass** (US 3,475,623, expired): four stages of transistor pairs. The solver can play it, but it costs several times Q Filter (about 2.9 µs a sample now), so measure it before it goes on the wall.

title: init: an SSR app's server build under outDir stays out of the static Worker's assets
text:
Work on GitHub issue #5767: "init: an SSR app's server bundle under outDir is deployed as public assets (Foldkit, Rat Stack)".

Read it first with `gh issue view 5767 --comments`. Create a new branch, implement the change, verify it, then open a pull request that closes #5767.

You're in your own git worktree, on a fresh branch made for this task. Commit there, push it, and open the pull request from it.
init: an SSR app's server bundle under outDir is deployed as public assets (Foldkit, Rat Stack)
Found in the Rat Stack trial (#4803). The app is a Foldkit app with server rendering (`foldkit({ ssr: { serverEntry, clientEntry, build: { prerender } } })`). Its vite config puts the server build under `<outDir>/server`.

So the static Worker that `init` writes (`assets: "dist/web"`) would ship `dist/web/server/fetch.js` and `foldkit.build.json` as **public static files**, and the bundle would never run. The deployed site would be the prerendered HTML only: no server renderer for other paths, and no `/rpc`. The builder's listing showed `dist/web/server/{assets,fetch.js,foldkit.build.json}` after `plan --offline`.

Rat Stack itself is open source, so this one leaks nothing. But any SSR-under-outDir app would publish its server bundle the same way.

Fix: `init` reads `@foldkit/vite-plugin`'s `ssr` (or any `<outDir>/server`) and either
- leaves `server/` out of the assets (an `.assetsignore`, or an outDir split), or
- runs the server bundle as the Worker (`worker` mode, as it does for TanStack Start's `<outDir>/server/server.js`).

Test: an `init` fixture with that vite config, then check the asset list leaves out `server/`.

init: an SSR app's server build under outDir stays out of the static Worker's assets
Closes #5767

A Foldkit app with server rendering (`foldkit({ ssr: ... })`) writes its server build to `<outDir>/server`. The assets-only Worker that `init` writes would have shipped `server/fetch.js` and `foldkit.build.json` as public static files.

- `inferVite` now sets `serverInOut` when the config has Foldkit's `ssr`, or names `"<outDir>/server"` itself.
- For such an app, the web build ends by appending `server/` to `<assets>/.assetsignore`. This step runs after vite, because vite empties the outDir. Cloudflare, Alchemy (`Util/Ignore`) and the desktop's `stageAssets` all honour that file

text:
Work on GitHub issue #5749: "Sound wall: Q Keys' firmware (MIDI to CV and clock on the ATtiny1614)".

Read it first with `gh issue view 5749 --comments`. Create a new branch, implement the change, verify it, then open a pull request that closes #5749.

You're in your own git worktree, on a fresh branch made for this task. Commit there, push it, and open the pull request from it.
Sound wall: Q Keys' firmware (MIDI to CV and clock on the ATtiny1614)
Follows #5690. Q Keys (`apps/fm-daw/circuits/wall-keys.tsx`, the sound wall's MIDI to CV and clock) has an ATtiny1614 on its board, and the sim plays what its firmware should do (`Keys` in `apps/fm-daw/src/wall/sims.ts`), but there is no firmware yet.

**Write it:** MIDI in on USART0 (PB3, 31250 baud); the last key held as the pitch on the MCP4822's A channel (SPI: PA1 MOSI, PA3 SCK, PA4 CS; LDAC is tied low), C2 at 0 V and 1 mV a step for U5's gain of two; the velocity on channel B; the gate on PA6 while any key is held; the MIDI clock (24 a beat) divided by the Div knob (ADC on PB1, in thirds: quarters, eighths, sixteenths) to PA7, high for the first half of each. Programmed over UPDI on JP3.

It should build with avr-gcc or megaTinyCore in CI (no hardware needed), and the sim's `Keys` and the firmware should share one table of what they do, or a test that runs the same notes through both.

Sound wall: Q Keys' firmware, MIDI to CV and clock on the ATtiny1614
Closes #5749.

Q Keys now has firmware, in `apps/fm-daw/firmware/keys`:

- `keys.c` / `keys.h`: the logic with no hardware in it. MIDI bytes come in on every channel, with running status, real-time bytes mixed in, note-off sent either way, and all-notes-off. Out come the codes: DAC A is the last key held (C2 at 0, 1 mV a step for U5's gain of two), DAC B is that key's velocity, the gate is high while any key is held, and the clock is the MIDI clock divided by Div, high for the first half of each step. Start and the song position line the clock up with the beat.
- `main.c`: the ATtiny1614's pin

text:
Work on GitHub issue #5766: "init: run a workspace app's generate steps before its build (Rat Stack's apps/web)".

init: run a workspace app's generate steps before its build (Rat Stack's apps/web)
Found in the Rat Stack trial (#4803), on rat-stack `4869d23`, run from `apps/web`.

`apps/web` imports files that a sibling app generates (`apps/site/src/bundled-content.generated.ts`). So on a fresh clone the worker build that `init` infers (`pnpm exec vite build --outDir dist/web`) fails with `UNRESOLVED_IMPORT`. `workspacePrebuild` doesn't help: `@rat-stack/site` exports source, so nothing looks unbuilt.

Rat Stack does it in `predev` (`pnpm --filter @rat-stack/site generate`) and through turbo's `dependsOn` for `build`. Its cold-clone acceptance runs `pnpm sources:fetch`, `pnpm --filter @rat-stack/capability build`, then `generate`.

Options:
- `init` puts a workspace member's `prebuild` (and a `predev` that only runs `--filter <workspace dep> <script>`) in front of the inferred build;
- or, with `turbo.json` at the root, the build is `turbo run build --filter=<app>^...` and then the app's vite build.

Done when a fresh Rat Stack clone gets through `rustybuns plan --offline` with no hand steps (bar `git-snapshot`, which is Rat Stack's own staleness). Run it on the builder: this build froze the 16 GB office Mac twice.

Closes #5766.

Follow-up to #5665 (items 2 and 3, which need a real file to check against). Hot cues from DJ software tags landed with #5665; these two did not, because both depend on a file layout the public write-ups only partly give.

1. **The four-deck program's grid marker from its in-file PRIV `TRAKTOR4` frame.** `apps/fm-daw/src/dj/tags.ts` reads only the BPM (leaf HBPM). The cue list (CUEP) holds a GRID cue, but the public write-up (hellricer, 2021) gives its layout only partly (field widths, whether START is in ms). Today that grid comes from a dropped `.nml`. Decode CUEP against a real tagged file from that program, and read its hot cues from the same list.
2. **The ~26 ms MP3 decoder delay.** For an MP3, the vinyl-emulation program's beat grid and hot cue positions may be offset by the encoder delay (LAME/Xing header), against what the browser's `decodeAudioData` gives. Load a real tagged MP3, compare the grid's first beat with the audible kick (or `detectGrid`), and shift by the delay if it shows.

What's needed first: one MP3 analysed by each program (a beat grid and a hot cue or two set). Tests: extend `apps/fm-daw/test/dj-tags.test.ts`'s table with byte-built files, as the rest.

#5807 puts every live guitar and PA mic from someone else through a limiter at the listener's ceiling (src/studio/limiter.ts, set in the Esc menu), and adds an always-on brick wall in front of the speakers.

Still left:
- Slices that arrive late or at the desk (`OpusIn`/PCM through `FarSound` in src/studio/plugin-line.ts) play inside the fm-daw audio thread on a track. They hit the always-on wall and the engine's -1 dBFS peak limiter, but not the listener's per-person ceiling. To fix that, the worklet would need a per-peer ceiling (a `ToWorklet` message carrying the dB value, applied on the tracks those peers play) using the same curve as `clipCurve`.
- Room YouTube decks (src/dj/room-tube.ts) play in cross-origin iframes. Web Audio can't route them, so neither limiter can touch them. The only lever there is the player's volume API, if anyone wants it.
Qollab Studio: per-person ceiling on loop slices, on the audio thread
Closes #5808

Someone else's loop slices (Opus or PCM through `FarSound`) play on the fm-daw audio thread. Until now they skipped the listener's "Loudest anyone else can be" ceiling. Now they go through it as well:

- `ToWorklet` gets `{ t: "peerCeiling", db }`. The worklet builds `clipCurve(dbGain(db))` once, and `hearSound` shapes each incoming slice with `shaped()` before it goes on the remote line. The curve is the same one the live guitar and mic limiters use. `null` (the default) leaves the slices as they come, so FM DAW's own page doesn't change.

text:
Work on GitHub issue #5812: "Sound wall: build the transistor ladder module, played by its stage equations (owner picks the sim)".

Read it first with `gh issue view 5812 --comments`. Create a new branch, implement the change, verify it, then open a pull request that closes #5812.

You're in your own git worktree, on a fresh branch made for this task. Commit there, push it, and open the pull request from it.
Sound wall: build the transistor ladder module, played by its stage equations (owner picks the sim)
Follows #5748, which measured it first (`bun apps/fm-daw/bench/ladder.ts`, WALL.md's "The ladder, measured").

**What the measurement found.** In the circuit solver, a ladder of ten transistors (a drive pair and four stages of pairs, a capacitor across each) costs 38 to 46 µs a sample, 9 to 11 times Q Filter. In Q Filter's place in the first voice, the voice falls to 0.4 to 0.5 times real time. That doesn't fit the page's audio thread.

The same ladder as its stage equations, every number from the board's parts (tail current, C, VT, the dividers, the output gain), costs about 0.2 µs a sample. Its output is 5 to 7% from the solved ladder at 1.4 and 4.7 kHz cutoffs, and 18% at 19 kHz with Res high. The voice then runs at about 7 times real time. This is how the wall already plays its switching modules (Q Saw, Q Steps, Q Brigade).

**Decision for the owner.** Which way should the module's sim play the ladder?
1. **Stage equations from the board's parts (recommended).** Measured above. The board, panel and fab files are drawn as usual. The sim reads C, the converter's current, the dividers and the gain off the board, as `Vco` and `Bbd` do. Change C on the board and the cutoff follows.

text:
Work on GitHub issue #3978: "Qollab sold alone: a developer's own sign-in at the door, and a deploy into their own Cloudflare account".

You're in your own git worktree, on a fresh branch made for this task. Commit there, push it, and open the pull request from it.
Qollab sold alone: a developer's own sign-in at the door, and a deploy into their own Cloudflare account
The owner's direction in #3972 (2026-11-08): Qollab stays built into eqosys and is also its own product, sold to other developers (realtime rooms for any app on Cloudflare: rooms, seats, parties, presence and saves). The docs now say so. Two things the code doesn't do yet:

1. **Their own sign-in at the door.** Every Qollab door (`apps/eqosys/src/door.ts`) checks an eqosys token: `TokenChecker` against eqosys's JWKS, `aud` an app in `APPS`. Selling it alone means a developer brings their own identity, for example a JWKS URL and an audience they register, or a server-side key that mints a short Qollab ticket for their user id. The user id in the token stays the only key, so `Hub`, `Party` and `Space` shouldn't need to change. Friends then belong to that developer's users, not to eqosys accounts.
2. **Running it in their own Cloudflare account.** `apps/qollab` reads eqosys's D1 in place and binds back to eqosys for its keys (`EQOSYS`). A standalone deploy needs its own D1 (parties, saves, spaces), no eqosys binding, and the account delete path as an API the developer calls.

Until then the Qollab page and README sell it as built into eqosys. Comes after the go-live in #3898.

CUTMAN: cut LOC and casts repo-wide, one type per wire shape
Repo-wide cut: fewer lines, fewer casts, one type per wire shape. Survey of 2026-10-27, counts from grep and approximate.

## Rules the work follows

- A type is declared once, in a `types.ts` or `wire.ts` next to the code that owns it, and imported by Worker, Durable Object, page and test alike. Never a second hand-written copy at a call site.
- A parsed body, fetch reply, socket message or stored string is `unknown` until one `decode(raw: unknown)` or guard looks at it. No `as X` after `.json()`, `JSON.parse`, `deserializeAttachment()` or `localStorage.getItem`.
- Where the type already flows (D1 `first<T>()`/`all<T>()`, the `"use server"` action proxies in `packages/cli/src/glue/desktop-scaffold.ts`), use it instead of casting.
- Grep before writing a helper; copies die in the same PR.

artstewengine: admin sign-in forms likely refused in a real browser (Origin: null)
Found while building eqosys (#2764), which started from artstewengine's code. artstewengine sets `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` (`src/worker.tsx`). Chrome then sends `Origin: null` on the page's own form POSTs, and `crossSite` in `src/env.ts` treats `null` as a foreign origin and answers 403. In eqosys, Chrome got `{"error":"cross-site request refused"}` on our own sign-up form until the policy became `same-origin`. The journey test misses this because it sets `origin` itself.

Fix: use `Referrer-Policy: same-origin` (or have `crossSite` fall back to `Sec-Fetch-Site` when the origin is `null`), then sign in on the dev server in a browser.

title: Work on GitHub issue #3216: "Delayed Reaction: offline render of a 128-bar track takes five minutes; place voices in chu
text:
Work on GitHub issue #3216: "Delayed Reaction: offline render of a 128-bar track takes five minutes; place voices in chunks".

Read it first with `gh issue view 3216 --comments`. Create a new branch, implement the change, verify it, then open a pull request that closes #3216.

You're in your own git worktree, on a fresh branch made for this task. Commit there, push it, and open the pull request from it.
Delayed Reaction: offline render of a 128-bar track takes five minutes; place voices in chunks
`bun scripts/render.ts "?setup=warren"` (128 bars at 86 bpm, six minutes of audio) takes about five minutes of wall clock, and `--all` (six 128-bar and six 64-bar setups) the better part of an hour. A 56-bar slice of the same track renders in 15 seconds.

Cause: `Music.prepare` places every voice of the whole song on the offline clock at once (`schedule(Infinity)`), so Chrome processes thousands of not-yet-started oscillators, buffer sources, filters and gains on every render quantum for the full six minutes. The cost is node count times length.

Fix: schedule in chunks on the offline clock with `OfflineAudioContext.suspend(t)` / `resume()` every few bars, the same look-ahead the live clock uses, so only the next bar's voices exist at any time. The stems already render concurrently (PR #3214); this is the next step for `--all` to take minutes.

Agent Office 3D client: hire a desk run and send it home through POST, not the socket (#3423 slice 2 meets slice 3)
Part of #3423. For whoever builds slice 2 (the 3D client served from the Worker).

Slice 3 (#4069) lets a desk run a codeSplitter agent: `POST /api/office/<floor>` with `{t: "worker.spawn", repo: "owner/name", path, prompt, deskId?, name?, provider?}` seats a worker and starts the run as the hirer. Only the Worker can start or stop a run, so the floor's socket refuses two things with a warn toast:

- a `worker.spawn` that names a `repo`
- a `worker.kill` of a worker whose `run.status` is `running`

**What the client needs:** send those two as `POST /api/office/<floor>` (same body as the socket message). Everything else (queue, plain hires, kills of idle workers) can stay on the socket. Run changes still come back over the socket as `worker.update`, with `worker.run = {owner, repo, path, id, agent, status, branch?, output?}`; the desk can show `branch` and the tail of `output`.

Done when: hiring at a desk in the 3D office with a repo and file starts the run, and sending it home stops it, with no toast.

wrangler auth token | tail -1 recipes break on wrangler 4.155 (token moved to stderr), deploy gets 403
`rustybuns deploy` with `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN=$(bunx wrangler auth token 2>/dev/null | tail -1 | tr -d '[:space:]')` fails with `Cloudflare refused the API token for account … (HTTP 403)`, even though the wrangler login is fine.

Wrangler 4.155 no longer prints the token as the last line of stdout: with `2>/dev/null`, stdout is one empty line, and the token sits on stderr after the banner. So the recipe exports a wrong value. Wrangler's own token checked separately gets HTTP 200 on the account.

`rustybuns plan/deploy` don't need the export: with no `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` set, they read wrangler's login themselves through `wrangler auth token --json` (`packages/cli/src/cloudflare-auth.ts`). Workaround: `unset CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` and set only `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`.

The owner asked: a newer PR passes its tests before an older one does. Does codeSplitter handle that, and can it?

**Today, from reading the code (an agent's research, not tested on a live repo):**
- Checks run on the branch's own sha. `refChecks` (apps/codesplitter/src/checks.ts ~619-656) marks a run stale only when the branch itself changed after the run. Main moving does not make it stale.
- So once B merges, A's old green still opens the gate. Nothing tested main+B+A.
- Only a branch that clashes with the one that merged takes main in again (`afterBlocker`, branches.ts ~692) and reruns its held checks. A PR that doesn't clash but breaks semantically (B renames a function A calls, in another file) merges unseen.

- The swarm sim's "car of PRs in one test run" (swarm-sim.ts) is a simulation only.

Spike: Qollab, a party kit beside eqosys (lobby, chat, cloud saves)
Spike: decide the shape first, build later. Nothing here is built yet.

## Why

About seven apps each rebuilt lobby, room code, ready and chat: `park-hide-seek`, `hippo-tycoon`, `splat-spray`, `git-recon`, `skate-tech-park`, `two-fronts`, `fm-daw`. Most games need only keys and permissions from eqosys plus a party kit. Qollab is that kit (working name).

## The split

- **eqosys** owns identity, access (keys and permissions), and the library of apps a person owns or has. It stays auth only.
- **Qollab** owns the social pieces: parties, lobby, room codes, ready and start, chat, and a cloud-save backup (opaque, versioned blobs per user per app, size quota, keep the last N).
- **Games** own live game state and the schema of their own saves. Gameplay sync, ticks and simulation stay in each game.

Everything stays Workers and Durable Objects. Services are partitioned like shards: by user id (one DO per user) and party id (one DO per party). Each service has its own D1; no shared tables, no cross-service joins. The eqosys token is the only glue, which is also a deliberate way to dogfood the cached token.

## Questions this spike must answer

1. **Friends and presence.** They live in eqos

Q Amp: a pedalboard, slots in any order, effects loop, stereo, load per slot
Lane 2 of the analog map (`apps/fm-daw/ANALOG.md`, section 2). Q Amp has one pedal slot. Make it a board:

- Slots in any order, drag to reorder, a footswitch each.
- An effects loop on the amp: time effects after the preamp, before the power stage.
- Mono until the first stereo effect, stereo after.
- A load share on each slot, so a player sees what costs what.

Budget (CIRCUITS.md "Speed"): pedal 5 to 6x real time, 4-tube amp 2.3 to 3.3x, so a full board won't fit at 4x oversampling on one thread. In order:

2. Split the chain over worker threads with a `SharedArrayBuffer` ring, one block of latency per hop, only when one thread is over budget.

`qamp.state()` reports the chain and each slot's load. Test: one journey through `src/amp/live.ts` that reorders two pedals while the riff plays, output bounded, no Newton misses.

Pixel RAG: ask in words (Clef ranks tiles, Clairic pulls the answer)
Pixel RAG (`apps/pixel-rag`) finds tiles by picture: click a tile, get the tiles that look like it. Next comes asking in words, the RAG half, on Workers AI so it all stays on one Cloudflare bill.

## Flow

```
question -> embedding -> hamming_topk (the index we have) -> top tiles
  -> Clef (@cf/cloudflare/clef): "does this tile answer it?" as a probability per tile, "none" allowed (the step Jev does in PixelRAG + Jev)
  -> Clairic (@cf/cloudflare/clairic): the typed answer pulled out of the winning tile
```

## Open before building

- **Embedder.** Text questions need a model that puts text and images in one space. No such model is confirmed on Workers AI; the changelog lists text-only embedders (`qwen3-embedding-0.6b`, `embeddinggemma-300m`). Options: run one on the box, or caption each tile once at index time and embed the caption.
- **Clairic and images.** Does it take an image, or only text? Clef does take images (excalibrawl, `apps/excalibrawl/src/engine/brain.ts`).
- **Price per question** at k = 10 tiles, worked out before any deploy, behind a budget guard like excalibrawl's.

## Later: the cloud index

The same crate as wasm in one Durable Object per corpus, codes in its SQ

Agent Office: storage cap per worker sandbox, pause and alert when it is hit
On 2026-10-29 the Mac's disk hit 100% (192 MB free) while workers were running. Builds and file writes failed (`ENOSPC`), and the cause took a long hunt to find.

What was found: about 117 GB of per-worktree `node_modules` (2-3 GB each, ~49 worktrees), about 7 GB of per-session scratch folders in `/private/tmp/claude-501` (up to 2.3 GB for one worker), and Docker's `Docker.raw` at ~175 GB on top of the Bun cache (39 GB). Clearing worktree `node_modules` freed only a few GB.

## Wanted
- A **per-worker cap** on its sandbox: its worktree (node_modules included) plus its scratch folder. At the cap the office **pauses** that worker (does not send it home) and **alerts the owner** with the biggest directories.
- A **volume floor** (free space on the volume, e.g. 15 GB). Below it every worker pauses and the owner is alerted, since no one worker can fix it.
- Resume once the owner clears space or raises the cap.

## Notes
- Numbers above are starting points, e.g. cap about 4 GB over a fresh checkout; make them settings.
- A scan must be cheap: `du` over ~70 worktrees took minutes. Skip `.git`, and size `node_modules` less often.
- Docker's disk image is outside any worker's control; the v

CI: every app's tests in three time-balanced lanes by default (one knob to scale to many boxes)
Owner, 2026-11-19: every app's CI tests run in three lanes by default, bucketed by time, as one horizontally scalable primitive. Later the same split can spread testing over many boxes.

## Why

A Mythic Masters PR waits 9-10 minutes for `test mythic-masters`, whatever it changes. Three headless-Chrome journeys run one after another and take about 7.8 of the 9.3 minutes (run 44419316548):

| test | time |
|---|---|
| two friends walk one world | 229 s |
| a first fight teaches move, jump, attack, guard and a special | 140 s |
| a new game from the title to the world | 98 s |
| the other 538 tests | ~90 s |

## What's there already

`scripts/ci-apps.ts` has `shards?: number`. `shardedTests()` spreads an app's test files over N jobs with Ester's `shard()` (`apps/codesplitter/scripts/ester.ts`), weighted by `apps/<name>/test-times.json` (`scripts/test-times.ts`). Only codesplitter (3), skate-tech-park (3) and two-fronts (4) set it. Everything else runs as one job.

1. **Three lanes is the default.** Every app with a `test` gets 3 shards unless its row says otherwise (two-fronts keeps 4). An app with too few files for three lanes gets fewer, not empty jobs; `shardedTests

Part of #1052. Follows #2698.

Wildclash becomes **Mythic Masters**. The roster moves off the renamed creatures from the stats API and onto creatures from world folklore and mythology. Those are public domain, so they're ours to use, name and draw.

## Goal

Each creature is a beast from a real legend: the Jersey Devil, the Mothman, the Hodag, the kelpie, the tengu, the gumiho, the Mapinguari. Release rings: a straight-through score picks each PR's lane (standby, fast, express)
Part of #4486 (release rings). The picture is in notes/release-rings.html, sections 3 and 4.

Agents open hundreds of PRs a week, so not every PR should wait the full soak (3 green hours, 3 green nights, Monday). Each PR gets a score from facts we already measure, and the score picks its lane. The checks stay the same in every lane; only the waiting changes.

**Score (0 to 100)**
- What it touches: one app +30, a few apps +15, `packages/` or the lockfile 0, CI, deploy or secrets wiring -25
- Its tests fail on the old code (`bun scripts/test-bites.ts`): +25
- Changed lines its tests run (`test-bites --lines`): most +15, some +5
- Size: under 100 lines +15, 100 to 500 +5, over 500 -10
- Its app's last 30 days on the rings: rarely red +15, often red -10

**Lanes**
- Fast lane (score 60 or more, and no CI/deploy/secrets wiring): 1 green hour and 1 green night, then the owner's OK. A red sweep drops it into standby at that ring.
- Standby: the normal soak.
- Express (owner only, already built in #4756): a security advisory on something we ship, a hijacked package or Action in our build chain, or a host incident. Every sweep runs now. A red keeps it in express and the next fix forward go

You're in your own git worktree, on a fresh branch made for this task. Commit there, push it, and open the pull request from it.
Reading code by sed -n ranges is the biggest agent chore: an outline tool or codeSplitter code mode
Dexter's chore count over 14 days of sessions (620 sessions, PR #3165): reading code by `sed -n` / `cat` / `grep` was 5,316 calls and 5.3M result tokens, with 1,084 streaks of the same chore back to back (an agent paging through a file range by range). It is the biggest chore by far and PR #3165 only added a tip for it.

What would cut it:

- A local outline tool: `bun run outline <file>` (or a codeSplitter MCP tool) that prints each exported symbol, function, class and top-level const with its line range and the first line of its doc comment, so an agent jumps to one `sed -n` range instead of walking the file. TypeScript's own parser, or a regex over the top-level declarations, is enough for this repo's style.
- Through codeSplitter, one `execute` program (`read_file` plus a filter) that returns only the matching lines; Dexter's mode lines show 3,032 direct MCP calls against 2 code-mode programs in those two weeks.

Numbers come from `DEXTER_HOURS=336 bun apps/agent-office/ester/dexter.ts` (the "Chores done by hand" lines).

Wildclash becomes **Mythic Masters**. The roster moves off the renamed creatures from the stats API and onto creatures from world folklore and mythology. Those are public domain, so they're ours to use, name and draw.

## Goal

Each creature is a beast from a real legend: the Jersey Devil, the Mothman, the Hodag, the kelpie, the tengu, the gumiho, the Mapinguari. It has its folklore name, a body sheet (mass, height, six stats) and six moves that come out of its legend. The region list for the whole game is in the Mythic Masters regions issue (#2708).

Games say less: move explanations behind ? popovers in the rest of the games
The owner's ask (2026-11-11): simplify every game's UI a lot. Fewer explanations and much less text. A screen keeps its name, its buttons and its pictures, in plain words if it needs any. How a mode or a mechanic works goes behind a popup.

Done so far: Mythic Masters and Git Recon (#4234). The pattern from that PR:
- A small `?` button (lucide `circle-help`) with `popovertarget`, next to the screen's heading, opens a native `<div class="about" popover>` holding the moved words. A click outside it or Escape closes it. No new JS.
- Story and blurb lines become a tooltip (`title`) on the card they describe. Key lists move into the popover. Labels become one or two words ("More", "Versus", "New game").
- A gun or item list is icon + number, and only the selected one shows its name (see Git Recon's HUD).
- Lore and copy words are moved, not rewritten. Shorten only button labels and how-to lines.

Introducing 𝚡𝚎𝚎𝚝: http://xeet-rs.vercel.app.

A hermetic, pixel-perfect X post renderer in safe Rust / wasm. Zero browser, network, filesystem, system fonts. Renders a post to PNG in ~1ms (and 0.4 ms for 
@jack
's "setting up my twttr" 😁).

X is the global town square, and the medium is the message. Being able to preview what things will look like before posting is great for both humans and agents.

Rendering with xeet is is 100x-1000x faster than booting up a browser and taking a screenshot, yet it's just as accurate.

It reproduces Blink & HarfBuzz text shaping, 1/64px line breaking, RTL bidi, 28 Chirp font subsets, CJK/Math/Emoji fallbacks, "Show more" rules, etc. It's the kind of thing that would be wildly impractical, if not impossible, for a human engineer to pull off.

Except 𝚡𝚎𝚎𝚝 is structured as an "autorepo." An oracle boots up Chrome, and verifies tens of thousands of text layout rules. A CI canary then watches the evolution of the original, and files signed PRs for agents to act on. It was conceived from the ground up around 'verification engineering', and the result speaks for itself.

Enjoy!

Look again: a libretro-style save/load contract for game sims (save states, rewind, rollback netplay)
A note to look at this again later. It came out of a chat about what libretro has that RustyBuns games don't. Nothing is built yet.

## What libretro is

Libretro is one small C header (`libretro.h`, MIT) that splits a game into two halves:

- A **core** (the game or emulator) does three things: step one frame from the inputs, hand back video and audio, and save its whole state to bytes and load it back.
- A **frontend** (RetroArch) does the rest: the window, audio, controllers, shaders, saves and netplay.

Because every core keeps the same contract, every frontend feature works with every core for free.

3. **Rollback netplay.** Machines predict the other player's input and roll back when the guess was wrong. Qollab rooms are server-authoritative instead, which is worse for frame-tight duels in Mythic Masters.
4. **A shared shader layer** over any game's output.

Spike: Goose for small hot kernels (port hippo_fluid, load via bun:ffi)
**Question:** is [Goose](https://github.com/aardappel/goose) (a new memory-safe systems language: no GC, no heap allocator, no lifetime annotations; compiles to one C file; Apache 2.0) worth a place next to Rust for small hot kernels in RustyBuns?

**Timebox:** one worker, about half a day. Out of CI, nothing shipped to an app.

## Why it might fit

- Goose emits a single C file. Bun can compile and load C at runtime with `cc()` from `bun:ffi` (TinyCC, the same backend Goose bundles). So a Goose kernel could load straight into a Bun script: no cargo, no `build:native`, no Bob.
- Agents may write it more easily than Rust (no lifetimes).

## Target: `hippo_fluid`

`apps/hippo-tycoon/native/crates/hippo_fluid/src/lib.rs` (177 lines) is the oil geyser's particle sim. It already has a C ABI (`fl_init`, `fl_step`, `fl_count`, `fl_out`), uses only f64 `+ - * / sqrt`, and has a TypeScript twin (`src/client/render/fluid.ts`) that agrees bit for bit. That twin is the oracle.

1. Install Goose locally (scratch dir, not the repo). Note how it installs and its version.
2. Port `hippo_fluid` to Goose with the same four exports.
